title: Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modelling for high-frequency dynamics of high-speed rail pantographs
abstract: Stable sliding contact between the pantograph and catenary is essential for reliable current collection in high-speed rail. As operating speeds increase beyond 350 km/h, the pantograph-catenary system exhibits unprecedented high-frequency dynamic behaviors caused by the excitation of flexible structural modes. Traditional lumped mass pantograph models are unable to represent the structural flexibility, while fully flexible finite element models, though accurate, are computationally constrained for large-scale simulations. To fill this gap, a Koopman Neural Operator-based surrogate modeling framework is proposed to integrate dynamic theory into a data-driven learning scheme, enabling efficient and accurate representation of the high-frequency pantograph dynamics. The surrogate model integrates a deep autoencoder for the observable and inverse-observable functions with a modified Transformer as the evolution operator. Training data are generated from an accurate fully flexible pantograph model, which has been validated via experimental tests, under broadband random excitations. The training process is supervised by a combined loss of multi-step prediction and physical consistency. Inference tests demonstrate that the surrogate model maintains finite element-level accuracy while reducing computational time by three orders of magnitude when predicting 1000-step dynamic responses. Comparative analyses confirm its superior balance between physical interpretability and forecasting performance, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for real-time simulation, efficient optimization, and comprehensive evaluation of the high-frequency behaviors of a high-speed pantograph-catenary system.

title: DRN-PISSM: a pitch bearing fault diagnosis network integrating dilated residual convolution and a Physics-Informed State-Space model
abstract: Pitch bearings in wind turbine equipment operate for long periods under extremely low rotational speeds and time-varying loads. Under such conditions, fault-induced impulses are weak and span long periods, while diagnostic information is easily masked by background noise. As a result, conventional signal-processing methods and purely data-driven models often show insufficient stability under strong noise and cross-load conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Dilated Residual Network with a Physics-Informed State-Space Model, termed DRN-PISSM. The proposed method first uses a one-dimensional dilated residual convolutional network to extract multiscale temporal features, thereby enhancing the perception of weak fault information in low-speed heavy-load bearings. A physics-informed state-space recurrent branch is then designed to explicitly strengthen the modelling of periodic information associated with fault characteristic frequencies, improving both physical interpretability and feature discriminability. Finally, adaptive gated fusion, together with joint constraints of physical consistency and noise invariance, is used to improve robustness and generalization under strong noise and load variations. Experimental results show that the proposed method maintains high diagnostic accuracy under different noise intensities and outperforms several comparison models in cross-load transfer tasks with noise disturbance, demonstrating good robustness and generalization capability.

title: End-to-end prediction and inverse identification of gear grinding and EOL performance based on physics-informed neural networks
abstract: Existing open-loop quality control paradigms and traditional dynamic models are inadequate for actively suppressing high-frequency whine and ghost noise in electric vehicle (EV) gears, primarily due to unmodeled boundary uncertainties and time-varying transfer functions. Furthermore, purely data-driven methods are inherently constrained by causal feature leakage and insufficient out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization capabilities. To overcome these fundamental bottlenecks, this paper proposes an end-to-end differentiable gray-box framework based on physics-informed integration, which rigorously decouples the forward physical deduction process from the inverse parameter identification process. During the forward prediction phase, the compensation network (NNgrind) exclusively processes remote machine tool vibrations to reconstruct the microscopic three-dimensional (3D) surface waviness. Facilitated by a differentiable smooth relaxation operator, the inverted waviness formulation subsequently drives a 16-degree-of-freedom (16-DOF) gearbox ordinary differential equation (ODE) model. Concurrently, the state-dependent neural operator (NNdyn) strictly extracts transient physical states (i.e., displacement and velocity) to autonomously compensate for nonlinear dynamic residuals, thereby mathematically mitigating the computational overhead and convergence instabilities associated with implicit algebraic loops.During the inverse identification phase, empirical end-of-line (EOL) vibration data serves uniquely as the ground-truth supervision label. Driven by automatic differentiation, the spectrum error gradient backpropagates directly through the ODE solver, achieving the closed-loop calibration of the dual operators with zero causal feature leakage. Blind bench test validations demonstrate that the predicted vibration root mean square error (RMSE) is reduced to 0.052 g. Crucially, this framework strictly complies with cross-axis kinematic conversion laws, precisely resolving the mapping of non-integer ghost frequencies (e.g., accurately tracing a 3.1st-order machine tool excitation to a 26.87th-order macroscopic response on the input shaft). Finally, process sensitivity analysis confirms that actively reshaping the waviness topology can sever its geometric coupling with the line of action, thereby suppressing the ghost noise amplitude by up to 79% directly at the manufacturing source.

title: An unsupervised deep learning method for extracting weak reflections from strong guided waves in array data
abstract: The separation of overlapping wavefields in array sensor measurements is a fundamental challenge in acoustic and vibration diagnostics, with critical applications from structural health monitoring to subsurface imaging. A particularly challenging scenario occurs when extremely weak target signals (e.g., geological reflections from fractures) are completely masked by strong guided-wave interference in borehole acoustic reflection imaging. Traditional methods inadequately suppress guided waves, resulting in residual interference that obscures the weak reflections. Furthermore, supervised deep learning methods face practical constraints due to the limited availability of labeled data in field applications. To address these limitations, we propose a novel unsupervised approach that integrates the time-frequency network (TF-GridNet) with a Multi-Frame Wiener Filter (MFWF). Our approach exploits the distinct kinematic properties of guided waves and reflections in array data to achieve separation without requiring labeled training sets. Comprehensive validation on both simulated and field data from complex geological lithologies demonstrates our method’s superiority. On simulated data, it achieves a lower separation residual (L2-norm) than conventional F-K and Multichannel Singular-Spectrum Analysis (MSSA) methods. Crucially, on field data, it enables the reliable extraction of weak reflections, producing significantly clearer images of high-dip-angle fractures and fracture networks with enhanced continuity and reduced artifacts. This work presents a robust, label-free solution for extracting weak signals from strong interference in waveguide structures, as demonstrated in borehole acoustics. The method shows strong potential for advancing structural health monitoring applications that rely on guided-wave sensing.

title: Physics-informed dual digital twin for online friction updating and decoupled wear identification in robots
abstract: Joint friction is influenced by reversible variations in temperature and load and by irreversible degradation caused by wear. This leads to challenges in friction identification, including operating condition coupling, strong nonlinearity, and poor long-term stability. We present a Physics-Informed Dual Digital Twin (PIDT) framework to overcome these issues. This framework comprises a baseline digital twin trained offline and an evolving digital twin updated online. They enable accurate friction modeling, robust online updating, and decoupled wear monitoring under varying operating conditions. The baseline digital twin uses a ResNet based hybrid deep kernel to learn nonlinear features of temperature and load coupling, and then constructs the kernel function. A multi output sparse variational Gaussian process (SVGP) provides a probabilistic friction model and quantifies predictive uncertainty. The evolving digital twin performs mini batch incremental learning while keeping part of the structural parameters fixed and enforcing physics constraints. Taking the difference between the evolving digital twin and the baseline digital twin suppresses reversible fluctuations and extracts wear related drift. Experiments on the JAKA MiniCobo show that the baseline digital twin reduces RMSE by at least 16.1% compared with conventional methods. The online updating process further improves accuracy and refines uncertainty estimates. The estimated wear related health indicator (HI) correlates with the simulated HI with r = 0.996. The framework remains stable during long duration experiments on the real robot.

title: System-dynamics-oriented design of electromagnetic active suspension via physics-informed modeling
abstract: Electromagnetic active suspension (EAS) performance is fundamentally governed by actuator dynamics, where the thrust saturation and ripple of permanent magnet linear synchronous motors (PMLSMs) directly affect the ride comfort under random road excitations. In conventional FEA-driven actuator design, the pathway linking electromagnetic design variables to system-level vibration responses is not explicitly revealed, which renders performance-oriented optimization computationally prohibitive. This study proposes a physics-informed modeling and optimization framework that establishes an explicit knowledge pathway from suspension dynamics to electromagnetic actuator design. An analytical Optimal Equivalent Radius-Maxwell Stress Tensor (OMST) formulation is developed to characterize the electromagnetic thrust, and embedded together with Maxwell equations into a physics-informed neural operator (PIMNO) built upon an enhanced Fourier Neural Operator. This enables accurate magnetic field and thrust prediction with substantially reduced data requirements. A MORIME scheme is further introduced to synergize with the PIMNO-OMST model for efficient design exploration. More importantly, device performance requirements are derived directly from system-level vibration simulations using a dual-condition robust weighting strategy, allowing actuator optimization to be guided by vibration and signal-domain indices rather than purely electromagnetic criteria. Experimental results demonstrate that the designed actuator yields suspension vibration responses, power spectral density characteristics, and ride comfort performance nearly identical to those obtained using FEA-driven optimization, while reducing computational cost by over 99%. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient and physically consistent method for system-dynamics-oriented force performance design in EAS, bridging electromagnetic field-to-force modeling and mechanical system vibration analysis.

title: High-fidelity wear simulation of gas foil bearing-rotor systems in hydrogen fuel cell air compressors using a physics-guided neural network
abstract: A Gas Foil Bearing (GFB)-rotor system is critical to a hydrogen fuel cell air compressor, yet highly susceptible to wear under frequent start-stop operations. Existing simulation models rarely consider wear and lack simulation accuracy, inadequately assessing lubrication performance and frictional power loss of GFB-rotor systems. To address this issue, this study proposes a high-fidelity dynamic model for a GFB-rotor system based on a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN), coupling a physics-based GFB-rotor dynamic model with a neural network used for model error compensation. The GFB-rotor dynamic model incorporates wear-induced gas film thickness variation, Reynolds equation, foil structural dynamics, and rigid rotor motion equations. To compensate for deviations from theoretical simplifications, the neural network embeds a learnable model discrepancy term into the GFB-rotor dynamic model. The model parameters and neural network weights are then iteratively optimized via experimental calibration. The simulated results of the proposed high-fidelity model match well with experimental data, with relative errors below 5.73% across all operating conditions. Parametric analyses demonstrate that wear significantly deteriorates gas film lubrication performance. Increased wear depth and worn region reduce minimum gas film thickness, raise maximum gas film pressure, and shift the pressure field from single-peak to dual-peak concentration. Wear amplifies viscous shear dissipation via reduced gas film thickness and elevated gas film pressure, increasing frictional power loss of the GFB-rotor system by up to 44.5% under 20,000 rpm. The proposed high-fidelity model enables accurate condition monitoring of GFB-rotor systems, ensuring stable performance and optimal efficiency of hydrogen fuel cell air compressors.

title: Physics-informed online intelligent discharge state identification for high-energy electrical discharge milling: Theory and methods
abstract: High-energy electrical discharge milling (HEDM) offers considerable potential for high-efficiency machining of difficult-to-machine materials in aerospace and other advanced manufacturing sectors. However, compared with conventional electrical discharge machining (EDM), HEDM is characterized by substantially higher single-pulse energy, greater fluctuations in discharge behavior, and lower process stability. To address the limitations of purely data-driven models in terms of physical interpretability and cross-condition generalization, this paper proposes a physics-informed semi-supervised learning framework for online HEDM discharge state identification. First, a time-threshold-based semi-automatic labeling method is developed to generate discharge state labels and identify key pulse-level physical information. Second, an empirical model for estimating the equivalent plasma channel radius is established based on high-energy single-pulse discharge experiments. The estimated radius is then combined with the actual single-pulse input energy and equivalent short-circuit conduction to construct a multi-level physical supervision framework. These three quantities characterize the spatial scale of thermal effects, heat input intensity, and short-circuit-related conduction behavior, respectively. By jointly optimizing the pulse-level classification loss and the window-level physical consistency loss, the proposed framework enables the model to learn discriminative features while constraining its predictions using discharge-related physical quantities. Comparative and ablation experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an identification accuracy of 99.17 ± 0.75% under the new operating conditions and improves both cross-condition generalization and physical consistency. Real-time validation further confirms its capability for online HEDM monitoring, thereby providing a theoretical and technical basis for future intelligent control of HEDM processes.

title: Physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold networks for sound field estimation
abstract: The sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed neural network (PINN) integrates physical prior information, which not only significantly reduces dependence on the size of the training set but also improves the accuracy of sound field estimation. However, PINN usually employs multilayer perceptrons with fixed activation functions, resulting in limited model interpretability and flexibility, which constrains its performance in complex acoustic environments. Therefore, this study proposes a sound field estimation method based on a physics-informed Kolmogorov-Arnold network (PIKAN). PIKAN constructs its edge activation functions as a linear combination of radial basis functions (RBFs) and adaptively learns the RBF coefficients during training, thereby substantially enhancing the interpretability and expressive capability. The proposed method is evaluated on sound field interpolation and extrapolation tasks across small and large meeting rooms at multiple frequencies, and benchmarked against plane wave expansion (PWE) and PINN. Analysis of the learned edge activation functions reveals that they spontaneously exhibit sinusoidal-like oscillatory characteristics. For interpolation, PIKAN demonstrates clear advantages over PINN and PWE under sparse training conditions at mid-to-high frequencies. For extrapolation, PWE retains a competitive advantage. Furthermore, to improve the performance under high reverberation, a transfer learning strategy is introduced, fine-tuning parameters pre-trained under moderate reverberation. Overall, this study demonstrates PIKAN as a promising alternative for sound field estimation, with results highlighting its potential for practical acoustic modeling.

title: Multi-task mixture-of-experts vision transformer for cross-bridge anomaly detection
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems deployed on large-scale bridges accumulate massive amounts of anomalous data, which undermines the reliability of structural condition assessment and damage identification. As monitoring targets gradually expand from individual bridges to bridge groups, the costs associated with model training and management continue to increase, placing higher demands on unified model deployment and centralized system management. Meanwhile, although anomalous patterns from different bridges contain potentially shareable information, such commonality cannot be fully exploited through simple data aggregation. This study proposes a multi-task mixture-of-experts Vision Transformer (MT-MoE ViT) framework for data anomaly diagnosis, which imposes parallel constraints during the joint optimization of multi-bridge tasks to reduce reliance on structure-specific or local condition features and instead learn anomalous features that remain discriminative across multiple bridge scenarios. To further characterize task-level differences among bridges, task embeddings are incorporated into the gating network to guide adaptive expert selection and balance shared representation learning with task-specific modeling. To mitigate routing collapse and optimization conflicts in multi-task learning, sparse routing strategies achieve feature-level expert selection, while adaptive multi-task optimization mechanisms dynamically adjust gradient weights and expert load balancing. Experimental validation conducted on real structural health monitoring data from nine long-span bridges of different structural types demonstrates that the proposed method enables stable cross-bridge anomaly representation and collaborative diagnosis within a unified model framework.

title: Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: a comprehensive review and emerging trends
abstract: Bayesian learning has emerged as a compelling and vital research direction in the field of structural dynamics, offering a probabilistic lens to understand and refine the analysis of complex dynamical systems. This review meticulously traces the three-decade evolution of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics, illuminating core principles, groundbreaking methodologies, and diverse applications that have significantly influenced the field. The narrative commences by delving into the basics of Bayesian theory, clarifying essential concepts, and introducing primary methods for deriving posterior distributions, with an in-depth exploration of three types: Laplace approximation, stochastic sampling, and variational inference. Subsequently, the text explores the implementation of two types of Bayesian learning in structural dynamics: physical model learning and data-centric statistical model learning. Physical model learning emphasizes inferring physical model parameters within a Bayesian framework for system identification and prediction, while statistical model learning integrates Bayesian learning methodologies into data-centric statistical modeling within probabilistic machine learning. Both types resonate across various applications, such as modal analysis, model updating, damage detection, and reliability updating, highlighting their pivotal role in enhancing comprehension of dynamical systems and decision-making. The paper also navigates obstacles by proposing ways to enhance existing Bayesian inference strategies. Distinguished from previous research, this study offers a thorough examination of both traditional and cutting-edge Bayesian methods. It not only underscores the transformative influence of Bayesian approaches but also serves as a beacon, guiding researchers in the judicious selection and refinement of suitable methods for various challenges in structural dynamics.

title: A novel method for bearing fault diagnosis based on deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning
abstract: Bearing health monitoring is crucial in rail transit vehicles, and deep compressive sensing has gained attention for its low redundancy, minimal storage, and fast signal reconstruction. However, conventional networks often adopt single-branch convolutional structures, limiting feature stability and temporal modeling, especially under complex conditions and strong noise. Moreover, typical transfer learning approaches rely on a single loss function during fine-tuning, which, under small sample scenarios, can cause intra-class feature dispersion, blurred inter-class boundaries, and reduced discriminative ability. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a cross-domain bearing fault diagnosis method combining deep compressive sensing and contrastive transfer learning. In the compressive sensing stage, a multi-branch attention-based reconstruction network is designed to capture key signal features under complex conditions, enhancing feature richness and providing a conditional analytical explanation for the possible domain-discrepancy suppression mechanism between source and target data. In the transfer learning stage, a staged loss optimization strategy is employed: pre-training uses contrastive loss to obtain discriminative embeddings, while fine-tuning combines Triplet Loss and Cross Entropy to balance embedding structure and classification power. Experiments on Case Western Reserve University bearing open datasets and BJTU-RAO Bogie Datasets demonstrate the method’s effectiveness, achieving a signal MSE of 0.00321 and fault diagnosis accuracy of 98.51 %, highlighting its superior cross-domain diagnostic performance under small sample conditions.

title: A physics-informed framework for online cable force identification and Bayesian corrosion-fatigue life updating of stay cables
abstract: To address the need for cable force identification and fatigue life assessment of in-service stay cables under long-term structural health monitoring, this study proposes a monitoring-informed framework that integrates time-varying frequency extraction, rapid cable force identification, corrosion-fatigue damage evaluation, and Bayesian life updating. First, based on multi-year monitoring data from the Qingzhou Channel Bridge of the Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macao Bridge, the amplitude and phase estimation of a sinusoid method is employed to extract time-varying frequencies from cable acceleration responses. A dynamic-stiffness-guided micro physics-informed neural network (µDS-PINN) is then developed for rapid and accurate identification of time-varying cable forces. Second, based on time-varying stress data and combined with wind speed and temperature, a corrosion-fatigue coupled damage model is established. Finally, a Bayesian life updating model is developed to update the intercept parameter of the S–N curve posteriorly, thereby quantifying the remaining life distribution and failure probability. The results show that µDS-PINN significantly improves cable force identification efficiency while maintaining high accuracy, meeting the demand for rapid identification in long-term online monitoring scenarios. The proposed life prediction method enables probabilistic characterization of remaining life and failure risk. Long-term monitoring results show distinct cable-to-cable differences in daily fatigue damage, and the remaining life obtained through online updating is significantly negatively correlated with daily fatigue damage, demonstrating that the proposed method can continuously revise life prediction results as damage accumulates. This study provides a practical basis for fatigue state tracking, life management, and risk warning of in-service stay cables.

title: Integrated physics-informed and unsupervised learning assessment of hemp-reinforced masonry barrel vaults under shaking table testing
abstract: The seismic assessment of strengthened masonry vaults through full-scale shaking-table testing remains limited, particularly for sustainable, heritage-compatible systems. This study investigates the dynamic response and damage evolution of full-scale masonry barrel vaults strengthened with a hemp-mesh biocomposite embedded in a cocciopesto matrix. A two-phase experimental campaign was carried out on two geometrically identical vaults subjected to progressively scaled three-component earthquake records, enabling the analysis of three representative structural configurations: unreinforced, newly reinforced, and damaged-then-reinforced. Reinforcement effectiveness and damage progression were assessed through a multi-indicator framework combining modal parameters with two proposed indicators: an energy-based indicator derived from Arias intensity and an autoencoder-based indicator. Each is formulated in a baseline-relative (excitation-dependent) form and in an input-normalized form where the energy-based indicator is normalized by the Arias intensity of the input and the autoencoder-based indicator by the squared RMS of the input. It follows that the input-normalized indicators isolate structural regime transitions from the excitation amplitude growth. Results show that the reinforcement, in both newly reinforced and damaged-then-reinforced configurations, enhances seismic capacity and damage tolerance, with delayed damage onset and reduced stiffness degradation. The proposed indicators consistently captured structural regime transitions and damage evolution across all configurations, showing strong agreement with modal trends. In particular, energy-based indicators provide a straightforward signal-level description of regime changes, while the feature-based autoencoder approach proves effective in detecting subtle statistical deviations that may precede visible damage, confirming its effectiveness in tracking stiffness degradation and nonlinear structural response.

title: LCA-PINN: A lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network for interpretable tool wear monitoring
abstract: Tool wear monitoring (TWM) is essential to ensuring product quality and sustaining the efficiency of intelligent manufacturing. However, the variability of cutting parameters across different configurations results in significant condition differences, making it difficult to generalize hybrid models built on physical formulas or empirical knowledge for specific conditions to unseen parameter combinations. To address this limitation, a lightweight condition-aware physics-informed neural network (LCA-PINN) is proposed for interpretable TWM under unseen cutting conditions. Specifically, key physical coefficients are dynamically learned by minimizing the residual between the tool wear physics equation and the observed wear. On this basis, a conditional mapping between cutting parameters and physical coefficients is established, enabling adaptive and physically consistent learning across parameter combinations. In addition, a joint data-driven and physics-driven output strategy is employed to estimate tool wear, ensuring accurate monitoring while maintaining physical consistency. Experiments on a full-lifecycle dataset covering a wide range of cutting parameter settings show that, compared with the best-performing baseline, LCA-PINN achieves relative reductions in RMSE, MAE, and MAPE of 36.30%, 34.38%, and 34.57%, respectively, along with an improvement of 2.07% in R2. Moreover, LCA-PINN exhibits favorable complexity, requiring only 5.86 kFLOPs and 23.69 KB memory, meeting the requirements for lightweight deployment in industrial applications. This study offers a feasible pathway to deploying reliable and physically consistent intelligent monitoring in advanced manufacturing environments.

title: Physics-informed unit-normalized selective embedding with harmonic loss for fault identification using vibration and acoustic signals
abstract: Induction motors generate vibration and acoustic signals from mechanical imbalance, electromagnetic forces, and structural transmission through the machine housing. Interpreting harmonic fault signatures from these responses becomes difficult when different types of sensors are used due to bandwidth and signal scaling limitations. This work investigates how physics-informed signal representation can improve fault diagnosis using both industrial sensors and cell phone sensors. A unit-consistent normalization approach is introduced to allow comparison between vibration acceleration and acoustic pressure signals by converting both signals into equivalent vibration velocity representations. Based on this formulation, a structured signal processing framework named Unit-Normalized Selective Embedding with Harmonic Loss (UNSE-HL) is proposed, combining unit normalization, selective embedding, and a physics-informed harmonic loss function to improve the representation of modulation patterns during diagnosis. Experiments are conducted using the induction motor datasets collected under multiple operating conditions with both structurally mounted sensors and cell phones. Envelope spectral analysis shows that rotor harmonics are observable across cell phone sensors after normalization; this observability does not by itself establish classification reliability, which is evaluated separately. Time-frequency representations combined with the proposed embedding strategy improve diagnosis accuracy and classification stability relative to conventional signal representation approaches on the datasets and devices evaluated in this study. These findings highlight the importance of signal transmission physics in condition monitoring and indicate that, for the specific smartphone sensors and operating conditions tested here, appropriate preprocessing improves the usability of low-bandwidth sensors for fault diagnosis.

title: Causal Bayesian optimization for sensor placement and deconfounding in structural health monitoring
abstract: Structural health monitoring systems must distinguish genuine damage from environmental effects. Current methods rely on correlational reasoning that cannot separate causal influences from spurious associations. Temperature variations, for instance, often produce larger shifts in natural frequencies than actual structural damage does. Here, we introduce a causal inference framework that addresses this limitation at its root. A structural causal model encodes the physical relationships among environmental conditions, structural properties, damage states, and sensor measurements. Formal causal reasoning then separates the genuine effect of damage on sensor responses from the confounding influence of environmental conditions. Counterfactual analysis further allows engineers to evaluate hypothetical scenarios, such as alternative sensor layouts or different environmental conditions, without physical experimentation. Built on this causal foundation, a multi-objective Bayesian optimization algorithm identifies Pareto-optimal sensor placements that balance detection probability, localization accuracy, false alarm robustness, and instrumentation cost. Validation spans numerical and experimental benchmarks together with an end-to-end evaluation on a full-scale bridge. Causal deconfounding lowers false alarm rates compared to conventional normalization, the optimizer reaches better Pareto fronts with far fewer evaluations than evolutionary alternatives, and the advantages persist under model misspecification and hidden confounding.

title: Early anomaly detection in wind Turbines by Causality-based graph attention networks
abstract: Early anomaly detection is a key issue for ensuring reliability, availability and efficiency in Wind Turbines (WTs) operation. Traditional condition monitoring techniques struggle to identify anomalies because of: i) the strong interconnections among the subsystems of a WT, which induce complex spatio-temporal dependencies in the measured signals and can enable the cascading propagation of the effects of anomalies, ii) the variability of the operating conditions, which can affect the anomaly signatures, and iii) the presence of control systems that can mask the anomalies signatures. To address these challenges, this work proposes a novel anomaly detection method employing a Graph Neural Network (GNN) autoencoder. GNN is selected for its capability in modeling the interconnected nature of subsystems and capturing the spatio-temporal dependencies in operational signals. A key contribution is the use of the Granger causality test to generate the GNN functional graph. By leveraging the causal relationships among turbine signals, the obtained graph ensures that the learned topology reflects the underlying physical dependencies rather than spurious correlations, as it may occur in traditional graphs. To handle variability of the operating conditions, graph attention layers adaptively weight sensor relationships, while gated recurrent units process the temporal dynamics. The proposed method is validated on synthetic data simulated using a high-fidelity WT model and applied to SCADA data collected from real WTs. Results demonstrate a 4% increase in recall and a 45% reduction in detection delay compared to state-of-the-art methods.

title: An integrated autoencoder-based framework for unsupervised domain adaptation in structural health monitoring of bridges
abstract: The limited availability of long-term bridge-monitoring data presents a significant obstacle to the application of machine learning in structural health monitoring (SHM). Domain adaptation offers a means of addressing this data scarcity, but existing methods often have limited generalization and are sensitive to hyperparameter choices. This study proposes a reconstruction-based domain adaptation framework in which target-domain observations are geometrically aligned with the latent space learned by an autoencoder trained on data from a source bridge and, subsequently, reconstructed using its decoder. Unlike conventional feature-alignment approaches, the proposed formulation transfers the reconstruction model itself, enabling target-domain evaluation without labels, classifier retraining, or threshold recalibration. The autoencoder is trained on baseline data collected during commissioning of the source bridge, using observations composed of natural frequencies as damage-sensitive features. Adaptation is performed through orthogonal Procrustes alignment in the latent space, followed by reconstruction with the source-trained decoder. Validation using the Z24 Bridge dataset demonstrates that the framework mitigates seasonal domain shift while preserving sensitivity to controlled damage. The approach is then transferred to a twin bridge over the Itacaiúnas River using only latent-space alignment and no model retraining. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework enables damage assessment across bridges while substantially reducing the data and training requirements for practical deployment.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for semi-active structural control using a variable inerter device
abstract: Structural control devices employing inerters have attracted considerable attention owing to their superior vibration mitigation performance. Variable inerter devices, which enable real-time adjustment of inertance and damping, offer further performance enhancement but also introduce a challenging nonlinear control problem. This paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based control strategy for a tuned variable inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TVIMET) installed in a five-story base-isolated building. The proposed controller is developed using recurrent proximal policy optimization (RPPO) with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to account for both the partially observable nature of practical structural control and the history-dependent nonlinear behavior of the lead–rubber bearing (LRB) isolation system. Numerical simulations are conducted under a wide range of earthquake excitations, and the proposed method is compared with passive base isolation, a passive tuned viscous mass damper (TVMD), and a semi-active tuned inertial mass electromagnetic transducer (TIMET). The proposed TVIMET successfully adapts both the inertance and damping coefficient according to the changing dynamic characteristics of the structure. Unlike the passive TVMD, which is designed assuming post-yield structural behavior, the proposed controller remains effective even under earthquake excitations that do not induce significant yielding of the isolation layer. It also achieves the best overall vibration reduction, particularly in terms of the RMS structural responses. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of simultaneously adapting the inertance and damping through DRL for nonlinear structural vibration control.

title: FNO-PD: A Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven framework for efficient dynamic response computation in vehicle-track coupled systems
abstract: Accurate and efficient computation of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems is essential for safe, smooth, and reliable high-speed railway operation and maintenance optimization. However, traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit a significant efficiency bottleneck in solving large-scale dynamic problems, while existing deep learning approaches struggle to accurately characterize the global dynamic coupling characteristics of the system. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Fourier neural operator-based physics-based data-driven (FNO-PD) framework for the efficient prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems. The framework comprises a physics-driven module and a data-driven module: the physics-driven module integrates physical information into FNO to predict train dynamic responses, while the data-driven module combines proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) with FNO for rail displacement field prediction. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed framework are evaluated using the probability density evolution method (PDEM) as a benchmark. Within the same vehicle-track numerical framework, the model is assessed for numerical generalization under measured track irregularity inputs, near-range speed extrapolation, and robustness to noise interference. Results demonstrate that the FNO-PD framework achieves high prediction accuracy and online computational efficiency, with good agreement between its predictions and the PDEM results. During online prediction, the proposed method achieves an approximately 1200-fold speedup over PDEM. Tests conducted with measured track irregularity inputs at speeds within and just outside the training range, together with noise interference tests, indicate satisfactory numerical generalization and noise robustness under the tested conditions. This study provides a novel and efficient technical pathway for the numerical prediction of dynamic responses in vehicle-track coupled systems, with potential for large-scale numerical analyses in high-speed railway engineering.

title: Physics-informed identification of dynamic propeller excitations via EM-based Kalman filtering
abstract: Accurate identification of propeller-induced hydrodynamic loads is crucial for vibration control and structural reliability in propeller propulsion systems. However, direct measurement of propeller excitation is infeasible due to the harsh operating environment and inherent structural constraints, which necessitates indirect identification approaches such as Kalman filtering. While these methods enable online estimation external inputs, the conventional random-walk assumption fails to represent the colored nature of hydrodynamic excitations, leading to spectrum mismatch and potential instability. To address this limitation, this study proposes an adaptive identification framework that integrates a scaled spherical simplex filter (S3F) with a physics-informed latent force model. The latent model combines an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck (OU) process with a single-degree-of-freedom (SDOF) system to simultaneously capture the broadband attenuation and hump-resonance features of propeller loads. Furthermore, to mitigate the difficulty of filter parameter tuning, an adaptive expectation–maximization (EM) strategy is incorporated to update noise covariances directly from structural response measurements, thereby enhancing robustness against uncertain prior settings. Numerical simulations and experimental validations confirm that, compared with the random-walk assumption, the proposed method significantly suppresses low-frequency drift, improves estimation accuracy, and maintains stability under varying noise conditions. These results highlight the method’s potential as a reliable strategy for indirect hydrodynamic load identification in propeller propulsion systems.

title: Physics-informed DeepONet with modal coordinate encoding for predicting dynamic responses of unseen motor housings
abstract: This study proposes a unified physics-informed machine-learning (PIML) framework for predicting the dynamic responses of traction motor housings under unseen geometric conditions. The framework incorporates three key forms of physical priors into a neural network. First, an observation bias is introduced through modal coordinate encoding, which embeds both geometric characteristics and excitation-dependent modal contributions into the neural network. Second, an inductive bias is incorporated by deploying a separable deep operator network architecture, which effectively learns nonlinear operator mappings and generalizes them to unseen housing geometries. Third, a learning bias is enforced by embedding the governing equations of structural dynamics into the training process to ensure physically consistent predictions. Novel training strategies are also employed to enhance convergence and numerical stability during physics-informed training. Quantitative evaluations and ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, achieving a mean MAPE of 3.32 % across the full test set and outperforming conventional neural networks. A design-optimization application further confirms that the proposed framework improves computational efficiency compared with conventional finite element analysis. Overall, this study establishes a robust framework for accelerating AI-driven design optimization and advancing intelligent structural engineering methodologies.

title: Stochastic model updating using conditional diffusion-based probabilistic generative models
abstract: This work aims to explore the integration of novel and powerful deep learning techniques and intractable engineering problems, especially by adopting deep generative models to tackle model updating problems under uncertainty. A conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model-based updating framework is presented to extend the field of deep generative models-based model updating methods. The diffusion model is a representative generative AI technique that employs a Markov chain to progressively add noise to data (forward process), then train a deep neural network to reverse this corruption (reverse process), enabling high-quality data generation. The conditional denoising diffusion extends the standard diffusion model, which guides data synthesis by injecting conditional inputs into the diffusion process. The conditional diffusion-based model updating framework consists of two primary neural networks: a conditional network and a denoising network. The conditional network can summarise the synthetic/measured response data into an informative fixed-length vector, called a conditional embedding, for guiding the training and denoising process of the denoising network. The denoising network can learn to predict the noise added in the forward process and denoise to generate the posterior samples conditioned on the conditional embedding. Both networks are trained jointly, and their architectures are flexible and problem-dependent. The framework is applied to solve a simulation-based problem, which is a customised version of the NASA and DNV Uncertainty Quantification Challenge 2025, and an experimental case study, which is a recently designed benchmark testbed with both experiment uncertainty and controllable parameter uncertainty.

title: A sequential bayesian operational mode classification for SHM under discrete operational variability
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) evaluates a structure’s condition by comparing its current state to a baseline representing a healthy state. However, many structures operate under multiple regimes, requiring multiple discrete baselines. This operational variability challenges conventional mitigation approaches, highlighting the need for methods that can automatically account for discrete variations in operation. This study leverages the concept of operational modes to address multiple discrete operating regimes as classes which are subsequently determined via a robust Bayesian classifier capable of handling variations, noise, and transition periods between modes. Specifically, a Bayesian Multinomial Logistic Regression model integrated with a Hidden Markov Model (BMLR-HMM) is proposed, where the probabilistic approach ensures robustness to noise, supports informed decision-making for each classification, and exploits the temporal structure in the evolution of the modes. The model was first tested on a simple. simulated dataset, and then using the vibrational responses from gearboxes on a Crew Transfer Vessel during operation. Results demonstrate high accuracy in mode classification, with the probabilistic nature of the model enabling uncertainty quantification, forming the basis for informed decision-making when classifications are less confident. This approach contributes to the development of robust classifiers for operational analysis in dynamic environments, with applications in SHM and other domains requiring mode identification for performance or integrity assessment.

title: Physics-guided generative data augmentation for vision-based signal processing under class-imbalanced conditions in directed energy deposition monitoring system
abstract: • Addresses signal processing limits from class-imbalanced DED molten pool signals. • Physics-guided CVAE-GAN synthesizes high-fidelity visual signals. • Thermodynamic losses enforce spatial and spectral signal consistency. • Augmented data improves decision boundaries for rare defect detection. • Validated on a real-world aerospace component with complex geometry. Vision-based signal processing is critical in metal additive manufacturing (AM), particularly within Directed Energy Deposition (DED), for capturing the rapid thermo-fluid dynamics essential for detecting process instabilities and ensuring structural integrity. While DED operates as an open, inherently non-stationary system and molten pool visual signals carry rich spatiotemporal information, effective processing is fundamentally constrained by the scarcity of anomalous events relative to stable deposition. This data sparsity leads to imbalanced training sets that fail to represent the full spectrum of transient process dynamics, causing classifiers to misclassify rare but critical failure modes and degrading overall monitoring performance. Crucially, conventional data augmentation techniques, being agnostic to the underlying physics, often introduce signal artefacts that violate governing thermodynamic constraints, thereby degrading the physical validity of the training data. To bridge the gap between data-driven feature learning and physical principles, this study proposes a physics-guided generative data augmentation framework based on a Conditional Variational Autoencoder–Generative Adversarial Network (CVAE-GAN). The framework explicitly learns the intrinsic physical manifold of the process, incorporating thermodynamically motivated loss functions to ensure the synthesis of high-fidelity, physically coherent molten pool visual signals. Validation through both spectral analysis and downstream classification confirms that the augmented signals preserve essential morphological and textural properties while significantly improving the decision boundaries of sequence classifiers. A case study on a complex aerospace component demonstrates the framework’s practical utility in enhancing robust in-situ monitoring under varying geometric conditions. By addressing the sparse representation of critical dynamics through a physics-aware methodology, this work offers a reliable pathway for advanced signal processing in data-scarce engineering systems.

title: A real-time and offline weld defect detection framework using planar EMT with selective measurement and deep learning
abstract: Electromagnetic tomography (EMT) offers a non-contact approach for weld defect imaging, yet traditional full-pair configurations suffer from low speed and limited adaptability to uneven weld surfaces. This study proposes an integrated real-time and offline weld-defect detection framework that couples selective coil-pair planar EMT with a prototype-guided similarity-fusion UNet (ProSiF-UNet). A 16-channel planar EMT sensor was developed, and a simplified sensitivity matrix using next-nearest coil pairs (d = 2) significantly reduced computation while preserving image fidelity. For real-time monitoring, a lightweight linear back projection (LBP)-based reconstruction enables 200+ frames per second (FPS) imaging, whereas an offline Landweber (LW) iteration ensures high-fidelity analysis. The prototype-guided similarity-fusion segmentation network (ProSiF-UNet) integrates cosine-similarity prototypes and exponential moving average (EMA)-based fusion to enhance defect segmentation on limited data, reducing missed detections by 40% compared with standard U-Net. The unified framework achieves a practical balance between speed, accuracy, and robustness, demonstrating strong potential for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled industrial weld inspection.

title: Probabilistic machine learning aided acoustic emission source localization in mode-I fracture test of multi-layer engineered wood
abstract: The mode-I fracture test is an important technique to evaluate materials’ fracture toughness and behaviors, where tracking the crack front is essential. This is usually done by visual inspection or computer vision, which could be problematic due to the large process zone and the difficulty of determining the onset of material cracking. Source localization via acoustic emission (AE) offers an alternative solution to this challenge. Locating AE sources in homogeneous materials is intuitively straightforward by leveraging phase differences from the measured time of arrival and potentially angle- or path-dependent velocity models. But it becomes complicated and intractable once the material heterogeneity comes into play. This is especially true for multilayer engineered wood, like laminated veneer lumber (LVL), where natural and manufacturing defects (knots, voids, discontinuity, and non-uniform textures) impose great challenges for 2D AE source localization. To cope with this problem, this study proposes probabilistic machine learning models, namely the Student-t process regression and the Gaussian process regression, for the 2D AE source localization on two LVL samples. To enhance prediction performance, both the multi-output Student-t and Gaussian process regression are developed. These probabilistic machine learning models are first trained and verified via pencil lead break tests and then applied to locate the crack tips in two mode-I fracture tests. Meanwhile, the Gaussian mixture models, along with Laplacian scores, are considered to identify AE events related to crack tip locations. The results suggest that the Student-t process can outperform the Gaussian process both in pencil lead break tests and mode-I fracture tests. The multi-output models can further enhance the prediction performance compared with the single-output processes. The multi-output Student-t process and the multi-output Gaussian process can support similar prediction performance when the degree of freedom of the Student-t process is large enough, and therefore, both are recommended for AE source localization in complex heterogeneous media like engineered wood.

title: Generative adversarial fault-tolerance for robust multimodal sensor fusion in industrial systems
abstract: Modern industrial systems rely heavily on multimodal sensor data to handle random emerging faults. To address this, we propose a novel generative adversarial framework embedded within a multimodal autoencoder architecture for active latent restoration of compromised sensor streams. Our method leverages a two-stage training process: first, a multimodal autoencoder is pre-trained on clean data to learn robust latent representations; then, a generative adversarial network is optimized to map corrupted latent vectors to their correct distributions while preserving cross-modal consistency through a task-specific penalty. Additionally, we adopt the discriminator optimization process to identify anomalies in the underlying data. Therefore, the discriminator is designed to conditionally initiate the generator’s fault-correction mechanism. Experiments on multimodal industrial robotic datasets demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms conventional methods in reconstructing accurate signals from corrupted inputs, even under several failure scenarios. The proposed system not only enhances fault resilience but also opens new directions for generative models in industrial automation, bridging the gap between robust data fusion and real-time error recovery.

title: FedSSLMfg: Federated self-supervised learning for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing
abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, reliable condition monitoring increasingly relies on cross-factory collaboration. However, operational data from industrial equipment are highly sensitive, leading to data silos that hinder collaboration and limit the development of generalizable diagnostic models. While federated learning (FL) provides a privacy-preserving paradigm that enables distributed factories to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data, its performance is often constrained by data heterogeneity and label scarcity. To address these two challenges, a federated self-supervised learning framework for heterogeneity-resilient and label-efficient condition monitoring in smart manufacturing, referred to as FedSSLMfg, is proposed. It involves three steps: signal preprocessing, federated self-supervised pre-training, and federated supervised fine-tuning. First, all vibration signals are unified to the same sampling frequency through anti-aliasing filtering and downsampling, and then transformed into time–frequency representations using the continuous wavelet transform. Then, feature representations are learned using a masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning scheme within a federated setting. Lastly, the learned representations are transferred to downstream tasks by fine-tuning the federated models with labeled samples. The effectiveness of FedSSLMfg is validated on a federated setting consisting of three real-world rolling bearing datasets. Experiments show that it achieves high diagnostic accuracy and strong robustness under heterogeneous data distributions and label scarcity, outperforming both federated and non-federated baselines. Ablation studies further reveal that FedSSLMfg has low dependency on data augmentation, benefits from moderate masking ratios, and maintains high accuracy even when only a small fraction of samples are labeled.

title: Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) for real-time long-term calibration of rotordynamic models
abstract: Efficient, timely and accurate calibration of digital twins is critical for their application in real-time decision-making and condition monitoring. Digital twins, as dynamic virtual representations of connected physical systems, require continuous recalibration to adapt to evolving system states, environmental changes, and degradation over time. Without timely and effective recalibration, discrepancies between the digital and physical counterparts accumulate, potentially leading to compromised safety and operational inefficiencies. This study addresses these challenges by introducing the Online Adaptive Reinforcement Learning and Approximate Bayesian Computation (OARL-ABC) framework, a novel and model-agnostic calibration algorithm. Building upon the foundational RL-ABC framework, OARL-ABC offers enhanced adaptability, scalability, and robustness, facilitating real-time adjustment of model parameters across diverse systems. By integrating reinforcement learning strategies with approximate Bayesian computation, the proposed framework effectively accounts for uncertainties in model parameters and environmental variables, ensuring reliable predictions in complex and dynamic scenarios. To validate its efficacy, the OARL-ABC framework is applied to the calibration of a rotordynamic system for rotating machine fault diagnosis, demonstrating its capability to maintain alignment between the digital and physical domains in real-time. However, while the results demonstrate improved real-time calibration performance in this context compared to conventional calibration methods, OARL-ABC remains limited by its use of sampling techniques for repeated full-scale model runs. Further improvement should prioritize applying the method to a broader range of use cases, exploring simplified model forms, or enhancing the sampling scheme to run more efficiently.

title: Study on real-time prediction for porosity in laser melting based on a digital twin-driven deep learning framework
abstract: The keyhole-induced pore defect is recognized as a major nuisance in laser melting (such as welding and 3D printing). As a crucial indicator for assessing the specific severity of pores, porosity has long been obtained only through complex and offline internal inspection after manufacturing. In this paper, guided by the formation mechanism of pores revealed via numerical simulation, a digital twin-driven deep learning framework (DTDLF) is proposed that enables direct and real-time porosity prediction during laser beam welding. In the perception field, keyhole depth and keyhole opening circumference are acquired through multi-sensing measurement and signal processing. In the physical field, simulation can acquire maximum temperature on the bottom wall of the keyhole. Subsequently, a sparse auto-encoder is constructed to fuse the original fluctuation characteristics mined from their respective digital twin data sources, and all of the obtained overall features are demonstrated to be highly correlated with porosity. In the DTDLF, a tandem structure of two deep neural networks (DNNs) connected in series is adopted, where the former DNN conducts online prediction of the fused overall feature in the physical field utilizing process parameters to circumvent the long simulation runtime, and the latter DNN couples all the fused overall features in the perception-physics fields for predicting porosity online. The final results indicate that the DTDLF has a significant accuracy advantage over monitoring frameworks that use solely single-field information, and meanwhile its real-time performance is not compromised.

title: Physics-guided neural network architectures for modeling nonlinear behaviors: Application to shape memory alloy wires
abstract: A novel physics-guided machine learning framework is proposed for the numerical simulation of complex nonlinear behaviors and to improve the generalization capability of data-driven models under limited information conditions. It combines an a priori physics-based model with a new neural network (NN) architecture designed to compensate for its inaccuracies. A differential evolution algorithm is adopted for the parametric identification of the physics-based model. On the other hand, an original transformer-based NN, enhanced with a long short-term memory (LSTM) feature fusion layer, is employed to capture the inherent aspects of the nonlinear behavior that are overlooked by the physics-based model so as to reduce overall errors.This approach is applied to simulate the hysteretic tensile behavior of NiTiNOL shape memory alloy wires subject to different loading rates. A comprehensive experimental comparative assessment is carried out between a physics-based (phenomenological) model and four NN architectures, including the uni- and bi-directional LSTM models, a transformer model, as well as the proposed model merging LSTM and transformer components. These NN architectures are employed both in a fully data-driven setting and within the physics-guided framework herein conceived with the purpose of mitigating the inaccuracies arising from the selected phenomenological model.The results indicate that the proposed NN architecture connecting LSTM and transformer components achieves the best overall performance. Furthermore, the physics-guided approach consistently improves both accuracy and reliability of the predictions.

title: Towards a more realistic evaluation of machine learning models for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Reliable detection of bearing faults is essential for maintaining the safety and operational efficiency of rotating machinery. While recent advances in machine learning (ML), particularly deep learning, have shown strong performance in controlled settings, many studies fail to generalize to real-world applications due to methodological flaws, most notably data leakage. This paper investigates the issue of data leakage in vibration-based bearing fault diagnosis and its impact on model evaluation. We demonstrate that common dataset partitioning strategies, such as segment-wise and condition-wise splits, introduce spurious correlations that inflate performance metrics. To address this, we propose a rigorous, leakage-free evaluation methodology centered on bearing-wise data partitioning, ensuring no overlap between the physical components used for training and testing. Additionally, we reformulate the classification task as a multi-label problem, enabling the detection of co-occurring fault types and the use of prevalence-independent metrics based on the ROC curve. Beyond preventing leakage, we also examine the effect of dataset diversity on generalization, showing that the number of unique training bearings is a decisive factor for achieving robust performance. We evaluate our methodology on four widely adopted datasets: Case Western Reserve University (CWRU), Paderborn University (PU), University of Ottawa (UORED-VAFCLS) and Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST bearing). This study highlights the importance of leakage-aware evaluation protocols and provides practical guidelines for dataset partitioning, model selection, and validation, fostering the development of more trustworthy ML systems for industrial fault diagnosis applications.

title: Multimodal spatiotemporal graph attention network with uncertainty quantification for aircraft engine prognostics
abstract: Aircraft engine prognostics is critical for safety, cost reduction, and efficient fleet management. Despite the availability of rich multimodal sensor data, most current prognostic approaches are limited to single-modality analysis, lack uncertainty quantification, and rely on predefined sensor graphs. To address these limitations, this paper introduces the Multimodal Spatiotemporal Graph Attention Network with Uncertainty Quantification (MST-GAT-UQ), a novel deep learning framework for aircraft engine prognostics. The proposed model integrates temporal patterns via CNN-LSTM networks, spatial correlations through graph attention mechanisms, and frequency signatures using Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) with 2D CNN processing. Key innovations include a correlation-driven graph construction method that automatically learns sensor relationships from operational data, hierarchical attention fusion to adaptively weight different modalities, and Monte Carlo dropout augmented by temperature scaling for simultaneous Remaining Useful Life (RUL) and health state prediction with calibrated uncertainty intervals. The framework is comprehensively validated on a real-world operational dataset comprising 84 sensors and 43,492 samples from F100-PW-229 turbofan engines, achieving R 2 = 0.911, RMSE = 0.087, MAE = 0.072 on a normalized RUL scale within a synthetic-label verification framework (no ground-truth operational RUL is available for this dataset; reported metrics quantify the model’s fidelity in reproducing a synthetically imposed linear degradation trajectory and should not be interpreted as ground-truth remaining-life predictions), and a synthetic health-state replication accuracy of 99.5% (auxiliary task; health-state labels are a deterministic step-function of the synthetic RUL signal and carry no independent diagnostic information). Comparative analysis against the standard NASA C-MAPSS benchmark is presented as a zero-shot domain-transfer diagnostic, characterising the label-distribution shift between the two datasets, and confirms that native C-MAPSS training yields positive R 2 across all four subsets (FD001–FD004: R 2 = 0.607–0.863). This work represents a significant step toward reliable, uncertainty-aware, and multimodal prognostic systems for safety–critical aviation applications, with uncertainty intervals that are directionally informative but moderately overconfident (empirical coverage 88.7% at the 95% nominal level; ECE = 0.254), indicating that further calibration refinement is required before safety–critical operational deployment.

title: Anti-load performance evaluation method for electro-hydrostatic actuators based on physics-embedded attention mechanism
abstract: High-precision performance degradation evaluation of electro-hydrostatic actuators (EHAs) is critical for aerospace reliability. Among all potential hardware degradation, internal leakage stands out as the most frequent and dominant fault in EHA systems. However, existing methods often fail in dynamic flight environments, where genuine internal leakage signatures are deeply entangled with external variable load disturbances. To address this load-fault coupling challenge, this study proposes an Anti-load Performance Evaluation Method. Firstly, an EHA dynamic model is established to analytically derive a Baseline Contribution Score (BCS), explicitly quantifying the relative sensitivities of multi-source signals to faults versus loads. Then after a dual-screening purification of statistical features, the BCS is deployed as a dual-purpose physical constraint linking the subsequent core modules. It first functions as a physical prior in a Physics-Embedded Channel Attention Mechanism to adaptively highlight fault signatures while suppressing load noise, and then acts as a regularization penalty within a Correlation-Regularized Stacked Autoencoder to constrain the deep fusion process. Driven by this sequential BCS guidance, the network ultimately condenses these refined representations into a highly robust, anti-load 1D Health Indicator. Validated through simulations and physical testbench experiments, the ACFN successfully disentangles complex coupled signals into a linearly separable manifold. It achieves a superior diagnostic accuracy of 95.24% under the 3 kN load. This physics-guided framework effectively bridges the gap between mechanistic interpretability and deep learning, providing a highly robust solution for EHA health management.

title: Interpretable U-Net RCNN for blind peak detection in vibration spectra
abstract: Accurate peak detection in vibration spectra is key to early fault diagnosis but remains challenging due to noise and unknown spectral content. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining the benefits of U-Nets and Region-based Convolutional Neural Networks for blind peak detection, trained on complex simulated 1D data with extension to real-world signals. The model combines classification and regression to identify and localise peaks without prior knowledge of the signal or machine. Its performance is benchmarked against the Exact Order Model Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotational Invariance Technique and a Topological Peak Identification approach using labelled simulated data, demonstrating robustness and practical effectiveness. The method is further tested on real offshore wind turbine data, where it successfully detects visually identifiable peaks, confirming its applicability in real-world scenarios.

title: Deep learning based reconstruction of fiber orientation in short fiber reinforced composites from ultrasonic wave responses
abstract: Fiber orientation plays an important role in the mechanical behavior of short fiber-reinforced composites, yet its internal distribution is difficult to characterize nondestructively. This study proposes a deep learning-based framework to reconstruct fiber orientation fields from boundary ultrasonic wave responses. A two-dimensional anisotropic wave propagation model with free-boundary conditions was developed to simulate wave signals in composite plates, where the local anisotropy was governed by sectional fiber orientation. Based on this model, a synthetic dataset was generated using a sectional representation of the plate. The simulated sensor signals were used as inputs to a multilayer perceptron, while the section-wise principal-direction angles were encoded using an angle aware representation to account for periodicity. The trained model directly predicted the orientation field from the simulated boundary wave responses. Reconstruction accuracy was evaluated using wrap-aware angular error metrics. Parametric studies were conducted to examine the effects of dataset size, excitation frequency, anisotropy strength, sensor ablation, and wave transmission factor on prediction performance. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively reconstruct the main features of the section-wise principal-direction field and remains reasonably robust under varying sensing and material conditions. The proposed approach provides a promising data-driven strategy for nondestructive characterization of internal fiber orientation in short fiber-reinforced composites.

title: Physics-constrained neural parameter calibration of a Bouc-Wen hysteresis model for bolted joint assemblies
abstract: Bolted joints are characterized by friction-induced hysteresis and response dependence on excitation and tightening conditions, which complicates the calibration of reduced-order nonlinear models. A physics-constrained neural framework is introduced for calibrating a Bouc-Wen model using mean vibration records obtained under varying tightening torques. For each torque, a bounded neural generator proposes admissible model parameters, and a differentiable forward solver integrates displacement, velocity, and the model-internal hysteretic state. Calibration relies exclusively on measured velocity and measurement-derived displacement, while additional excitation levels are reserved for evaluating the torque-specific calibrated ensembles. Multiple independent calibration paths are maintained according to a prescribed convergence criterion and are organized using loss-informed empirical Gibbs weighting. Complete joint parameter vectors are then propagated to obtain time-domain, receptance, and hysteresis summaries. The results indicate torque-conditioned parameter organizations, consistent convergence behavior across most calibration paths, and close agreement with measured resonance locations. Propagation at excitation levels excluded from calibration further demonstrates that the calibrated ensembles can reproduce the principal amplitude-dependent response trends. The proposed framework thus offers a systematic approach for neural parameter calibration and empirical variability propagation, while preserving the prescribed Bouc-Wen dynamics throughout the inverse problem. • Physics-constrained neural calibration of Bouc-Wen bolted-joint parameters. • Mean-response calibrations are performed independently at two torques levels. • The unobserved hysteretic state is integrated using a measured-only loss. • Converged optimization paths form loss-informed joint empirical ensembles. • Frozen ensembles are propagated to amplitudes excluded from calibration.

title: Performance-based probabilistic RUL prediction via particle filtering with neural-guided inference
abstract: Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is essential for efficient operations and predictive maintenance of industrial systems. Prognostics is traditionally structured as a two-step procedure comprising estimation of the current system condition and prediction of future behavior and condition. Many data-driven approaches map sensor measurements directly to RUL without explicitly modeling degradation dynamics. We propose a data-driven prognostic framework that preserves this estimation–prediction structure without requiring physics-based state models. In the estimation stage, health indices are inferred from sensor measurements. Degradation parameters are treated probabilistically and inferred within a Bayesian framework, with online sequential updates via particle filtering. In the prediction stage, the stochastic degradation model is evaluated conditioned on the inferred parameter posterior, yielding an RUL distribution as a random variable with a hitting time. An offline-trained neural network serves as a particle-filter (PF) controller to improve adaptability while maintaining principled uncertainty propagation. Evaluation on the N-CMAPSS benchmark demonstrates competitive RUL accuracy and statistically grounded uncertainty across operating conditions, and comparisons indicate the advantages of explicitly separating estimation from prediction in data-driven prognostics.

title: Tool-grounded large language models for decision-level fusion in fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern condition-monitoring systems generate heterogeneous information, such as high-rate sensor streams, derived health indicators, and discrete event histories, that must be combined into actionable diagnostic statements. Large language models (LLMs) are attractive as a decision-level fusion mechanism because they natively handle the textual modality, but their use in safety-critical fault diagnosis is impeded by hallucinated numerical content and stochastic outputs. This paper proposes a two-level information-fusion framework that uses an LLM as a constrained fusion operator rather than as a generator of facts. At the feature level, a recursive joint state-and-fault estimator built on a linear state-space model produces a vector of derived indicators, including an estimate of the actuator-fault parameter and its uncertainty. At the decision level, the LLM is restricted to interact with the estimator state and the event history exclusively through a finite library of typed deterministic tools, and must copy every numerical token in its response from a tool output. Grounding of the response is then satisfied by construction, and consistency follows once the sequence of tool calls is fixed. The framework is illustrated on a realistic actuator-fault scenario in which an autopilot-driven autonomous surface vessel encounters three fault events of different characters and the LLM produces reproducible operator-facing reports. A structured comparison against the two alternative reporting architectures available for this task, a rule-based template reporter driven by the same estimator and a flat-prompt LLM given the same numerical context, identifies open-ended query coverage at fixed numerical reliability as the property that neither alternative provides, and states the metrics under which that claim is to be tested.

title: Review of fault diagnosis for rotating machinery: Prior knowledge integration in data-driven methods benefits model interpretability and generalizability
abstract: Fault diagnosis for rotating machinery has always been a hot research topic in both academia and industry. This review provides a holistic and concise overview of relevant studies that are categorized into three main research directions: fault mechanisms, signal processing, and machine learning. It is found that studies on intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) today face two significant challenges: model interpretability and generalizability. Model interpretability refers to the degree to which humans can understand the decision process in IFD models; generalizability refers to the performance decrease that IFD models exhibit when tested on samples with different data distributions from the training samples. These two challenges are especially critical, given the risk-sensitive nature of machinery fault diagnosis and the ever-increasing demand for responsible artificial intelligence. At the same time, it is also observed that prior knowledge derived from fault mechanisms and signal processing is not fully utilized in most IFD studies. As a result, although many methods have been proposed to address the two challenges, the final outcome is still not satisfactory. Recently, much attention has been paid to integrating prior knowledge derived from studies of fault mechanisms and signal processing into IFD models. This integration is effective and enlightening. However, prior knowledge and integration techniques are diverse and not systematic. Therefore, we provided a clear taxonomy and an in-depth discussion at the end of this paper to support the development and application of prior knowledge integrated IFD.
