title: Variational and approximated Bayesian updating with data-driven autoencoder and homotopy eigenpair expansions
abstract: The variational inference is frequently employed in Bayesian updating framework to enable efficient estimation of the posterior distribution. To enhance its efficiency and adaptability in uncertain and high-dimensional applications, this study proposes a variational Bayesian model updating method that integrates Homotopy Stochastic Finite Element Method (HSFEM) into the architecture of Variational Autoencoder (VAE). A deep neural network is set as the encoder to be optimized, and HSFEM is used as the decoder to estimate the likelihood function through Approximate Bayesian Computation (ABC), thus obtaining explicit expression of Evidence Lower BOund (ELBO). The posterior distribution can be efficiently approximated by maximizing the ELBO. In this architecture, the Bhattacharyya distance is introduced as the distance metric in ABC to ensure a precise quantification of the likelihood function; Gaussian kernel based binning technology is used to construct a derivable Probability Mass Function (PMF) of the distribution, reducing the calculation cost of estimation of probability density with certain accuracy. The proposed approach also addresses the potential complexity of the ‘two-step procedures’ when employing both the Euclidian distance and Bhattacharyya distance as metrics in two separate steps. Two numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed method, as well as its advantages in facing high-dimensional problems. Finally, the proposed method was applied to update a lab-scale aircraft model, yielding satisfactory results and demonstrating its practical value for engineering applications.

title: A novel interval prediction model for buffeting response of a long-span bridge based on machine learning
abstract: With bridges being longer and lighter, buffeting response can be of importance for bridge management and corresponding prediction model is needed. Data-driven models have advantages on prediction accuracy and computational efficiency compared to traditional buffeting analysis. However, existing data-driven models mainly focus on deterministic prediction, few models can perform probabilistic prediction. To this end, a novel interval prediction model for buffeting response of a long-span bridge is proposed. The proposed model selects gated recurrent unit neural network as the basic module, and it incorporates quantile regression and lower upper bound estimation for interval prediction. Specifically, the proposed model employs quantile regression for initial estimation of interval bounds in the form of quantiles, and then it uses lower upper bound estimation method to optimize initial bounds to enhance prediction accuracy. Besides, to enhance training efficiency of lower upper bound estimation method, an adaptive-weight training strategy that can tune the weight parameter during the training process is proposed. The proposed model is validated by the monitoring data of a long-span bridge, where effectiveness and superiority of the proposed interval prediction model are demonstrated.

title: Data-driven system identification using improved recurrent network for structure-borne noise in vehicle cabin
abstract: This study proposes a data-driven system identification framework for predicting structure-borne noise in vehicle cabins using real-world driving data. An Inception network, applied in the time–frequency domain, is combined with a linearized pseudo-time stepping method to enhance accuracy and generalization. Structural acceleration is used as input, and cabin noise as output, with both signals transformed via short-time Fourier transform. The model effectively captures hysteretic and nonlinear behaviors under various driving conditions. As a result, the proposed framework achieves improved prediction performance across multiple frequency bands and scenarios, demonstrating its potential for practical vehicle noise modelling.

title: Spatio-temporal MLP model incorporating physical-informational neural networks for remaining useful life prediction
abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, as a core technology to facilitate the transformation of equipment maintenance from preventive to predictive, uses sensor monitoring information to predict equipment RUL and provides an important basis for intelligent maintenance and decision-making. However, current prediction models generally suffer from high model complexity, low prediction accuracy for multiple operating conditions and poor interpretability. To address the above issues, a spatio-temporal perceptron model that incorporates physical information is proposed for RUL prediction. Specifically, the model is based on a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) network structure, and a gated Attention Spatio-Temporal Multilayer Perceptron model (AST-MLP) is proposed, which significantly reduces the model complexity while sufficiently learning the deeper information of spatio-temporal dimensions through a lightweight architectural design, so as to improve the computational efficiency and prediction accuracy. Secondly, to effectively utilize the loss of partial differential equations and the loss of lifespan, a Fused Loss Model of Lifespan and Physical Information (FLP-Loss) is proposed. This model makes the optimization process more consistent with the physical laws and improves the accuracy of the predictions. Ultimately, comprehensive experiments were conducted on the C-MAPSS dataset, and the results showed that the model has higher prediction accuracy and better prediction results, especially in complex environments.

title: Physical model-embedded neural network for milling surface roughness monitoring via spindle current signals
abstract: To address the high experimental and implementation costs associated with data-driven surface roughness monitoring methods, a novel surface roughness monitoring method based on Physical Model-Embedded Neural Network (PMENN) is proposed in this paper. The key innovation lies in integrating the surface roughness physical model into neural network architecture, where neural network is employed to modify the theoretical values of surface roughness. First, we reveal a nonlinear relationship between surface roughness and spindle servomotor current through combination of surface roughness physical model and cutting force-current correlation analysis. Subsequently, dedicated neural network modules for cutting force calculation and surface roughness calculation are separately trained, enabling dynamometer-free roughness monitoring in actual machining. Experimental validation through milling operations demonstrates the effectiveness of this method. Furthermore, a practical application in aero engine box casing cover manufacturing confirms PMENN’s superior performance in few-shot learning, highlighting its advantage in actual machining with limited training data.

title: CNC-VLM: An RLHF-optimized industrial large vision-language model with multimodal learning for imbalanced CNC fault detection
abstract: CNC fault detection in industrial scenarios still suffers from several important challenges, such as poor generalization to imbalanced samples, poor consistency between visual-textual semantics, and limited utilization of domain-specific multimodal knowledge. To address these issues, we propose an RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)-optimized industrial large model (CNC-VLM) that leverages vision-language multimodal knowledge for autonomous fault detection. CNC-VLM consists of a visual encoder, a projector, and a textual decoder. Specifically, the visual encoder extracts discriminative visual landmarks from fault time-frequency images, which are then further mapped into a modality-aligned latent space via a projection layer. The decoder incorporates a vision-language cross-attention mechanism to combine visual semantics with textual prompts for precise reasoning and detection. We further design a direct preference optimization (DPO) algorithm for CNC fault detection based on the RLHF training paradigm, which combines the model output with human feedback (expert knowledge) to enhance the imbalanced detection ability for small sample faults. Through engineering samples obtained from CNC machines, the verification results demonstrate that CNC-VLM significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art models in terms of accuracy and F1-score. Moreover, CNC-VLM can automatically generate detection descriptions and maintenance suggestions, showing good potential for practical deployment in the field of intelligent manufacturing.

title: A data-driven framework for distributed dynamic load identification incorporating physics-based temporal causality constraints
abstract: As the second inverse problem in structural dynamics, dynamic load identification is highly dependent on the system’s intrinsic properties. For distributed loads, establishing an accurate mapping between structural responses and the underlying dynamic excitations remains particularly challenging, and the ill-posed nature of the problem further amplifies measurement noise, leading to significant identification errors. To overcome these difficulties, this study proposes a novel distributed dynamic load identification framework based on a Transformer architecture that directly learns the inverse dynamic relationship without requiring explicit system parameter estimation. Specifically, Legendre orthogonal polynomial decomposition is first employed to transform the load identification task into the estimation of a finite set of orthogonal polynomial coefficients. Building upon this framework, innovative architectural optimizations are introduced by embedding physical constraints into attention computation and linear prediction, leveraging the temporal causality of dynamic responses. These enhancements improve model interpretability and substantially reduce training difficulty. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately identify sinusoidal, impact, and random loads under various noise levels. Furthermore, a distributed load identification experiment on a cantilever beam is carried out, validating the practical applicability of the approach. Finally, the selection of model hyperparameters is discussed based on fitting and generalization performance, and a comparative study with traditional dynamic calibration methods was conducted in an experimental setting, further demonstrating the superior accuracy, noise robustness, and practical reliability of the proposed framework.

title: A vision-based vibration measurement method of bridge structure using swin transformer motion magnification and improved recurrent all-pairs field transform algorithms
abstract: Accurate measurement of bridge vibrations under load excitation is often impeded using traditional computer vision-based measurement (CVBM) methods in complex environments, particularly when small amplitudes and low-texture surfaces are involved. This paper proposes a CVBM method that estimates the full-field dynamic displacement and modal parameters of bridge structures by integrating the swin transformer motion magnification (STMM) with the improved recurrent all-pairs field transform (IRAFT) algorithm. The STMM algorithm could capture high-frequency information about structural vibrations while effectively suppressing noise, blurring, and motion artifacts during magnification. The IRAFT algorithm could improve the calculation accuracy of full-field optical flow in low-texture and large-motion scenes. First, vibrational videos of bridge structures are acquired and calibrated, and then the pixel motion in the video is magnified by the STMM algorithm. Subsequently, the IRAFT algorithm is employed to compute full-field optical flow from the magnified video. Finally, pixel motion within regions of interest is converted to a displacement time-history curve through motion normalization and a scale-factor method, from which modal parameters are identified based on fast Fourier transform and covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification. The proposed method was validated on a synthetic truss bridge, a laboratory experiment of a Q235 simply-supported beam, and on-site inspection of a pedestrian overpass. The results show that the utilization of the STMM algorithm is not only effective in acquiring high-frequency information of structural vibrations but also has the advantage of suppressing motion noise and artifacts during magnification. By integrating the STMM with the IRAFT algorithm, the identification performance of the full-field dynamic displacement and modal parameters of structures is significantly improved, with better robustness to illumination changes and partial occlusion.

title: Bias drift compensation of butterfly gyroscope under temperature change with two-stage hybrid deep learning model
abstract: This paper proposes a two-stage hybrid deep learning compensation strategy that integrates Bayesian optimization (BO), Transformer, and temporal convolutional network (TCN) to suppress bias drift in butterfly gyroscope under temperature change. First, a theoretical model for the butterfly gyroscope output was established, and the composition of thermally induced bias was analyzed. Subsequently, the original bias output signal from the gyroscope control system was decomposed using variational mode decomposition (VMD). Permutation entropy and Pearson correlation coefficient were employed as screening methods to extract the intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) caused by temperature change and strip noise. Then other temperature-related parameters that can be output serve as physically interpretable feature vector, which, together with the bias signal from the previous time step, constructs an enhanced input sequence that integrates historical memory. Subsequently, a two-stage compensation strategy was established: In the first stage, the Transformer model, which is equipped with self-attention mechanisms that capture long-range dependency, was then employed to model and compensate for deterministic drift within the reconstructed bias signal; In the second stage, the preliminarily compensated non-deterministic residual signal was fed into the TCN network, which has strong local modeling capabilities to further fit residual error, achieving precise compensation for local fluctuations. Finally, BO was employed for adaptive joint hyperparameter tuning across preprocessing and submodels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed two-stage hybrid compensation strategy achieves superior compensation accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability compared to traditional polynomial fitting methods and various single or combined deep learning models. Specifically, it improves the standard deviation of the compensated bias signal by over 38.3% and 42.8%, respectively, across different temperature change rates and gyroscope samples.

title: Deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for early prediction of milling surface roughness
abstract: As a key part of intelligent machining systems, surface roughness prediction plays a vital role in improving machining efficiency and ensuring product quality. However, the prediction accuracy of traditional mechanism-based physical models is restricted by idealized assumptions, whereas data-driven approaches rely excessively on monitoring signals, limiting their ability to capture future machining information and lacking model interpretability. To address these issues, this study proposes a deep learning-based mechanism- and signal-driven framework for the early prediction of milling surface roughness. First, a physical model of surface morphology is established by comprehensively accounting for the tool rigid motion trajectory, runout, and deflection. The global mechanism knowledge generated by the physical model is embedded into the data-driven modeling process. Second, multi-source signals are synchronously monitored online during machining, and preliminary multi-domain features are extracted from the time-series data to support subsequent modeling. Third, an integrated mechanism- and signal-driven Transformer (IMSformer) is constructed, consisting of the deep mechanism knowledge mining module, deep signal feature extraction module, mechanism-signal fusion module, and regression prediction module. Mechanism knowledge and signal features are jointly used as inputs to IMSformer, enabling the prediction task through deep extraction and fusion of high-level representations. Experimental validation is conducted under both the same and different conditions using milling data collected from a machining center, demonstrating the superior performance of the proposed framework.

title: Lamb wave-based cross-domain damage identification for CFRP composite structures using a modular deep learning framework
abstract: Machine learning in Lamb wave-based damage identification has significantly advanced diagnostic technologies due to its exceptional feature extraction capability in processing massive monitoring data. However, existing methods still exhibit significant limitations in identifying damage at locations not covered by the training data, which severely hinders their practical engineering applications. To address this, this study proposes a cross-domain damage identification method for CFRP composite structures based on a modular deep learning framework. The framework architecture integrates three core modules: a multi-channel signal fusion module, a feature extraction module, and a domain adaptation regression module. The multi-channel signal fusion module enhances the characterization of damage features by integrating Lamb wave damage-scattered signals from multiple sensing paths. The feature extraction module employs continuous wavelet convolutional layers to realize adaptive extraction and interpretability enhancement of sensitive features of Lamb wave signals. The domain adaptation regression module introduces a novel joint distribution adaptation approach, significantly improving the model’s generalization performance for unseen damage locations. Lamb wave signals are collected using the lead zirconate titanate (PZT) sensors array on a composite stiffened panel and an aluminum plate, covering four cross-domain damage localization tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significantly lower localization errors in identifying unseen damage locations compared to the existing state-of-the-art damage localization methods. Meanwhile, the framework maintains its excellent cross-domain generalization ability under scenarios involving variations in damage size, material, and structure.

title: Utilization of acoustic emission signals for monitoring CFRP drilling quality with AI-based methods: evaluation, prediction, and morphological reconstruction
abstract: Drilling Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymers (CFRP) is a critical process in composite manufacturing, but ensuring high precision and quality poses significant challenges. The presence of defects such as delamination, fraying, and rough hole walls directly impacts the material’s performance and durability. Conventional quality control methods often involve post-process inspection, which is time-consuming and cannot prevent defects during manufacturing. There is a need for real-time, non-destructive monitoring methods to maintain high-quality standards while improving efficiency. This study aims to develop an advanced approach for real-time monitoring and prediction of CFRP drilling quality using Acoustic Emission (AE) signals and state-of-the-art machine learning models. A robotic drilling system was employed to conduct the experiments. During drilling, AE signals were collected, and hole edge images were captured using an industrial camera. White-light confocal profilometry was used to acquire hole wall morphology data. Relationships between drilling parameters and hole quality were analyzed, alongside AE signal features. Advanced AI models were proposed, including a probabilistic drilling stage identification model, K-means-based defect evaluation, a Transformer-based real-time defect monitoring model, and a VAE-Transformer hybrid model for reconstructing hole wall morphologies from AE signals. The proposed models successfully characterized drilling defects and enabled precise identification of drilling stages. Real-time defect monitoring based on AE signal slices showcased high accuracy, while the reconstruction model effectively predicted hole wall morphologies. This study introduces a transformative approach for real-time, non-destructive CFRP quality monitoring during drilling, significantly enhancing production efficiency and ensuring defect-free manufacturing in aerospace and automotive applications.

title: Data-model-co-driven approach for real-time reconstruction of unmeasured responses via multi-fidelity surrogate modeling
abstract: The data-model-co-driven approach offers a promising solution for real-time reconstruction of structural responses without prior measurements, exemplified by unmeasured responses. However, the accuracy of existing co-driven approaches is highly dependent on the fidelity of the Finite Element (FE) model, which limits their practical applicability in Structural Health Monitoring (SHM). To tackle this issue, this study proposes a co-driven framework based on multi-fidelity surrogate modeling. In the proposed framework, a Low-Fidelity (LF) model substitutes the FE model to estimate the full-field structural responses, while a High-Fidelity (HF) model learns the error mechanism between FE-simulated and measured data and subsequently improves the accuracy of all LF outputs. The proposed approach is validated through the full-field reconstruction of cable forces in a cable net structure. For three cable force locations assumed to be unmeasured, an investigation into the influence of the correlation between LF outputs and measurements on reconstruction accuracy reveals that the proposed approach is not strictly dependent on the fidelity of the FE-simulated data. Meanwhile, the proposed approach achieves a maximum Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 17.93 kN at these measurement points, compared with RMSE values exceeding 38 kN obtained using an existing co-driven approach. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the proposed approach enables real-time reconstruction of unmeasured structural responses with acceptable accuracy, while reducing its dependence on the fidelity of the FE model.

title: Deep learning-based dynamic load reconstruction and localization: A novel multi-task learning framework with physical distance-aware graph attention
abstract: Direct measurement of dynamic loads is often infeasible due to deployment constraints or harsh environments, necessitating indirect inference through responses. Traditional methods face limitations due to reliance on precise modal parameters, while existing data-driven approaches often decouple reconstruction and localization tasks, ignoring their inherent coupling. This paper proposes a novel multi-task learning (MTL) framework for dynamic load identification that synergizes graph attention network (GAT) with physical distance-aware attention mechanism. The graph structure representing the dynamic load identification issue is constructed and the GAT layer-based shared feature encoder is introduced to process spatially distributed sensor response as node features. This design utilizes task-specific attention weights that facilitates cross-task knowledge transfer while preserving the uniqueness of each task, reconstruction and localization. Furthermore, physical distance between the sensor and the load locations is embedded as constraints of attention weight learning, which leads to the adaptive narrowing of solution space and the improvement of localization accuracy. A series of numerical and experimental scenarios are designed to validate the performance of the method. The findings demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve satisfactory outcomes in both reconstruction and localization tasks while circumventing the intricate process of modeling dynamic characteristics. Moreover, the proposed method is insensitive to sensor arrangement and can function even when the response data sources of the training and testing phases are different, rendering it practical in engineering scenarios.

title: Physics-guided neural network for force identification in component-based transfer path analysis
abstract: In component-based transfer path analysis (TPA), the accuracy of estimated results depends on the treatment of accelerance matrix inversion for equivalent force identification. However, the measured accelerance often exhibits significant uncertainty, even though it should satisfy the reciprocity condition, which substantially degrades TPA accuracy. Conventional regularization methods, which use uncertain accelerance, mainly focus on mitigating ill-conditioning without effectively resolving the problem. In this study, an innovative physics-guided neural network model was proposed to replace the conventional matrix inversion process in component-based TPA. The proposed model acts as a trainable version of TPA capable of compensating for uncertainties in nondriving-point accelerance. Its architecture is designed to identify the equivalent forces at the hidden layer, and tailored training strategies improve estimation accuracy. Physical information, such as the driving-point accelerance and noise transfer function, is incorporated into the model to preserve the physical characteristics of the system during training. In addition, the output layer is virtually expanded by exploiting the property that the equivalent forces remain invariant to modifications in the passive part stiffness, thereby improving the accuracy of the estimated forces. The proposed method was validated through a numerical simulation in which intended uncertainty was imposed on the known accelerance, and the estimated equivalent forces closely matched the references despite the uncertainty. Furthermore, the application of a road noise vehicle experiment revealed that the suggested neural network-based method surpasses conventional inversion-based methods in accuracy and offers a reliable framework for component-based TPA in practical applications.

title: Head-tracking active road noise control by real-time path adaptation using neural networks
abstract: Conventional active road noise control (ARNC) with virtual sensing requires accurate secondary path estimates and observation filters. However, these paths are dependent on the listener’s head position, and the use of fixed models results in modeling errors and consequent degradation in control performance. To overcome this limitation, this study proposed a head-tracking ARNC (HARNC) framework that uses neural networks (NNs) to update secondary path estimates and observation filters in real time based on the listener’s head position. In addition, a prefilter-based initialization scheme was introduced to accelerate the convergence of the control filter after head movements. NN models for estimating secondary paths and observation filters were trained using a dataset measured at multiple listener head positions and integrated into a virtual sensing ARNC algorithm. The proposed HARNC framework was validated through simulations and experiments, including a comparative assessment of prefilter initialization and path update strategies. Simulation results evaluated over 30–500 Hz showed that compared with conventional ARNC using fixed paths, the proposed HARNC achieved an additional noise reduction of 3.02 dBA on average. It was also compared with look-up table and interpolation-based updating strategies and outperformed them in terms of path estimation accuracy and noise attenuation in ARNC simulations. The framework was further validated through real-vehicle experiments, confirming its effectiveness in achieving robust ARNC performance under realistic driving conditions.

title: Unsupervised deep learning framework for damage identification under ambient excitations: trait of damage localization and demonstrative applications
abstract: Developing unsupervised deep learning-based damage identification (uDLdi) under ambient excitations is crucial for civil engineering but remains hindered by insufficient feature extraction from complex original acceleration responses and a lack of damage localization capabilities. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel framework of uDLdi under ambient excitation (F-uDLdi-ae) by adopting the following innovative techniques: (1) a cube-shaped sample set is constructed to theoretically protrude damage information while suppressing interference information; (2) a self-attention module dedicated to protruding damage feature so as to largely identify damage samples is constructed; and (3) an uncertainty-weakened damage probability strategy for localizing damage accurately and reliably is proposed. Validation using a numerical steel truss bridge and a laboratory three-story frame structure demonstrates the superior damage discrimination and localization performance of the proposed framework. Specifically, in the numerical case under a high-noise environment (SNR = 5 dB), F-uDLdi-ae achieves an F‑score of 91.98%, outperforming several advanced unsupervised methods by 6.27% to 20.65%. In the three-story frame structure, F-uDLdi-ae achieves an F‑score of 100%. Furthermore, the framework is applied to a long‑span cable‑stayed bridge, Yonghe Bridge, where it achieves an F‑score of 99.17% and successfully localizes the damage via the maximum damage probability. The proposed F-uDLdi-ae overcomes the limitations of existing uDLdi, holding the promise for viably and intelligently identifying damage in practical engineering structures.

title: A novel parallel feature fusion strategy-based machine learning approach for accurate prediction and early warning of wind-induced vibrations of solar towers
abstract: Solar towers are highly flexible structures prone to wind-induced vibrations, which can significantly reduce the operational efficiency of concentrated solar power (CSP) plants and, more critically, may jeopardize the structural integrity. With the growing maturity of structural health monitoring (SHM) technologies and the increasing availability of multi-source sensing data, data-driven prediction has emerged as a key method for real-time evaluation and early warning of wind-induced vibrations. However, conventional machine learning models often exhibit some randomness in their predictions and struggle to accurately predict wind-induced vibration responses arising from strong fluid–structure coupling, which is particularly pronounced in solar towers. In addition, these models typically require extensive hyperparameter tuning, leading to high computational cost and reduced prediction efficiency. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel data-driven prediction method based on a parallel feature fusion strategy. The model integrates Long Short-Term Memory Network(LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit(GRU), and improved Transformer within a dual-branch architecture, leveraging gated mechanisms and multi-head attention for multi-scale feature extraction. Then, an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM)-based hierarchical feature fusion module is designed to achieve efficient integration of multi-source features from both branches. The proposed approach is validated through wind tunnel experiments on a scaled aeroelastic model and tested against field measurements from a full-scale operational tower. Finally, an early warning system based on the model is developed and shown to be reliable for real-world wind hazard mitigation in CSP plants.

title: A two-stage approach for predicting tribological variables via latent-regularized blind denoising and machine learning in microscratch testing
abstract: The development of predictive models in tribology has emerged as a tool for predicting key process variables. Penetration, tangential force, volume removed, coefficient of friction, and specific energy are critical parameters for minimizing energy consumption and reducing losses due to friction and wear. This work proposes a two-stage methodology that integrates signal denoising and predictive modeling. In the first stage, a recurrent autoencoder with contrastive learning and temporal smoothness constraints is employed to enhance the quality of force and position signals in a blind, unsupervised manner. In the second stage, a Random Forest (RF) model estimates tribological variables while integrating mechanical properties of the materials to improve generalization. The methodology was validated through microscratch tests performed on four steels (AISI 303, 304, 310, and H13) under normal loads between 40 and 100 mN, enabling analysis of material-dependent tribological responses at the microscale. Compared to conventional filters (Savitzky–Golay, moving average) and data-driven baselines (EMD, DAE), the proposed latent-regularized blind denoising autoencoder (LR-BDAE) achieved the highest signal preservation, with mean SNR improvements of 18.5dB and Pearson correlation exceeding 0.93 across materials. When integrated into the predictive stage, this denoising enhanced model consistency and reduced mean squared error by up to 42.3% for tangential force, 36.6% for penetration, 25.2% for the friction coefficient, and 20.8% for removed volume, with a minimum gain of 5.1% for specific energy. Incorporating material properties further increased R2 for specific energy by 26.2%, demonstrating robustness across distinct steels and supporting the general applicability of the framework to other tribological systems with noisy multi-sensor data. This proposal represents a step forward in integrating signal processing and machine learning techniques for tribological systems, providing a physically interpretable and scalable framework for industrial applications.

title: Analysis, optimization, and feature reduction in neural network models for quasi-static prediction in systems exhibiting Bouc-Wen hysteresis
abstract: This article addresses quasi-static torque prediction in systems with Bouc–Wen hysteresis, illustrated using a Vacuum Packed Particles Torsional Damper (VPPTD). A modified Bouc–Wen model (augmented with additional dry-friction and nonlinear stiffness components) was employed, with its parameters generalized as functions of chamber vacuum. The study was conducted on a dataset containing n=399,200 samples generated for multiple vacuum and material configurations. Five neural network architectures were compared, including a single-output model and multi-output variants predicting intermediate Bouc–Wen variables before estimating the torque M. Two input-reduction strategies were investigated: (S1) only physical parameters of the model, and (S2) a minimal control set (p,ABS) extended with selected intermediate signals. Feature selection was based on repeated-measures correlation (rmcorr), block-permutation clustering, and SHAP analysis; hyperparameter tuning was performed with Hyperopt. The highest accuracy was obtained for S2: the multi-output architecture with skip-connections achieved MAE(M)=0.043Nm (≈0.18%σM) for the full set of intermediates (INVI), while with only four inputs {φ,sign(φ̇),p,ABS} (INIVb) it maintained MAE(M)=0.051Nm (≈0.21%σM). Excluding dynamic signals (S1) increased the error to 0.38–0.61Nm (≈1.6–2.5%σM). Robustness tests (Gaussian noise, sign reversal of sign(φ̇), feature occlusion, repeated data splits) confirmed the greater stability of configuration INVI and the key role of φ and the correct sign of φ̇. A comparison with classical regressors (kNN, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting) indicated that although sometimes competitive under noise, they failed to provide consistent estimation of intermediate variables. The recommended solution is a multi-output architecture with skip-connections; in applications with limited sensor availability, a four-input configuration can be employed, with a conscious trade-off in robustness.

title: A rotating stall warning method for a contra-rotating compressor based on deep learning with automatic hyperparameter optimization
abstract: The dynamic pressure signals during the rotating stall process of a compressor exhibit pronounced nonlinearity and non-stationarity. In addition, the small amplitude of pre-stall disturbances makes early stall identification and warning a challenging signal-processing problem. Moreover, the hyperparameters of conventional neural network models rely on manual, experience-based tuning, which limits their prediction accuracy and robustness under complex operating conditions. To address these issues, this study proposes a rotating stall early warning method based on a convolutional neural network combined with a long short-term memory network (CNN-LSTM) with automatic hyperparameter optimization. A low-speed axial flow contra-rotating compressor is selected as the test object. Stall experiments are conducted under different inlet and rotational speed configurations. Dynamic pressure time series data are acquired using sensor arrays mounted at the blade tip of the front and rear rotors. After preprocessing, including filtering, normalization, and resampling, a dataset is constructed for neural network training and validation. The Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO) algorithm is introduced to globally optimize key hyperparameters of the CNN-LSTM network. And the optimal NGO-CNN-LSTM model is then applied to predict dynamic pressure stall time series data. The results show that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves higher prediction accuracy than the conventional CNN-LSTM model. Furthermore, a kernel density estimation (KDE) method is employed to adaptively determine stall warning thresholds for different operating conditions. Under uniform inlet conditions, the NGO-CNN-LSTM model achieves a stall warning lead time exceeding 10 s for most speed configurations and improves the poor warning performance of the CNN-LSTM model under some speed conditions. Under inlet distortion conditions, the proposed model still provides a stable stall warning time of no less than 7 s. Comparison between the predicted data and the original measurements indicates that the NGO-CNN-LSTM model can identify smaller amplitude pre-stall disturbances with clear physical significance at an earlier stage. Its predictions show higher consistency with the original data, leading to more reliable stall warning results.

title: Data-driven predictive model and uncertainty analysis of vehicle-induced vibrations based on experimental measurements
abstract: Rapid urbanization has increased building construction near railway tracks, where ground vibrations induced by trains can damage structures and cause occupant discomfort, including headaches, nausea, and sleep disturbances. A number of different vibration comfort indicators were proposed for the assessment purposes, including the root mean square (RMS), vibration dose value (VDV), and maximum transient vibration value (MTVV). In order to better evaluate them, a multi-output chained gradient boosting model (MOC-GBM) is proposed in this paper, which adopts a strategy of integrating target variables into the input dataset and continuously updating the inputs during the predictions. Five locations across northern Poland were selected, and buildings with timber, steel, and reinforced concrete (RC) structural systems were investigated to compile a comprehensive dataset. They were used to evaluate the capability of MOC-GBM model. Then, two different locations were used to measure a new unseen dataset for general assessment of those predictive models. In the individual dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model obtained accuracies of 98.2%, 99.2%, and 92.7% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively. In addition, in mean value dataset, the proposed MOC-GBM model demonstrated very good predictive performance across all vibration comfort indicators with the accuracies of 99.4%, 99.7%, and 99.5% for predicting RMS, VDV, and MTVV, respectively, as well as the best fitted curve and promising results for curve fitting.

title: Adaptive wavelet-enhanced data-driven framework for surface quality prediction in ultra-precision manufacturing
abstract: Real-time surface roughness prediction is pivotal for enabling autonomous quality control in ultra-precision manufacturing, bridging the gap between process dynamics and product quality. However, the inherent non-stationarity of multi-source signals and harsh industrial noise pose significant challenges for existing predictive models. To address these limitations, this study presents a novel end-to-end data-driven framework that integrates differentiable parameterized Morlet wavelet encoding with deep spatiotemporal learning. Unlike traditional methods with fixed parameters, the proposed framework enables the adaptive learning of wavelet center frequency and scale via backpropagation, thereby providing a task-adaptive time–frequency representation for noisy sensor data. Validated on an ultra-precision lathe, the method achieves superior predictive performance with a coefficient of determination of 0.9715. Crucially, the framework demonstrates an ultra-low inference latency of 3.34 ms per sample, meeting the stringent real-time requirements of in-process monitoring on the investigated platform. This work provides an effective and computationally efficient framework for intelligent quality characterization under the investigated ultra-precision machining conditions, and offers a methodological basis for future validation in more complex manufacturing environments.

title: Adaptive neural network control for ship-to-ship crane systems with dead-zone nonlinearity and actuator saturation
abstract: Ship-to-ship crane system plays a crucial role in offshore material transfer in modern maritime engineering. As a typical underactuated nonlinear system, the ship-to-ship crane system is subject to multiple challenges, including hull-coupling disturbances induced by ocean waves, parameter uncertainties, actuator dead-zone nonlinearity, and saturation constraints, all of which severely degrade positioning accuracy and swing suppression performance. To address these issues, an adaptive neural network control strategy is proposed in this paper. A smooth approximation function is employed to model actuator saturation, thereby avoiding potential instability and simplifying the controller design. A radial basis function neural network is applied to approximate the unknown nonlinear dynamics arising from system uncertainties and external disturbances, while an adaptive law is developed to compensate for the approximation errors and unknown parameters. By integrating the proposed adaptive mechanism, rapid swing elimination and accurate payload positioning are achieved simultaneously. Rigorous stability analysis based on Lyapunov theory and Barbalat’s lemma proves the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. Finally, experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed control scheme.

title: A self-supervised learning approach for intelligent surface roughness monitoring in thin-walled component machining
abstract: Surface roughness monitoring is essential for process quality control in intelligent manufacturing, yet reliable prediction in thin-walled component milling remains challenging because roughness labels are sparse and multi-channel vibration responses are spatially and dynamically heterogeneous. This study proposes a spatially aware self-supervised contrastive learning framework using six-channel spindle–worktable vibration signals. The task is formulated as sparse-label anchor-bag roughness regression: only the bag corresponding to the central small region in each large region is assigned a measured roughness label, whereas the remaining small-region bags are used as unlabeled data for representation learning. The framework integrates a multi-channel vibration encoder, a physics-guided gated bag aggregation module, and a spatially aware weighted InfoNCE objective. Bag-level self-supervised pretraining enables the model to learn transferable representations while reducing excessive separation between physically related neighboring bags; the pretrained encoder and aggregation module are then fine-tuned using only labeled anchor bags. Experiments on two thin-walled helical milling datasets, Ti2AlNb and GH4169D, demonstrate robust performance under sparse annotation and material variation using a workpiece-level evaluation protocol. The proposed method achieves R2 = 0.9431 ± 0.0337 and RMSE = 0.0274 ± 0.0145 μm on Ti2AlNb, and maintains strong performance on GH4169D with R2 = 0.9246 ± 0.0424, RMSE = 0.0171 ± 0.0093 μm. Comparative and ablation analyses support the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining, spatially aware contrastive learning, multi-channel fusion, and the anchor-bag supervision setting, providing a label-efficient route for surface quality monitoring in intelligent manufacturing.

title: Neural network assisted-augmented Kalman filter for joint input-state estimation
abstract: The augmented Kalman filter (AKF) is widely used for joint input-state estimation by augmenting the state vector with unknown inputs. However, its performance critically depends on the Gaussian white noise assumption and the proper selection of noise covariance matrices, making it sensitive to modeling errors in the state-space representation and hyperparameter tuning in practice. To address these challenges, this study proposes an AKF-inspired hybrid learned observer, termed AKFNet, for joint input-state estimation from sparse output-only measurements. Unlike the classical AKF, AKFNet no longer computes the Kalman gain analytically based on the minimum mean square error principle; instead, it is a hybrid data-driven and model-based algorithm that embeds a recurrent neural network (RNN) module into the AKF recursion and empirically learns the gain directly from measurements. The RNN module learns to map the information of real data within the state-space model to an effective Kalman gain, thereby improving the accuracy and robustness of joint input-state estimation in practical scenarios where model mismatches and complex noises are present. The proposed AKFNet is first validated on a numerical 9 DOF building for seismic input-state estimation, and compared with the classical AKF, dual Kalman filter (DKF) and an adaptive AKF with online covariance adjustment. Subsequently, an experimental shaker table test is conducted on a three-story frame to further validate its effectiveness. Finally, the AKFNet is used to estimate wind loads on a real-world large-span cable-stayed bridge using field data. In all tested scenarios, AKFNet provides competitive or improved accuracy, demonstrating its robustness and adaptive capability in the presence of modeling errors and non-white Gaussian noise.

title: Understanding biases in machine learning-based strain predictions for fighter aircraft
abstract: The use of machine learning models for strain prediction in aircraft structural health monitoring has shown a considerable interest in recent years. The confidence we can place in these models however depends on our ability to understand when and why they can make biased predictions, which is particularly important in critical applications. In fatigue monitoring, such biases may shift the mean stress level of the reconstructed signal and therefore affect fatigue damage estimation. In this context, our work investigates the origin of systematic prediction biases observed when estimating strains from standard flight parameters on a fighter aircraft. Similar biases were already mentioned in the literature, but no in-depth study was dedicated to their analysis. About a hundred flights of a Rafale fighter aircraft was used for this study. An amount of 20 input variables was also used for strain predictions, some of them representing environmental measures and other ones the flight controls. Our study identifies the source of bias in three steps. It first shows that the biases are not due to model-specific limitations, but rather to the data and/or physics-driven mechanism. We then combine explainability tools with aeronautical expertise, which shows that the trained models over-emphasize inertial variables, which govern high-frequency strains, while variables describing the flight environment have substantially weaker influence. Building on this insight, we finally decompose the measured strains into inertial components and environmental baselines. Each part is predicted separately using exclusively physically relevant variables. Interestingly, only the environmental baseline carries the systematic bias, while the inertial part is reconstructed accurately. These findings demonstrate that bias originate from the environmental contribution of the strain signal, with temperature effects emerging as a plausible root cause. The study thus provides a principled diagnostic framework for identifying and interpreting bias mechanisms in data-driven structural monitoring.

title: A noise-corrected data-driven approach for nonlinear dynamical system modeling in frequency domain
abstract: The development of parsimonious and accurate models is highly dependent on the quality of training data. To extract the underlying physical laws from noisy data, we introduce a noise-corrected data-driven approach. It begins by formulating a nonlinear sparse least-squares problem in the frequency domain, where noise correction terms and physical parameters are treated as unknowns. To solve this problem, we present a novel nested Levenberg-Marquardt (LM)-Sequential Thresholded Least-Squares (STLS) approach, which inherits the strengths of LM algorithm for solving nonlinear optimization problems and the sparsity-promoting capabilities of the STLS. This approach also offers a simple and intuitive way to incorporate prior physical knowledge into the sparsification process, preventing small coefficient terms from being pruned due to excessively large thresholds. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated by both numerical simulations and experimental tests. The results indicate its effectiveness in extracting underlying dynamic structures from measured data, which might be corrupted not only by white noise but also by distorted streaming.

title: A hybrid deep learning framework for reliable and interpretable remaining life estimation in turbofan Engines: Focusing on Robustness, Generalization, and Sensor-Level interpretability
abstract: Reliable prediction of Remaining Useful Life (RUL) is crucial for improving maintenance planning and operational safety in turbofan engines. This study proposes a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network–Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN–GRU) framework for prognostic analysis using the NASA C-MAPSS benchmark dataset. The CNN layers are employed to extract local degradation-related features from multivariate sensor measurements, while the GRU structure captures temporal degradation trends over long operational sequences. Beyond conventional accuracy-focused evaluations, the proposed framework emphasizes robustness, reproducibility, and interpretability through a reliability-oriented experimental strategy. Comparative analyses were conducted against standalone CNN and GRU models together with component-level ablation experiments and repeated training runs to assess statistical stability. In addition, SHAP and LIME methods were utilized to provide global and local explanations of model behavior and sensor importance. Experimental validation across FD001–FD004 subsets demonstrates that the hybrid CNN–GRU model achieves competitive prediction accuracy with improved consistency under varying operating conditions and fault scenarios. The explainability analysis further reveals strong dependence on degradation-sensitive thermodynamic sensor signals. Overall, the proposed framework offers an interpretable and reproducible deep learning approach for benchmark aero-engine RUL prediction while also acknowledging limitations related to real-world industrial deployment.

title: A data-driven digital twin update technology based on an invertible attention-enhanced conditional invertible neural network
abstract: The fidelity of a digital twin is maintained by continuously updating the models embedded in its virtual entity with real-time sensor data. Conditional invertible neural networks (cINNs) offer a promising data-driven approach for likelihood-free model updating. However, they struggle to capture strong couplings among model parameters and often fail to effectively use suboptimal or limited sensor measurements. Additionally, epistemic uncertainty cannot be rigorously quantified in standard cINNs. To address these issues, an invertible attention-enhanced cINN (IA-cINN) is proposed. A novel invertible attention layer is integrated into the architecture. This layer explicitly models intrinsic correlations among model parameters and cross-dependencies between parameters and measurements through self- and cross-attention mechanisms while rigorously preserving invertibility. Monte Carlo dropout is incorporated into the IA-cINN to quantify epistemic uncertainty. The method was validated on two engineering cases. In a simulated case of a material handling device, three material parameters of structural components were updated using only strain and deformation measurements. In an experimental bearing case, contact stiffness, defect length, and radial clearance were updated using vibration features. In both cases, the IA-cINN outperformed the conventional cINN, as well as a Bayesian updating method based on Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. The IA-cINN achieved significantly higher updating accuracy, especially for parameters that exhibited complex coupling relationships with others. It produced more reliable uncertainty intervals in both cases, as indicated by lower interval scores. These intervals were shown to be sensitive to key sources of epistemic uncertainty, including data scarcity and insufficient model learning.

title: Continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking performance degradation of expansion joints in long-span bridges
abstract: The neural network models driven by long-term monitoring data of structural temperature and thermal displacement in expansion joints are commonly employed to understand the operational condition of expansion joints in long-span bridges. But the continuous performance deterioration of expansion joints during the long-term operational period would change the temperature-displacement relationship and reduce the reliability of the corresponding neural network model. This paper presents a continuously updatable temperature-displacement hybrid neural network model for tracking the time-dependent performance degradation of expansion joints. First, a multi-domain feature fusion model fusing time-domain, difference-domain and spatial-domain features of long-term monitoring data is proposed by integrating a bidirectional long-short term memory network, an encoder-decoder, and a graph convolutional network to describe the complicated temperature-displacement relationship of expansion joints. Then, a model update method based on residual guidance and knowledge distillation was developed to continuously update the multi-domain feature fusion model so that the model could adapt to the degraded condition of expansion joints. Finally, long-term monitoring data from a long-span cable-stayed bridge is adopted as a case study to examine the accuracy of the proposed multi-domain feature fusion model and the effectiveness of the developed model updating method. The results indicate that the multi-domain feature fusion model has the capability of accurately capturing the historical temperature-displacement relationship embedded in expansion joints. The model updating method enables efficient and continuous updating of the temperature-displacement neural network, and the updated model can accurately track the performance degradation of expansion joints.

title: A kriging-based data-driven approach for localization of simultaneous impacts in composites
abstract: Detection of simultaneous low-velocity impacts in composite structures involve fundamental challenge as the uniqueness of time-difference-of-arrival (TDoA) features is compromised by guided wave superposition. This challenge becomes significantly more pronounced in the presence of simultaneous multiple impacts. We propose an artificial neural network (ANN)-based framework for both single and multiple impact localization on laminated composite plates employing TDoA features enhanced through singular value decomposition (SVD) for mitigating indeterminacy of source due to wavefield superposition. The effectiveness of the proposed methodology in localizing single and simultaneous impacts without explicit signal separation and densification of sensors has been demonstrated. The ANN trained solely on finite-element simulation data has been shown be robust enough when tested on unseen numerical and experimental datasets, including unequal energy levels and time delays between impacts. The robustness is further enhanced through a kriging-based post-processing correction without retraining. For dual impacts, the proposed framework exhibits 90% probability-of-detection between 24.01and 38.65 mm.

title: A deep reinforcement learning method applied to remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: As an important component of mechanical equipment, the health status of rolling bearings directly affects the reliability and safety of the equipment. Due to the harsh working environment of rolling bearings and the difficulty in identifying the early degradation trends, the accuracy of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is significantly challenged. To address these issues, this paper proposes a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) prediction model based on the deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm, which reconfigures the RUL prediction task as a sequential decision-making problem under Markov Decision Process (MDP) framework in a continuous action space. The DDPG algorithm can effectively capture the temporal dependencies among original data. By combining the feature extraction capabilities of residual networks (ResNet) and the time series modeling capabilities of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, high-precision RUL prediction is achieved. Firstly, a reinforcement learning (RL) agent based on ResNet-LSTM is constructed to extract deep degradation features from the original data. Subsequently, by designing appropriate reward functions and action spaces, the agent learns to map the current operating state of the rolling bearing to its RUL under the guidance of the DDPG algorithm through repeated trials and optimization. The proposed model was validated on two open-source datasets and a private dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves lower root mean square error (RMSE) and more stable degradation trend prediction compared with other approaches.

title: Power Bond graph-embedded causal flow-aware graph neural network for fault localization of electro-hydraulic systems
abstract: To achieve precise fault localization for electro-hydraulic systems of mechanical, a Causal Flow-aware Graph Neural Network (CFAGNN) is proposed, which integrates power bond graph topology with deep learning. A power bond graph model is constructed to characterize energy transfer mechanisms and clarify dynamic coupling relationships among subsystems, providing quantifiable physical constraints and edge-node attributes. To accommodate real-time operating conditions, learnable edge attributes are constructed with embedded dynamic correction parameters. These physical priors are embedded into the Causal Flow Attention (CFA) mechanism, where physical regularization and causal direction loss are utilized to constrain attention coefficients to conform to energy transfer laws, thereby enabling accurate tracking of fault propagation paths. Validation on a real engineering machinery dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art models. The results indicate that CFAGNN balances diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency effectively, providing a reliable solution for the fault diagnosis of complex electro-hydraulic systems.

title: Adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling for reliability analysis of nonlinear dynamic systems
abstract: Reliability analysis of nonlinear inelastic dynamic systems under uncertainty remains a critical challenge, owing to the path-dependent, high-dimensional nature of the problem. To this end, this paper proposes an adaptive and uncertainty-aware surrogate modeling framework comprising three synergistic components. The first component is the aLSTM–SNGP surrogate model, an uncertainty-aware surrogate for nonlinear dynamic systems that integrates an attention-enhanced LSTM (aLSTM) encoder with a Spectral-normalized Neural Gaussian Process (SNGP) predictor, jointly optimized through end-to-end co-training. The aLSTM encoder processes excitation sequences and system parameters together, capturing temporal dependencies while implicitly reducing dimensionality; the SNGP predictor provides scalable uncertainty-aware prediction through random Fourier feature approximation. The second component develops two surrogate-based failure probability estimation methods: Method I (aLSTM-SNGP-MCS) based on direct Monte Carlo simulation, and Method II (aLSTM-SNGP-IS) based on importance sampling with an adaptively constructed proposal density that concentrates sampling effort in failure-prone regions. The third component is an adaptive exploration–exploitation refinement strategy that iteratively refines the surrogate model by combining active learning with an alternating training scheme of full training and local fine-tuning. The framework is validated under stochastic seismic excitations through two examples: a numerical example based on a six-story nonlinear inelastic shear building model with Bouc-Wen hysteresis, and a practical engineering example based on a nine-story SAC steel frame represented by a nonlinear finite element model. Results demonstrate that both methods yield accurate failure probability estimates while significantly reducing the number of evaluations to the simulation model relative to crude Monte Carlo simulation, with Method II outperforming Method I.

title: Sensitivity-driven model updating for bridge structures using operational modal analysis and enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a robust and effective finite element model updating (FEMU) framework for inverse parameter identification of bridge structures by integrating operational modal analysis (OMA) and variance-based global sensitivity analysis (GSA) with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling-based Bayesian optimization (ETS-BO) method. Specifically, a Gaussian process (GP) model is constructed to approximate the nonlinear relationship between uncertain structural parameters and the corresponding modal responses. Leveraging the trained GP model, the variance-based GSA identifies the most influential parameters governing the dynamic behavior of the bridge, thereby significantly reducing the dimensionality of the FEMU problem and improving computational efficiency. Building upon the reduced parameter space, the ETS-BO method is developed by integrating an adaptive trust-region selection strategy with an enhanced batched Thompson sampling (ETS) method to efficiently solve the FEMU problem. The adaptive trust-region selection evaluates the improvement potential at the regional level, guiding the search toward promising regions of the parameter space while avoiding over-exploration of less promising ones. The trust region method is then applied to perform local optimization, whereby each trust region is adaptively expanded or contracted based on its observed improvement history, and local optimization runs exhibiting greater potential for further improvement are selectively continued. Within the selected trust regions, the ETS method is employed to determine the optimal updating parameters by iteratively selecting batches of candidate solutions sampled from the posterior distributions of the corresponding independent GP models. The effectiveness of the proposed ETS-BO is validated through a real-world case study of a bridge structure equipped with wireless accelerometers for vibration monitoring. Ambient vibration responses recorded under normal traffic conditions are analyzed using OMA to identify modal parameters, which subsequently serve as targets for updating the finite element (FE) model developed to represent the structural behavior of the bridge. The results demonstrate that the proposed ETS-BO requires substantially fewer FE evaluations than conventional optimization methods while achieving rapid convergence toward the optimal solution. Furthermore, the updated FE model closely reproduces the experimentally identified modal parameters, including natural frequencies and mode shape correlations, thereby providing a reliable numerical representation of the in-service dynamic behavior of the bridge and demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework to support long-term structural health monitoring of large-scale civil infrastructure systems.

title: Complex-amplitude design of dynamic acoustic holography via physics-assisted neural network
abstract: Acoustic holography promises diverse applications, including high-resolution imaging, water–air communication, and in-vivo tissue/organ printing. While complex-amplitude design of acoustic holography yields superior performance in resolution and information content for sophisticated acoustic fields, but most holograms are spatially and temporally static once fabricated. This dilemma may be addressed by introducing the incident wavefront modulation as an additional degree of freedom, and dynamic holography would be realized by tuning the incident wavefronts via electrically switching a transducer array. Here, we propose a physics-assisted neural network optimization framework for the complex-amplitude design of dynamic acoustic holography, which enables joint optimization of multiple incident amplitude and phase profile. The framework embeds an angular-spectrum propagation model into neural network and introduces amplitude-binarization regularization to enable dynamic control through an electrically switched partitioned transducer. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibits remarkable versatility, supporting the phase modulations in either continuous or binary manner and even cascaded configuration. As a proof-of-concept demonstration, it successfully achieves the dynamic display of three-frame animations and 26 alphabetic letters, creating compelling “acoustic movies”. Quantitatively, the proposed method outperforms traditional designs both numerically and experimentally, which reduces mean squared error by 24.1% and 32.1%, respectively. We believe this work would greatly advance acoustic holography and imply unprecedented opportunity for broad acoustics.

title: Simulation of near-fault strong ground motion with generative adversarial network
abstract: This paper proposes a generative adversarial network (GAN) for feature extraction and simulation generation of seismic data. Specifically, a Wasserstein-distance-based GAN model has been adopted using the well-acknowledged NGA-West2 ground motion American database of the Pacific Earthquake Engineering Research Center (PEER). Notably, this study adopts multi-dimensional convolution/deconvolution to extract and reconstruct multi-dimensional features from one-dimensional data, ensuring the generated data exhibit required features simultaneously. The validity and diversity of the generated data are verified by four aspects, such as time–frequency power spectrum, data similarity, and seismic intensity parameter distribution map. The results show that the generated data by the proposed method have good and diverse features and waveforms.

title: Computer vision-based cross-scale structural displacement estimation using amplitude-phase fusion
abstract: Accurate and robust structural displacement monitoring is essential for the safety assessment and maintenance of civil infrastructure. While phase-based vision methods offer sub-pixel precision, their applicability is severely limited by phase wrapping under large inter-frame motions. This issue hinders reliable monitoring in real-world scenarios where large pseudo-static displacements and small vibrations coexist. To address this limitation, this study proposes a cross-scale displacement estimation technique that fuses amplitude and phase information from vision measurements. The technique employs a two-stage estimation framework: amplitude-based pixel-level coarse alignment, followed by phase-based sub-pixel refinement. To ensure robustness and accuracy across varying structural responses, three key strategies are introduced: (1) a correlation-based active pixel selection algorithm to extract structurally meaningful regions, (2) a pyramid level optimization algorithm based on inter-scale phase linearity, and (3) a self-calibration algorithm using synthetic image sequences to determine the phase-to-pixel scale. The effectiveness of the proposed technique was validated through experimental testing on a single-story building model and a footbridge under multiple excitation scenarios. The results indicate that the proposed technique is capable of achieving high-precision displacement estimation, with root mean square errors maintained below 0.2 mm even for displacement amplitudes reaching up to 50 mm.

title: Knowledge-driven compound fault detection enhancement based on multi-modal feature generative adversarial collaborative learning for industrial rotating machinery
abstract: Compound faults of industrial rotating machinery are characterized by temporal-frequency multisource signals coupling, existing methods struggle to cope with the intrinsic correlations and distribution gap between the temporal signal and the frequency signal, leading to suboptimal detection performance. To tackle it, we proposed a multi-modal feature collaborative generative adversarial learning method for industrial rotating machinery compound fault detection enhancement. In this method, the feature representations of inter-modal complementarity (modal-shared) and the intra-modal specificity (modal-specific) are collaboratively learnt. First, we design two parallel knowledge-informed modal-specific feature extraction network models and a multi-modal transfer model. Two modal-specific feature extraction models utilize the prior knowledge to learn modal-specific feature from the temporal and frequency modals. The multi-modal transfer model aggregates and transfer modal-shared feature by calculating modal-specific feature neighbors of each modal. Then, a generative adversarial-based multi-modal collaborative training strategy is developed for feature collaborative learning. In this strategy, three feature learning models acts as multi-modal feature generator, which intends to generate and fuse modal-specific and modal shared features to form the cross-modal propagated feature, and a feature modal discriminator is introduced to identify the source belonging modal of the cross-modal propagated feature. Based on such feature generative adversarial training, the cross-modal propagated feature no longer clearly belongs to one certain modal, thus achieving effective multi-modal feature transfer. Finally, two industrial rotating machineries cases demonstrate the compound fault performance of the proposed method.

title: Zero-shot bearing life state identification method based on multi-scale envelope entropy and contrastive generative Kolmogorov-Arnold network
abstract: Rolling bearings exhibit diverse failure modes, and obtaining fully annotated data for all failure modes in industrial scenarios is challenging, which limits the applicability of traditional diagnostic models. To address this issue, a zero-shot life-cycle state identification method is proposed. First, a Multi-Scale Envelope Entropy (MSEE) health indicator is constructed by integrating frequency-domain and time-domain features, enabling sensitive monitoring and division of degradation states. Second, a Contrastive Generative Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CGKAN) model is proposed. This network utilizes B-spline functions to accurately fit local transient features, combined with radial basis functions to capture global patterns, allowing it to learn feature distributions from data of known failure modes. Additionally, Wasserstein distance and a gradient penalty mechanism are incorporated with contrastive learning to optimize the feature space, generating high-quality sample features for unknown failure modes and training a classifier to identify these unseen failure modes. The proposed method is validated on two full-life-cycle bearing datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that the method effectively divides life-cycle states and, by leveraging data from known failure modes, achieves accurate identification of unknown failure modes not encountered during the training phase.

title: A Conditional constraint Generative adversarial networks model for predicting high cycle and very high cycle fatigue life of titanium alloy
abstract: Fatigue life prediction of aero-engine has been an important research topic in the aerospace industry. This study focuses on predicting the high cycle and very high cycle fatigue (HCF/VHCF) life of aero-engine titanium alloys under small-sample conditions. First, based on the test results and empirical phenomena, a dimensionless constraint index (δ) was designed to assign values to the test type (Typ) and fracture conditions (Fc), and life mapping characteristic variables were introduced to establish a foundation for subsequent data augmentation and predictive modeling. Second, a Kernel density estimation-Synthetic minority over-sampling technique (KDE-SMOTE) data enhancement method is proposed, which expands the dataset while preserving feature-variable correlations. Then, a Conditional constraint Generative adversarial network (C-cGAN) model was built by embedding δ and Fc computation as explicit constraints in the loss and implicitly guiding attention learning with adversarial training. Finally, under the conditions of high-density distribution test validation (Test set 1) and random test validation (Test set 2), the C-cGAN model shows better prediction results at 3–5-fold dispersion bands (satisfying 5-fold dispersion band) by training on KDE-SMOTE enhanced data, and extends to the fatigue life prediction studies of a variety of titanium alloys, which suggests that the model has a potential reference value.
keywords: High cycle and very high cycle fatigue (HCF/VHCF)

title: Motion acceleration reconstruction of projectiles under launch conditions using generative adversarial networks
abstract: Accurate measurement of in-bore projectile acceleration is critical for optimizing artillery launch systems and evaluating interior ballistic performance. However, signals from projectile-borne storage tests are severely corrupted by high-frequency bore collision noise, masking low-frequency motion features and hindering accurate identification of projectile dynamics. Conventional denoising methods, which rely on cumbersome manual parameter tuning, prove ineffective against such stochastic high-amplitude coupled noise. This study proposes a physics-constrained generative adversarial network (GAN) that integrates physical priors with adversarial training. The method leverages the intrinsic physical mapping between projectile base pressure and in-bore acceleration, including synchronized time-domain peaks, consistent temporal trends, and shared underlying combustion and motion physics, to guide the denoising process. Specifically, the normalized base pressure signal serves as a conditional input to the discriminator, which evaluates the denoised acceleration produced by the generator. Physics-based constraints regulate the acceleration generation scale, enabling synergistic noise suppression and signal preservation while reducing reliance on extensive pristine training data. Simulations across ten noise levels demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms traditional techniques such as discrete wavelet transform and empirical mode decomposition, particularly in high-amplitude noise suppression. Three independent live-fire tests confirm its robustness and generalization capability, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of up to 40 dB for the denoised in-bore acceleration. This work establishes a new paradigm for denoising dynamic signals in extreme launch environments, greatly enhancing the efficiency of ballistic testing and the accuracy of artillery performance assessment.

title: Generative adversarial networks for high frequency ultrasonic field modelling near fluid-solid interfaces
abstract: The propagation of high frequency ultrasonic waves enables the detection of fine inclusions and cracks in solid media, often induced by fatigue or impact loads. Accurate modelling of high frequency wavefields significantly enhances the ability of structural health monitoring systems to detect fatigue cracks and localize stress concentrations near defects within solid plates. Numerical solvers, such as the Finite Element Method (FEM), require fine meshing of the problem geometry, whereas semi-analytical modelling, such as the Distributed Point Source Method (DPSM), demand large number of distributed point sources to accurately model high frequency ultrasonic fields, resulting in significant computational overhead. However, such computational constraints limit their applicability in real-time or large-scale monitoring systems. To address these challenges, we propose a surrogate model for expensive numerical solvers (FEM/DPSM) to efficiently predict high frequency ultrasonic wavefields in isotropic solids coupled with a fluid medium. A conditional generative adversarial network (cGANs), based on the Pix2Pix architecture, which features a U-Net as a generator and a PatchGAN as a discriminator is employed for training. Multiple tailored loss functions, including frequency, edge, perceptual, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM) based losses are included within total generator loss to ensure physical accuracy and structural fidelity. The Pix2Pix model is trained on paired low- and high-frequency wavefield data encompassing both healthy and damaged configurations with a circular hole in the solid half-space. For both cases, the trained model demonstrates excellent predictive performance for generating high frequency wavefield, with SSIM values for displacement and normal stresses consistently exceeding 0.85.

title: Generative digital twin: A Sparse-xLSTM based self-evolution hybrid modeling approach for complex equipment
