abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into digital twins (DTs) offers transformative potential for characterizing the non-linear dynamics of complex equipment. However, realizing high-fidelity, self-evolution generative DTs remains challenging due to the computational prohibitiveness of Transformer based architectures and the insufficient long-term memory of traditional recurrent networks. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel generative digital twin (GDT) method driven by a Physics-Guided Sparse-xLSTM. First, we construct a Sparse-xLSTM architecture designed to model high-dimensional temporal dynamics efficiently. By leveraging exponential gating and matrix memory, this architecture achieves linear computational complexity while effectively capturing long-range dependencies, overcoming the quadratic bottleneck of conventional attention mechanisms. A sparse attention strategy is further incorporated to extract distinct state features from noisy sensor data, enhancing representation robustness. Second, to ensure physical consistency and generalization, a hybrid modeling mechanism is devised. Physical priors are embedded as input feature, and governing equations are integrated into the optimization objective as physical constraints, effectively confining the generative solution space to physically valid trajectories and mitigating model hallucinations. Third, addressing the imperative for continuous adaptation, a low-rank adaptation (LoRA)-based self-evolution engine is developed. This mechanism enables the GDT to perform online updates using limited streaming data by fine-tuning low-rank matrices, ensuring rapid synchronization with the time-varying states of the physical entity without catastrophic forgetting. Experimental validation on CNC machine tool wear datasets demonstrates that the proposed approach significantly outperforms advanced baselines in both prediction accuracy and adaptation efficiency, providing a robust paradigm for intelligent predictive maintenance of complex equipment.

title: Data-informed simulation of temperature effects in finite element models for structural health monitoring using inverse surrogate modeling
abstract: This work presents a data-informed framework to simulate temperature effects in a finite element model (FEM) for structural health monitoring (SHM), enabling realistic generation of synthetic modal data for both healthy and damaged states. A challenge in vibration-based SHM is that real damaged data are rarely available, so damage detection and classification methods are often validated using FEM simulations. However, temperature strongly affects modal data through changes in stiffness, connections, and boundary conditions, and these effects are difficult to reproduce realistically using standard thermo-mechanical assumptions, especially when only few temperature measurements are available. The proposed approach combines field monitoring data with an updated FEM through inverse surrogate modeling. First, an inverse surrogate model is trained on FEM simulations to recover temperature-sensitive mechanical parameters (e.g., Young’s modulus of elasticity) from modal frequencies. Then, this surrogate is applied to long-term monitoring data to estimate how these parameters evolve with temperature. A second regression model then learns a direct mapping from temperature to FEM parameters. Injecting these temperature-dependent parameters into the FEM allows simulation of realistic temperature-frequency trends, for both healthy and damage scenarios. The method is demonstrated on a numerical truss and on the KW51 railway bridge. Results show high accuracy in modal frequency prediction and consistent anomaly detection performance, indicating that the framework reproduces in-situ thermal effects without requiring explicit thermo-mechanical modeling, while preserving damage detectability under temperature variations.

title: Research on generative diffusion-based over-threshold restoration for oil and gas pipeline signals
abstract: Oil and gas pipeline detection signals are critical for pipeline defect diagnosis and assessment. However, during field signal acquisition, complex operating conditions, harsh detection environments, and inherent limitations of detector response and signal conversion may lead to over-threshold distortion in pipeline signals. Since the true complete defect distribution of field distorted signals is inaccessible, traditional supervised deep learning methods face limitations in constructing paired distorted-clean training samples. To address this problem, this study proposes an Over-Threshold Distortion Restoration (OTDR) method based on the diffusion probabilistic principle. OTDR adopts unsupervised forward diffusion training to learn the feature distribution of normal pipeline defect signals and incorporates a progressively guided restoration mode with a dynamic resampling mechanism to reconstruct over-threshold distorted regions during reverse diffusion. Case validations indicate that OTDR can reconstruct the main morphological structures, local details, and statistical feature distributions of field distorted signals. In the quantitative tests based on simulated distortion conditions, the restoration results achieve an average MAE of 0.045. The effects of different resampling strategies, prediction models, and diffusion strategies on restoration performance are further analyzed, and failure-case analysis is conducted under constructed extreme distortion conditions. Overall, the experimental results suggest that OTDR provides a feasible generative diffusion restoration mode for over-threshold distorted signals in oil and gas pipeline detection.

title: SFDM: Structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring utilizing computer vision-enhanced targetless monitoring system
abstract: Full-field dynamic displacement monitoring with high spatial resolution provides a more comprehensive representation of the dynamic characteristics of bridge structures, thereby significantly enhancing the effectiveness of bridge structural health monitoring (BSHM). In this study, a structural full-field dynamic displacement monitoring (SFDM) method is proposed to overcome the limitations of traditional discrete-point measurement techniques. To achieve targetless and accurate extraction of the lower edge of bridge structures, an effective computer vision framework is developed by integrating a robust fusion image processing (RFIP) strategy with a row-wise adaptive edge detection (RAED) approach. Additionally, a multi-target displacement transformation model (MDTM) is proposed to convert subpixel-level image displacements into physical displacements. A tied-arch bridge field test was conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The experimental results indicate that the proposed SFDM achieved correlation coefficients higher than 0.964, while the corresponding RMSE and NRMSE remained below 0.282 mm and 9.178% across all test cases, respectively, thereby confirming its accuracy and effectiveness for full-field displacement monitoring in BSHM applications.

title: CNSAO: A complex number space anomaly observer with multi-task masked LLM autoencoder for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speeds
abstract: Health monitoring of bearings under time-varying speed conditions remains a critical challenge in industrial applications. The speed fluctuations may disrupt the phase consistency of fault-related characteristics and lead to the dispersion of fault energy. This makes it difficult to capture stable fault modes for health monitoring in the dynamic scenario. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a complex number space-based anomaly observer (CNSAO) for bearing health monitoring under time-varying speed conditions. Firstly, a multi-task autoencoder (AE) is constructed to perform signal reconstruction and rotational speed prediction. Secondly, a pre-trained large language model-based AE (LLMAE) is used as the backbone for feature extraction and noise reduction. Moreover, a residual connection is applied to LLMAE to enhance information propagation. Thirdly, a complex number space health index (CHI) is constructed to quantify bearing health degradation from both amplitude and phase similarity perspectives, which can sensitively capture phase asynchrony caused by continuous speed variations. In order to verify the effectiveness of CNSAO, three bearing health monitoring tests are performed. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed CNSAO can achieve robust early fault detection. It outperforms traditional methods in terms of detection accuracy. Moreover, the visualization results illustrate that CNSAO can accurately extract the amplitude and phase differences in the dynamic industrial scenarios.

title: Augmented data-driven dynamic predictive maintenance strategy for multi-state system with RUL-maintenance level trade-off
abstract: In real industrial scenarios, critical components of multi-state systems experience performance degradation as operating time accumulate. Traditional data-driven Predictive Maintenance (PdM) methods fail in improving system performance and prolonging Remaining Useful Life (RUL) due to the insufficient data and set maintenance level manually. Therefore, in this work, a novel PdM strategy is proposed for multi-state system to address these issues. A minimum discrepancy criterion-based data augmentation method is first proposed to generate high-quality realistic samples by calculating the minimum discrepancy value from pairwise comparisons in the data sequence. A Stage Transition Points (STPs) localization method is then developed to detect degradation STPs by calculating mutation values in the two-dimensional feature space. Meanwhile, an Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm-Support Vector Machine (ISSA-SVM) is constructed to adaptively identify Multi-Stage Degradation (MSD). A hierarchical RUL prediction model is subsequently customized to predict the RUL of each degradation stage. Finally, an RUL-dependent PdM model is developed to minimize the total maintenance cost and maximize the RUL-maintenance level trade-off, obtaining optimized maintenance decision-making and avoiding over- or under-maintenance. The proposed method is compared to other methods using the C-MAPSS dataset and Silicon Rod Slicing Machine (SRCM) run-to-failure industrial dataset. Comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other methods in both RUL prediction and maintenance strategy.

title: Vibration data-driven supervised learning for low-speed bearing fault diagnosis using classical and nonlinear features
abstract: Fault diagnosis of low-speed bearings via vibration analysis is challenging due to the low energy of fault signatures and the high susceptibility to noise, particularly in early degradation stages. Recent deep-learning approaches have shown promising results in mitigating those limitations, yet many require large datasets, high sampling rates, or complex preprocessing for ensuring generalization. This study proposes a supervised learning framework optimized for limited data scenarios, advancing the state-of-the-art through four contributions. First, Rosenstein’s Largest Lyapunov Exponent (LLE) algorithm is modified by replacing Euclidean with Pearson correlation distance for nearest-neighbor identification in reconstructed phase space, enhancing class separability. Second, a hybrid feature set integrates classical time-domain indicators with nonlinear measures (LLE and Higuchi Fractal Dimension), tailored for incipient-fault conditions. Third, the influence of vibration signal window size, expressed in shaft revolutions, is systematically evaluated with the use of Welch’s t-test, providing guidelines for balancing sensitivity and computational cost. Finally, the framework is validated on two datasets, namely, (1) an experimental set simulating abrasive wear on bearing outer races at three severities under varied loads, representing a non-periodic defect type rarely studied, and (2) naturally degraded industrial pulley bearings. The results show high classification accuracy without complex preprocessing, confirming suitability for predictive maintenance in data- and resource-constrained environments. The approach offers a compact, interpretable, and data-efficient solution for early fault detection in low-speed bearings, with potential for deployment in industrial contexts where robustness and scalability are critical.

title: Fault diagnosis of ball screws in servo mechanisms using deeply integrated MEMS sensors and convolutional neural networks
abstract: Accurate fault diagnosis in critical mechanical systems like ball screws is hampered by the difficulty of acquiring high-fidelity signals from core operational areas. This paper presents a novel methodology for ball screw fault diagnosis that overcomes this limitation by leveraging a deeply integrated wireless monitoring system (WMS). The WMS utilizes both embedded and surface-attached MEMS accelerometers and temperature sensors with sensitivities of 18.8 mV/g and 3 mV/°C respectively to capture vibration and thermal signals directly from the ball-raceway contact zones, enabling more detailed observation of internal dynamics compared with conventional external sensing methods. The multi-modal signals are processed and analyzed using time–frequency analysis and a custom-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for automated condition recognition. Experimental results on a dedicated platform show that single-modal sensing achieves 76.7 % to 85.0 % accuracy for temperature signals and 93.3 % to 96.7 % accuracy for vibration signals, while multi-modal fusion of the WMS data enables the CNN model to reach 100 % classification accuracy, effectively distinguishing between normal and faulty conditions under various speeds. This work demonstrates a fully functional research prototype combining hardware and intelligent analysis for machinery fault diagnosis, from innovative signal acquisition to intelligent data analysis, offering significant potential for advancing predictive maintenance.

title: Enhanced multiple fault diagnosis in industrial robots through node-level capsule graph neural networks optimized with elk herd optimizer
abstract: The problem diagnosis and status monitoring are essential for industrial equipment to continue operating continuously. While the dynamics of the physical process must be modelled using traditional diagnostic techniques, it might be difficult to create an accurate dynamic model of intricately linked industrial systems. In this paper, Enhanced Multiple Fault Diagnosis in Industrial Robots through Node-Level Capsule Graph Neural Networks Optimized with Elk Herd Optimizer (EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO) is proposed. Here, the input data is gathered from PHME 2021 dataset. The gathered input data are given to the preprocessing stage. In preprocessing, Box-cox-sparse-measures-based blind filtering (BCSMBF) is used to data merging, columns concatenating, missing values imputation and dataset normalization. Then, pre-processed data are given into NCGNN for classifying fault diagnosis in industrial robots as fault and no fault. Finally, the Elk Herd Optimizer (EHO) enhances NCGNN for classifying fault diagnosis in industrial robots. The performance of the EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO is compared with other existing models. The EMFD-IR-NLCGNN-EHO method attains 6.58%, 8.25% and 5.29% higher accuracy; 8.96%, 5.21% and 6.89% higher recall; 6.12%, 5.23% and 8.87% higher f1-score when compared with existing techniques: Multi faults diagnosis for industrial robot fuse quality test bench utilizing DL (MFD-IRFTB-DL), Online fault detection of industrial robot utilizing IoRT with hybrid DL models, Experimental technique (OFD-IR-HDLT) and Model-dependent fault diagnosis algorithms for robotic systems (FDA-RS) respectively.

title: Prediction of equivalent damping ratio for round-ended hollow railway bridge piers with variable sections based on GA-BP neural network and quasi-static test
abstract: The equivalent damping ratio is a key parameter in the dynamic characteristics analysis of bridge piers and in performance-based seismic design. However, existing theoretical models primarily focus on solid piers and traditional hollow piers, and have not fully considered the unique mechanical properties of round-ended variable-section hollow piers, which arise from their variable stiffness characteristics and complex hysteretic energy dissipation behavior, leading to limitations in accurately evaluating the equivalent damping ratio. Therefore, a framework integrating “test-driven and machine learning” was proposed in this paper. First, seven scaled models of railway round-ended variable-section hollow piers were designed, and the hysteretic performance and evolution of the equivalent damping ratio were analyzed through a quasi-static test system, focusing on the effects of axial compression ratio, longitudinal reinforcement ratio, and stirrup ratio. Experimental results showed that the equivalent damping ratio exhibited a distinct two-stage pattern with the increase in displacement ductility ratio, and was significantly influenced by key design parameters. To overcome the limitations of conventional theoretical models, a prediction model was developed with displacement ductility ratio, axial compression ratio, shear span ratio, longitudinal reinforcement ratio, and stirrup ratio as inputs, and the equivalent damping ratio as the output. Both a traditional backpropagation (BP) neural network model and a genetic algorithm (GA) optimized BP neural network model were established. The comparative analysis revealed that the hybrid model, after GA global optimization, demonstrated a significant improvement in prediction performance: its mean square error and mean absolute error were reduced by 94% and 74%, respectively, compared to the BP model, with the coefficient of determination of 0.997 and a 79% reduction in maximum prediction error. The GA-BP model, validated through reserved independent experimental data, showed a prediction error standard deviation of only 0.0005, demonstrating excellent accuracy and generalization ability. Further global sensitivity analysis revealed the relative importance of each input parameter on the equivalent damping ratio, enhancing the interpretability of the model. The GA-BP prediction model developed in this study offers a novel, high-precision, high-efficiency data-driven approach for predicting the equivalent damping ratio of railway hollow piers, significantly promoting performance-based seismic design and analysis.

title: A liquid-impulse neural network model based on heterogeneous fusion of multimodal information for interpretable rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: For the problems of dynamic feature attenuation, low efficiency of multimodal fusion and insufficient diagnostic interpretability in rotating machinery fault diagnosis, this paper proposes an interpretable multimodal heterogeneous fusion liquid impulse neural network (LINN) model. First, a liquid state coding layer based on differential equations is constructed to model the time-series dynamic evolution features in non-stationary signals via a chunked feedback mechanism. Moreover, a multi-channel leaky integrate-and-fire (MC-LIF) impulse neurons are introduced to enhance the extraction of transient shock features by combining alternative gradient and membrane potential attenuation strategies. Finally, an attention-guided multimodal fusion mechanism is designed to realize adaptive integration and contribution interpretability quantification of time–frequency features. In the high-noise and variable-load condition tests, LINN achieves more than 98.7% accuracy with only 4.1 M parameters and 88.64% cross-condition generalization accuracy. The ablation experiments verify the key role of liquid layer and impulse mechanism in enhancing dynamic modelling and noise immunity, and the interpretability analysis based on time–frequency domain attention (TFDA) further reveals the sensitive response of the model to key time–frequency modal contributions. The method provides an effective solution with high accuracy, strong generalization and interpretability for intelligent diagnosis under complex working conditions.

title: A new method for quantitative evaluation of micro-cracks on turbine blade surfaces Fusing triboelectric sensing and hybrid deep learning
abstract: Surface micro-cracks, a common and severe processing defect in CNC milling of high-performance components such as aero-engine turbine blades, act as stress concentration sites that drastically reduce the fatigue life of the component and threaten the structural safety of the engine. However, existing non-destructive testing techniques face challenges in being integrated into machine tools to achieve rapid, online, and quantitative in-situ detection of micro-defects on complex curved components. To address this, this paper proposes a novel in-situ detection paradigm based on a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG), aiming to achieve high-precision quantitative inversion of the geometric parameters of micro-cracks on machined blade surfaces. The influence mechanism of crack width and depth on pulse amplitude and width was explained through systematic experimental research. Furthermore, by constructing multidimensional signal features that integrate time-domain and frequency-domain features, the coupling effects of width and depth can be decoupled. To achieve automated recognition, we constructed a hybrid deep learning model based on CNN-BiLSTM, which can autonomously mine the intrinsic correlation between spatiotemporal features and crack geometry parameters in the original signal, thereby synchronously outputting accurate predictions of width and depth. The experimental results show that the average absolute error of the model in predicting the width and depth of microcracks is as low as 0.0091 mm and 0.0047 mm, respectively, and the coefficient of determination (R2) is higher than 0.989. Furthermore, the potential of this method for identifying defects such as pitting, linear cracks, and network cracks has been further confirmed. This study not only confirms the enormous potential of TENG in intelligent manufacturing quality online monitoring, but also provides a solid technical path for the development of the next generation of intelligent integrated detection systems.

title: Simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressure process based on machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model
abstract: Accurately simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure fields on low-rise building roofs is critical for wind-resistant reliability design. This paper proposes a machine learning-enhanced Hermite polynomial model (ML-EHPM)-based method for the rapid and precise simulation of stationary non-Gaussian wind pressures. Building upon traditional moment-based HPM simulation methods, this study develops two machine learning models to enhance simulation accuracy and efficiency. First, in determining the ML-EHPM-based translation function, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), combined with the Bald Eagle Search optimization algorithm, is used to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order raw moments to the statistical moments of the translation function. This processing eliminates the need for integral solutions and monotonic interval constraints. Subsequently, a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) is employed to map non-Gaussian power spectra to Gaussian power spectra. To validate the simulation performance, three univariate simulation cases (strongly non-Gaussian, non-monotonic regions, and bimodal distributions) and one multivariate simulation case are given. Results indicate that the ML-EHPM approach offers substantially improved simulation accuracy than the conventional HPM method. Additionally, it can also simulate wind pressures in non-monotonic regions where the traditional HPM method is unavailable. Therefore, the proposed method provides a practical and efficient tool for high-precision simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures.

title: Phoneme-inspired acoustic frame embedded lightweight transformer for rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Acoustic-based fault diagnosis has gained increasing attention due to its flexibility and applicability under diverse operating conditions. Recent studies have demonstrated that Transformer-based architectures exhibit remarkable capability in modeling long-range temporal dependencies, so they are particularly effective for complex time series representation and analysis. However, applying Transformers to acoustic fault diagnosis faces the following critical challenges. The primary hurdle lies in discriminating short-duration nonstationary acoustic features amidst complex environmental interference, Simultaneously, how to ensure model diagnostic performance under limited computing resources is a challenge. Inspired by the phoneme processing paradigm where continuous speech is discretized into meaningful units, this paper proposes a lightweight acoustic segment-frame embedded Transformer, termed ASFE-Transformer, to address these issues effectively. First, an Analytic Amplitude-Phase Representation Module is introduced to derive physically meaningful representations, ensuring that the instantaneous evolution characteristics of multidimensional acoustic signals are faithfully retained. Second, an Acoustic Frame Embedding Module is developed to aggregate continuous analytic samples into a single token during the embedding stage. This strategy generates a more efficient token sequence and explicitly enhances the discriminability of transient fault cues while substantially reducing the computational burden. Third, the feed-forward network of the Transformer is redesigned by proposing a novel Swish-Depthwise Gated Linear Unit. By embedding a lightweight depth-wise convolution within the Swish-activated gating mechanism, this module introduces local contextual awareness into the encoder. Comprehensive experiments on two bearing acoustic datasets verify that the proposed framework delivers robust diagnostic performance with a lightweight design and highlight its strong potential for real-world industrial deployment.

title: Optimized S-transform embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network for aero-engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) has attracted significant attention for its powerful capability in fault feature extraction, and has has found widespread applications in intelligent fault diagnosis of mechanical systems. Nevertheless, its limited interpretability and vulnerability to noise remain key challenges in both academic and industrial contexts. Motivated by the strong theoretical foundations and physical interpretability of traditional signal processing methods, this study aims to enhance the performance of CNN by integrating signal analysis theory. Given the non-stationary characteristics and high noise levels commonly observed in aero-engine vibration signals, conventional time–frequency analysis methods often fail to provide optimal representations. To address this limitation, a first-order frequency function with two adjustable parameters are introduced into the Gaussian window function of the original S-transform, deriving an optimized S-transform (OST) that exhibits improved window adaptability and enhanced time–frequency representation capability. Then, an OST embedded time–frequency interpretable neural network (OSTNN) is proposed for fault diagnosis in aero-engines without any predefined parameters. This design enables the transformation of standard first layer convolutional kernel in the CNN method into OST convolutional kernel, whose parameters are continuously adjusted during the training procedure. The proposed OSTNN framework not only effectively suppresses noise interference effectively but also enhances model interpretability through visualization of learned time–frequency feature distributions and analysis of overall amplitude-frequency response. Extensive experiments on three aero-engine datasets, covering typical bearing and rotor faults, demonstrated that the OSTNN method consistently outperforms surpasses eight state-of-the-art diagnostic approaches in terms of effectiveness, noise robustness, interpretability, imbalance, generalization, and few-shot learning capability.

title: FCTransformer: An intelligent fault diagnosis method for multi-sensor information fusion based on Fourier convolution and transformer
abstract: Aiming at the problems of missing information and insufficient modelling in the frequency domain and time domain for the existing multi-sensor data fusion methods, an intelligent fault diagnosis method based on Fourier convolution and Transformer (FCTransformer) is proposed. Firstly, the method uses principal component analysis (PCA) to downscale high-dimensional and multi-modal sensor data, and converts them into RGB images by continuous wavelet transform (CWT). Then, a Fourier convolution (FC) is designed, which can not only effectively extract local periodic frequency domain features, but also enhances the nonlinear feature extraction capability of the model. Finally, a variational auto-encoding transformer (VAETransformer) is designed to achieve global dependency modelling, which enhances the identification for multi-sensor coupled features. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, experimental validation is carried out on the bearing and gearbox datasets. The results show that the average fault diagnosis accuracy of FCTransformer is 99.58% under normal sample conditions, and its average fault diagnosis accuracy is 96.10% under small sample conditions. This indicates that FCTransformer has superior fault diagnosis performance and can meet the requirements of rotating machinery fault diagnosis tasks.

title: Online detection of milling chatter based on multi-order graph convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a type of self-excited vibration that occurs during machining, particularly when processing weak-rigidity aerospace parts, adversely affecting machining quality and efficiency. In order to prevent the detrimental effects of chatter in milling processes, a physically interpretable multi-order graph convolutional neural network (GCN)-based method is proposed for online chatter detection. In this method, the vertex and edge of the network are first constructed through the measured multi-channel vibration signal time series segments with short duration, establishing the groundwork for online chatter detection. Then, a multi-order GCN is developed by gathering feature information from multiple orders of neighbors of the target vertex to enhance its accuracy. Next, based on the multi-order GCN, a deep neural network is constructed and trained using the vibration data obtained by numerous milling experiments. During the training process, the edge weights are optimized by the gradient descent method. After that, an online chatter detection system is constructed, which demonstrates robust noise resistance through tests with different levels of noise interference added. Finally, experiments under various milling conditions validate that the proposed method can accurately detect milling chatter at its early weak stage, thereby successfully preventing its adverse effects.

title: Multi-channel chatter detection in robotic milling based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition and hybrid deep convolutional neural network
abstract: Chatter is a critical factor that limits machining quality and production efficiency in robotic milling. Therefore, timely and accurate online chatter detection is essential for achieving high-precision and high-efficiency machining. However, the dynamic properties of milling robots are highly pose-dependent, which significantly increases the randomness and complexity of chatter. Furthermore, due to the strong nonlinearity and flexibility of milling robots, chatter induces coupled three-dimensional vibrations. As a result, relying on vibration signals from a single direction is insufficient for achieving reliable chatter detection. In this paper, a multi-channel online chatter detection method in robotic milling is proposed, based on successive multivariate variational mode decomposition (SMVMD) and hybrid deep convolutional neural network. First, the SMVMD method combined with a dimensionless chatter index is employed to adaptively extract the chatter components in the three-channel acceleration signals. Then, the energy ratio sequence between the reconstructed chatter signal and the milling signal is calculated. Finally, a hybrid deep convolutional neural network (ICR-DCN), composed of Inception, convolutional block attention module (CBAM), residual network (ResNet) and classification module, is constructed to automatically extract chatter features from the energy ratio sequence and achieve online chatter detection. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can achieve high-precision online chatter detection across variations in different robotic poses, cutting parameters, workpiece materials and tools. Comparative studies further validate the accuracy and stability of the proposed method across various scenarios.

title: Learning to predict and control with sparse model discovery and deep temporal difference reinforcement learning
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) has demonstrated remarkable success in complex decision-making tasks, yet its application to predictive control remains challenging due to high sample requirements and limited long-horizon generalization. Model-based DRL methods promise improved sample efficiency by leveraging learned dynamics, but their performance is often restricted by inaccuracies in online model learning, which degrade control quality. This work introduces the Model-Agnostic Predictive Temporal Difference (MAP-TD) framework, a deep reinforcement learning approach capable of controlling systems with unknown physics. MAP-TD employs a pre-trained, interpretable, and parsimonious dynamics model discovered offline using Sparse Bayesian Learning (SBL), which is used for long-horizon trajectory prediction within the DRL architecture. This parsimonious model enhances predictive capability and enables the DRL agent to learn superior control strategies. The optimal control policies are learned by accumulating rewards and value functions along predictive trajectories, supported by a jointly trained terminal value function. For faster learning, we propose a hybrid strategy that periodically switches between fine and coarse solvers. MAP-TD delivers accurate long-horizon predictions while eliminating the need for online adaptation of approximate models. Numerical simulations on benchmark control tasks, including active vibration control of discrete and continuous structural dynamical systems, demonstrate that MAP-TD offers a computationally efficient and robust solution for predictive control.

title: Enhanced AR-based simulation method for non-Gaussian wind pressure process using machine learning model and piecewise Johnson transformation model
abstract: Accurate simulation of non-Gaussian wind pressures on low-rise buildings is essential for structural wind-resistant design. Recently, autoregressive (AR) models combined with the maximum entropy method (MEM) have been employed to develop an AR–MEM-based non-Gaussian wind pressure simulation approach, which has demonstrated satisfactory accuracy and convenience. However, this method suffers from low computational efficiency, limited applicability, and difficulty in extension to multivariate wind pressure simulations. This study comprehensively uses AR, piecewise Johnson transformation model (PJTM), machine learning model (ML), and proposes a novel ML-enhanced AR-PJTM (ML-AR-PJTM) method for simulating non-Gaussian wind pressure, which significantly improves simulation efficiency and widens the application range. In this method, the Extra Trees (ET) model is firstly adopted to map the target power spectral density to the parameters of a set of formulas to determine the first ten-order standardized central moments of the input process in AR model, in which a formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has been developed. Subsequently, the Categorical Boosting (CatBoost) model, combined with Bayesian optimization (BO), is employed to establish a nonlinear mapping from the first ten-order standardized central moments to the corresponding statistical moments used to determine PJTM, in which another similar formulation for expanding the number of training samples based on limited experimental data has also been developed. Numerical cases show that the proposed method achieves significant improvements in computational efficiency while maintaining the same accuracy as the traditional AR-MEM-based method.

title: Attention-enhanced transformer with prototype alignment for few-shot fault diagnosis under noisy cross-condition
abstract: This paper introduces a robust and adaptive few-shot learning framework for intelligent fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions and diverse noise interferences. The architecture integrates multi-scale signal encoding, adaptive condition modulation, prototype-driven alignment, and transformer-based decision modeling. To ensure noise robustness, raw sensor signals are first processed via parallel dilated depthwise separable convolutions and refined by a channel-spatial attention unit to enhance fault-relevant patterns. A context-aware modulation stage then recalibrates feature maps according to operating-condition indicators, promoting cross-condition generalization. For classification with limited labeled examples, prototype estimation is performed using a median-based reliable estimator, and query embeddings are aligned to these prototypes through a cross-domain attention-based alignment mechanism. A transformer encoder captures global interactions among aligned features and produces the final predictions. Training is guided by a composite loss combining classification, outlier, and dependency-aware terms, with a warm-up strategy to balance fitting and regularization. Evaluation on two industrial benchmarks, the Tennessee Eastman process and gold hydrometallurgy process, demonstrates that the framework consistently outperforms existing methods in noise resilience and domain adaptation.

title: Quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer for noise-robust underwater propeller fault diagnosis
abstract: Underwater propeller fault diagnosis is crucial for marine engineering applications and autonomous underwater vehicles; however, traditional methods can degrade severely in complex underwater environments where sensor reliability is unpredictable. This paper proposes a quality-aware gated cross-modal transformer (GCM-T) for robust fault diagnosis by fusing acoustic and visual information. The core innovations include (i) a quality-aware gating mechanism that dynamically adjusts modality weights based on domain-specific quality metrics and (ii) a gated cross-attention module that mitigates contamination from low-quality inputs via quality-guided feature enhancement. Evaluation on a novel underwater propeller dataset (7 fault categories, 17 scenarios ranging from clean conditions to extreme degradation) shows that GCM-T achieves 99.4% overall accuracy, maintains 100% accuracy under clean conditions, and remains robust under severe degradations. Sea-trial validation on a real AUV platform further demonstrates the framework’s practical applicability. Compared with existing methods, GCM-T delivers consistent gains under extreme conditions, demonstrating improved adaptability. Interpretability analyses validate the quality-aware design by revealing strong correlations between the learned gate weights and the measured modality-quality gaps.

title: Evolutionary hypergraph: A Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network for multi-sensor rolling bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Modern multi-sensor systems generate high-dimensional, noise-contaminated, and dynamically evolving multivariate time-series data, in which complex spatiotemporal dependencies play a key role in accurate fault diagnosis. However, effectively modeling these high-order correlations remains a significant challenge. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Kalman-guided spatiotemporal dynamic hypergraph neural network(KSD-HGNN), which is designed to comprehensively characterize high-order relationships and dynamic evolution among multiple sensors. The framework first employs a learnable band-pass filter bank for adaptive frequency-domain feature extraction, and then constructs and optimizes a dynamic spatiotemporal hypergraph to jointly encode spatial adjacency and cross-step temporal dependencies. Furthermore, by integrating Kalman filtering into hypergraph convolution, the model performs temporal smoothing and state estimation over hyperedge sequences, yielding more stable spatiotemporal representations. Finally, the state dynamics learned by the Kalman-guided branch and the structural dynamics captured by the adaptive topology branch are fused via a gating mechanism, yielding a more stable and comprehensive system representation. Experimental results demonstrate that KSD-HGNN consistently outperforms existing methods under varying operating and noise conditions, significantly improving multi-sensor bearing fault diagnosis performance.

title: Self-supervised ViT-driven whole-line alignment of multi-date rail ultrasonic B-scan data for longitudinal infrastructure inspection
abstract: Multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data provide critical evidence for defect identification, cross-period reinspection, and longitudinal condition assessment. However, reliable comparison of inspection records acquired on different dates requires mileage alignment, so that B-scan indications from the same physical rail locations can be compared over time. Existing alignment methods generally follow two routes. Methods relying on external mileage or positioning references may suffer from accumulated drift, initialization offsets, and local data loss during long-distance inspection, whereas methods based on local signal similarity are easily disrupted by sparse indications, noise, missing features, and false alarms. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a whole-line cross-date alignment framework for multi-channel rail ultrasonic B-scan data. The method first converts pseudo-color B-scan indications into structured event-level cues and extracts repeatable local patterns from unlabeled inspection data. These cues are then used to estimate a global coarse offset, construct reliable candidate correspondences, enforce global order consistency, and fit a piecewise mileage mapping between inspection runs. Experiments on real multi-date heavy-haul railway inspection data show that the proposed method achieves stable whole-line alignment under noise, data discontinuities, and missing indications, suppresses drift accumulation, and reduces the mean alignment error to within 3 m. The results indicate that the proposed framework can provide a reliable mileage reference for cross-date ultrasonic reinspection and long-term rail condition assessment.

title: A Time-Frequency Fusion Spiking Neural Network for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on Learnable Neuronal Dynamics
abstract: Bearing fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions often suffers from insufficient feature representation and unstable performance. Many existing spiking neural network (SNN)-based methods use fixed neuronal dynamic parameters, which may limit their ability to accommodate operating-condition variations. Moreover, some diagnostic frameworks construct two-dimensional time-frequency representations before model training, introducing an additional offline transformation stage. In addition, some SNN-based diagnostic frameworks place less emphasis on explicit frequency-domain information. To address these issues, this paper proposes a time-frequency fusion SNN for bearing fault diagnosis based on learnable neuronal dynamics. First, one-dimensional vibration segments are replicated across four simulation time steps, and spectral information is modeled by an embedded Sinc-based branch. Then, temporal features and frequency-domain information are fused within a unified SNN framework, where learnable neuronal dynamics adjust temporal integration and spike-generation behavior during training to better match vibration patterns at different temporal scales. Experiments on the MFPT and JNU datasets show that the proposed model achieves accuracies of 98.33% and 99.33%, respectively, demonstrating competitive diagnostic performance.

title: Collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals using a physics-guided graph neural network
abstract: The acquisition of clean vibration signals is a fundamental prerequisite for structural health monitoring. With the development of distributed monitoring technologies, a key challenge for traditional single-point denoising methods is how to denoise signals from densely distributed measurement points while simultaneously preserving data quality and enforcing physical constraints. To address this issue, this study proposes a physics-guided graph neural network framework for collaborative denoising of multi-point vibration signals. The framework constructs a physics-embedded adjacency matrix to define node connections and introduces a physics-guided loss function with partial differential equation constraints, together with a boundary compensation mechanism, so that the denoised results not only conform to the statistical characteristics of the data but also satisfy mechanical laws. Experimental results from multiple test cases show that, compared with existing denoising methods, the proposed model achieves superior performance across all evaluation metrics and preserves the consistency of physical field characteristics more effectively. This study provides a new approach for vibration noise suppression in structural health monitoring.

title: Flow-induced vibrations in tandem square cylinders: machine learning analysis of structural response and energy harvesting under variable size and spacing ratios
abstract: Flow-induced vibrations (FIV) provide an effective mechanism for renewable energy harvesting, with potential applications in powering autonomous sensors, smart infrastructures, and low-power electronics. In tandem bluff-body configurations, wake interactions play a key role in modifying the structural response, leading to nonlinear and spacing-dependent vibration characteristics. This study experimentally investigates the performance of piezoelectric energy harvesters (PEHs) employing tandem square cylinders. Five configurations were tested at three spacings (S = 4, 8, and 12 cm) and flow velocities ranging from 2.4 to 13 m/s. The results show that the tandem arrangement significantly modifies both vibration amplitude and electrical output through wake-interaction effects. Depending on the size ratio and spacing, the system exhibits either enhanced or constrained oscillatory behavior. In particular, when a 4 cm cylinder is placed upstream of a 5 cm cylinder (Case 3), increased displacement and RMS voltage are observed compared with the isolated case, with maximum improvements of 356.5% in displacement and 171.9% in voltage. However, the response is strongly dependent on spacing, and no single configuration remains optimal across all flow conditions. This variability is addressed through the introduction of an integrated energy metric combined with normalized power comparison, enabling consistent evaluation across the full velocity range. To complement these findings and capture the nonlinear coupling among flow parameters, structural response, and harvested power, a CatBoost-based machine learning (ML) framework was developed and optimized using 10-fold cross-validation, incorporating an out-of-fold residual filtering step to suppress measurement noise and refine model accuracy. The combined experimental-ML approach enabled accurate prediction and facilitated the interpretation of trends associated with wake interference, achieving R2 = 0.98 for displacement and 0.85 for power, and demonstrates the potential of such tandem configurations within the investigated operating conditions for flow-adaptive energy harvesting systems and self-powered sensing applications.

title: Physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning agent for unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis
abstract: The reliable operation and accurate fault diagnosis of machinery under complex, varying operating conditions are crucial to the safety and reliability of industrial systems. However, existing unsupervised cross-domain fault diagnosis methods still suffer from limitations in modeling sample relationship topology and domain alignment. Physical information is difficult to integrate effectively with data-correlation features, and the dynamic domain alignment process lacks adaptive regulation. To address these issues, an embodied intelligence motivated physics-inspired graph fusion and reinforcement learning-based domain adaptation (PIFRLDA) method is proposed. First, a physics-inspired residual gated graph fusion mechanism is designed to construct an adaptive topology. It builds a physics-inspired graph in a latent dynamic space and adaptively fuses it with the data-driven graph through residual gating, thereby preserving sample relationships while introducing weak dynamics-related guidance into cross-condition feature interaction. A dual-path transformer sample-and-aggregate graph network is developed on the constructed graph to capture within-sample feature interactions and cross-sample topological relationships, thereby enhancing adaptability to structural correlations under complex conditions. In addition, a dual-agent cooperative domain adaptation framework is introduced to jointly optimize sample selection and feature perturbation, improving dynamic perception and adaptive regulation under varying operating conditions. Experimental results show that, compared with existing advanced unsupervised fault diagnosis methods, the proposed method offers significant advantages in both diagnostic accuracy and cross-condition generalization.

title: A novel hybrid data-driven approach for rapid estimation of building vibration responses in urban rail transit systems
abstract: Environmental vibration assessment conducted during the preliminary stage plays a critical role in identifying vibration-sensitive objectives along the railway that may experience excessive vibrations, thereby guiding the subsequent screening process and the design of vibration mitigation measures. This assessment typically relies on empirical formulas; however, the predictive accuracy of these formulas presents certain challenges, such as the risk of overly conservative evaluations, which may lead to unnecessary design expenditures. According to the core idea of multi-stage correction of empirical formulas, this study introduces a hybrid methodology that combines Bayesian Neural Networks with soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to enable efficient prediction of train-induced building vibration responses. Ground vibration data were first collected from seven different locations and synthesized into a comprehensive dataset. The spatial distribution of ground vibrations and the characteristics of vibration amplification zones were then systematically examined. Thereafter, a Bayesian Neural Network model was implemented to predict ground vibrations across 1/3 octave frequency bands, while effectively addressing the inherent uncertainties in the data. In the subsequent phase, the predicted ground vibration data were used as inputs in soil-structure coupling loss and building impedance models to calculate the soil-structure coupling loss and the corresponding building vibration responses. Finally, a case study was carried out to validate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed hybrid prediction framework.

title: A semi-supervised compound fault diagnosis method based on hierarchical attention and self-supervised graph learning for the rotary components of robots’ joints
abstract: Rotating machinery, which is a key component of industrial robots and precision equipment, is frequently susceptible to compound faults. However, diagnosing such faults remains challenging because of the coupling interference among fault features and the scarcity of labeled fault samples. To address this issue, this study proposes a semi‑supervised intelligent fault diagnosis method that integrates hierarchical attention and self‑supervised graph learning. The proposed method employs a three-layered progressive framework. At the node level, a multi-head self-attention mechanism screens and enhances the local features of each sample. At the edge level, a self-supervised graph autoencoder based on graph attention is constructed to model the correlations between samples from different sensors at the same time steps, thereby extracting and enhancing the features of various fault types. At the feature level, global similarity matching is applied to all extracted features to uncover the intrinsic relationships between compound and single faults. Finally, only a small set of labeled samples is used to train a multi‑label classifier to achieve an accurate diagnosis and effective decoupling of fault categories. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average accuracy of over 99.0% in diagnosing compound faults, maintaining excellent generalization and stability, even with limited training samples. This study not only presents an effective technical solution for the compound fault diagnosis of rotating machinery but also provides substantial theoretical support for the development of predictive maintenance systems in precision machinery applications.

title: Acoustic imaging method based on local-nonlocal attention and masked generative knowledge distillation
abstract: Deep learning (DL) has been extensively studied as a powerful data-driven method and shown encouraging results in numerous acoustic imaging-related tasks. Nevertheless, the notable improvements achieved through the advanced DL-based methods often come with increased model parameters and complexity, making the deployment of the models on devices with limited computational capabilities challenging. Knowledge distillation is an extremely promising technique for model compression, in which a lightweight student model is trained to mimic the behavior of the complex and powerful teacher model. The key idea of knowledge distillation is to leverage the supervisory information from the teacher model to enhance the overall performance of the student model without modifying its structure. Therefore, to develop lightweight models with enhanced performance in the context of acoustic imaging, a novel acoustic imaging method based on local-nonlocal attention and masked generative knowledge distillation (LNLMG-KD) is proposed. To apply the LNLMG-KD, a residual dense U-net teacher model (RDUN-T) and residual dense U-net student model (RDUN-S) are constructed. RDUN-T boasts superior performance and strong generalization ability in acoustic imaging, but it is burdened with sophisticated architecture and extensive parameters. RDUN-S is more efficient and possesses a more compact architecture with fewer parameters, but its capacity for acoustic imaging remains constrained compared to RDUN-T. During the training process of RDUN-S, LNLMG-KD is employed to transfer the knowledge learned from RDUN-T to RDUN-S. Through the local-nonlocal attention knowledge distillation, RDUN-S can effectively utilize both local and global information from RDUN-T. Additionally, the masked generative knowledge distillation enables RDUN-S to learn more robust features from RDUN-T. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through the comparisons of the proposed method with the advanced deconvolution methods using both simulation and experimental data. The results indicate that the proposed LNLMG-KD significantly enhances the performance of RDUN-S under the guidance of RDUN-T, which makes it a promising solution for deploying lightweight and superior models in embedded devices with limited computational resources for real-time and accurate acoustic imaging.

title: Robust feature selection for cross-domain fault diagnosis using deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Recent research on deep learning-based fault diagnosis has made significant progress. However, over-parameterized models often introduce redundant features, leading to degraded cross-domain generalization and limited deployability on resource-constrained devices. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a reinforcement-learning-based robust feature selection (RFS) framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis. Unlike existing methods that treat network pruning and domain adaptation as separate processes, the proposed approach integrates them at the decision level via a domain-aware reward formulation. Specifically, channel pruning is formulated as a sequential decision-making problem, where a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent learns an adaptive pruning policy. Meanwhile, domain alignment loss is incorporated into the reward function, enabling the pruning policy to directly optimize cross-domain feature robustness during the decision-making process rather than through post-hoc feature alignment. This mechanism promotes the retention of features that are both discriminative and transferable, while eliminating redundant or domain-specific components. This framework offers a principled approach for jointly optimizing model compactness and cross-domain generalization, rather than treating them as independent objectives. Extensive experiments on two gearbox datasets under various domain shift scenarios demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves cross-domain diagnostic performance while reducing model complexity. In particular, the method achieves up to 19.59 % improvement in target-domain accuracy and reduces computational cost by up to 73.87 % in FLOPs, with reduced inference latency. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in jointly achieving robust cross-domain generalization and efficient model deployment in practical industrial scenarios.

title: Nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor for UAV blade damage monitoring through hybrid deep learning
abstract: Real-time damage type monitoring of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) blades is essential for flight safety and operational efficiency. Vibration analysis serves as an effective approach to characterize blade damage types. However, existing vibration monitoring technologies exhibit limited responsiveness to low-acceleration vibrations and struggle to capture damage-induced signatures during flight. To address these limitations, this study proposes a nonlinear stiffness triboelectric vibration sensor (NS-TVS). Leveraging its nonlinear stiffness mechanism, the sensor achieves a broad monitoring frequency range of 5 to 1500 Hz and sensitivity to anomalous vibration responses induced by blade damage. Experimental results demonstrate the output characteristics of the NS-TVS and its adaptability to UAV. Outperforming conventional vibration sensors, the NS-TVS achieves a peak sensitivity of 8.33 V/g, an acceleration detection limit of 0.1 g, and an SNR of 45.27 dB under weak excitation. Accounting for merely 5% of a single UAV arm’s payload, it imposes negligible disturbance on blade aerodynamics. For signal processing and condition assessment, a gated-attention-based convolutional recurrent neural network (GA-CRNN) was developed for feature extraction and classification across seven predefined blade types. Experimental findings revealed that the proposed model achieved an average classification accuracy of 95.96% in identifying the predefined blade damage types. The GA-CRNN was subsequently deployed on a UAV onboard computer, and actual flight tests verified the sensor’s engineering practicality and reliability.

title: Health state assessment of complex electromechanical systems based on AINN and frequency domain causal network
abstract: The reliability of complex electromechanical systems is crucial for industrial and national operations. However, accurately assessing the health state of these systems presents significant challenges due to high-dimensional data, nonstationary conditions, and limited labeled data. To address these challenges, we proposed an unsupervised health state assessment method that integrated an Autoregressive Informed Neural Network (AINN) with Generalized Partial Directed Coherence (GPDC). Our approach, AINN-GPDC, introduced an Iterative Variable Selection (IVS) strategy to establish correlation models among high-dimensional parameters and leveraged GPDC to construct frequency-domain causal networks, effectively handling nonstationary and nonlinear data. The method provided a comprehensive evaluation of system health by constructing health indicators based on graph density and graph entropy, enabling precise detection of system state changes. The proposed framework was validated on the N-CMAPSS and real-world satellite datasets, demonstrating superior performance in early anomaly detection and failure prediction. Our findings highlight the potential of AINN-GPDC as a robust tool for health monitoring, particularly in complex, unlabeled, and dynamic environments.

title: Decision fusion for damage localization in CFRP laminate using Lamb wave and acoustic emission
abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) structures are particularly vulnerable to barely visible impact damage during service, requiring advanced methods for assessment. This study presents a novel damage localization approach that synergistically combines Lamb wave (LW) and acoustic emission (AE) techniques through decision-level fusion. Experiment using low-velocity impacts generated complementary active LW and passive AE datasets, which were processed using Hilbert transform and envelope extraction for feature extraction. A deep learning regression model was developed to predict damage coordinates, augmented by an optimized weighted-average fusion strategy. However, due to signal distortion and sparse sensor coverage, single-modality methods suffer from degraded performance in certain regions, particularly near structural edges. Feature-level fusion struggles to reconcile the nonlinear differences between LW and AE signals, often leading to information redundancy or loss. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a novel decision-level weighted fusion framework that leverages the complementary strengths of LW and AE while preserving their individual signal characteristics. Comparative analysis shows that the localization errors in the x and y coordinates are reduced by 41.49 % and 38.36 %, respectively, compared to single-modality methods. In the edge regions, the errors in the x and y coordinates are reduced by 18.04 % and 14.44 %, respectively. The methodology demonstrates significant potential in practical implementation in CFRP structural health monitoring systems, offering enhanced reliability for impact damage assessment.

title: Multi-view feature consistency learning for cross-domain open-set mechanical fault diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning-enabled cross-domain fault diagnosis plays a crucial role in improving the operational reliability and safety of mechanical systems. Conventional approaches usually assume that the testing data share an identical label space with the training data, implying consistent fault types across different engineering scenarios. However, in practical applications, fault types encountered during deployment are often unpredictable, and novel faults may arise, thereby undermining the effectiveness of existing domain adaptation methods. To address these challenges, a novel open-set domain adaptation framework termed multi-view feature consistency learning (MFCL) is proposed. Specifically, source-domain prototype constraints and domain-adversarial learning are jointly employed to align feature distributions between source and target domains, while multi-view contrastive learning enhances the representational quality of multi-view unlabeled target samples. Furthermore, an entropy-based adversarial separation mechanism is introduced to enable accurate identification of unknown classes during adaptation, thereby facilitating the separation between known and unknown classes. In addition, an unknown-aware consistency learning strategy is developed by integrating prototype-guided pseudo-labeling with multi-view features, which further boosts cross-domain classification performance. Extensive experiments on the SDUST and BJTU-RAO bearing datasets demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art approaches in open-set domain adaptation and holds strong potential for enhancing the reliability of mechanical systems in practice.

title: Residual-informed deep meta regressor for predicting modal frequencies of historical masonry buildings under environmental and operational data scarcity
abstract: Dynamic monitoring of historical masonry buildings is essential for preserving architectural heritage and ensuring structural safety under varying operational and environmental conditions. Field measurements for dynamic monitoring, while invaluable, often face significant limitations including high costs, logistical challenges of masonry buildings, limited sensor coverage, and sensor malfunctions. Although machine learning-based predictive models offer promising alternatives to complement or replace in-situ monitoring, their performance is often degraded by unmeasured environmental and operational factors, resulting in reduced accuracy and uncertainty in dynamic response prediction. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel predictive method called Residual-informed Deep Meta Regressor (RiDMR) designed to forecast dynamic responses (modal frequencies) of heritage masonry buildings under partially observed environmental and/or operational conditions. The proposed RiDMR model is developed from a long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network trained on a meta dataset. This meta dataset is constructed by combining measured data with residuals (prediction errors) extracted from some baseline regression models, thereby capturing hidden information of unmeasured but influential environmental/operational variables. The major innovation of this research lies in the development of a residual-informed meta learning framework that integrates statistical and deep learning models by leveraging residual learning to capture unmeasured influences, meta learning to enhance generalization under uncertainty, and hybrid learning to combine the strengths of multiple predictive approaches. Validation on a real-world historical masonry building demonstrates that the proposed RiDMR method significantly enhances prediction accuracy and generalization under unobservable and evolving environmental or operational conditions.

title: MAFN: A multi-view adaptive fusion network with image and time-series signal aggregation for additive manufacturing fault diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of additive manufacturing (AM) processes is crucial for improving product quality and performance. However, existing single-view fault diagnosis methods based solely on acoustic emission (AE) signals are limited in capturing the comprehensive features of the signals. In this research, a multi-view adaptive fusion network (MAFN) is proposed, which fully combines the image and time-series features of AE signals to achieve accurate fault diagnosis. Firstly, the one-dimensional time-series signals acquired by the sensors are converted into two-dimensional image signals using gramian angular difference fields (GADF) encoding. Subsequently, adaptive convolution neural network and Mamba (ACNN-Mamba) architecture is designed to capture the global contextual information and local features of the image signals, which effectively solves the insufficient extraction of high-frequency detail features of the images. Particularly, bi-directional gated recurrent unit and global focusing mechanism (BiGRU-GF) architecture is utilized to capture bidirectional dependencies of the sequence data. In addition, a cross-view signal interaction module (CSIM) is designed, which uses an adaptive interaction strategy to dynamically adjust the weights between images and time-series features. The proposed MAFN outperforms existing single-view and multi-view methods in terms of diagnostic performance and noise robustness after experimentally validated on selective laser melting and laser directed energy deposition datasets. This study not only provides an efficient and accurate new method for fault diagnosis in AM, but also provides new ideas for the application of multi-view fusion technology in industrial equipment monitoring and maintenance.

title: Interpretable compound fault diagnosis of hydraulic gear pumps via fusion of physical priors and probabilistic joint reasoning
abstract: The external gear pump is susceptible to coupled degradation involving multiple faults under complex operating conditions, which poses considerable challenges to fault diagnosis. However, existing methods generally lack interpretability and the capability to quantify uncertainty in compound fault modeling, which limits their reliability in practical applications. To address this issue, this paper proposes a three-stage compound fault diagnosis framework. The framework sequentially employs a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to invert key structural parameters under unlabeled conditions, a Bayesian Neural Network (BNN) to model parameter distributions and perform uncertainty reasoning, and a lightweight Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) based on the statistical features output by the BNN to accomplish fault classification. Using seven typical fault datasets obtained from an Electro-Hydrostatic Actuator (EHA) experimental platform, the results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially outperforms baseline models such as Transformer and 1D-CNN in terms of overall accuracy and compound fault recognition. It also maintains high robustness under small-sample and high-noise conditions, and exhibits promising generalization capability in partially labeled and unknown fault recognition tasks, providing a feasible path toward transparent and interpretable fault diagnosis under complex working conditions.

title: PGVAE-VBAKF: A robust strategy for complex system response prediction and noise variance estimation considering modeling errors and nonstationary noises
abstract: Accurate system response prediction is essential in understanding the latent physics and assessing the performance, safety, and durability of structures. Although numerous model- and data- based methods have been developed for structural response prediction, the combined effects of modeling errors and time-varying measurement noises can significantly reduce the response prediction accuracy. To address this issue, the present study proposes a Physics-Guided Variational Auto-Encoder with Variational Bayesian Adaptive Kalman Filter (PGVAE-VBAKF) strategy for complex system response prediction and noise variance estimation. First, to mitigate the impact of modeling errors on complex system learning, this study proposes a PGVAE-based approach that integrates state-space modeling with neural networks. This method enhances the accuracy of response modeling for complex systems. Compared to data-driven methods, the proposed PGVAE-based approach can significantly reduce the relative root mean square error (RRMSE) of response prediction. Second, this study employs a well-trained PGVAE to replace the transition and observation models in the Kalman filter, which can effectively mitigate the influence of inaccurate system matrices and yield precise response estimation. Third, to handle nonstationary noises, this study integrates PGVAE with VBAKF to enable effective response estimation for complex systems subject to modeling errors and nonstationary noises, which can quantify time-varying noise variances. Furthermore, a model reduction strategy that integrates PGVAE with Z-score normalization, modal superposition, and residual neural network is proposed to improve the training efficiency and high-dimensional system learning accuracy. Numerical and experimental studies are implemented to validate the performance of the proposed method. Research results show that the proposed method can accurately predict the complex system response and quantify the uncertainty of noise variances. The proposed method can effectively mitigate the combined adverse effects of modeling errors and nonstationary noises for complex system learning and has the potential to be applied for structural health monitoring (SHM) of complex nonlinear structures.

title: A unified Cross-Modal adaptive contrastive learning framework for acoustic fault diagnosis of rolling bearing under limited & imbalanced data
abstract: The intelligent fault diagnosis method based on acoustics provides a effective approach for achieving reliable data-driven maintenance in industrial scenarios. However, in actual scenarios, mechanical equipment is mainly in a normal operating state, which leads to limited monitoring data and an imbalance in fault categories (L&I). Moreover, multi-source heterogeneous data are often fragmented and difficult to integrate, while most artificial intelligence models merely provide fault warnings without dynamic optimization or decision-making capabilities. To address these issues, this paper proposes a unified cross-modal adaptive contrastive learning framework jointly models the ideas of data-level augmentation and algorithm-level adaptation within a single end-to-end architecture. From a data-level perspective, inspired by the multi-view representation theory, the proposed method constructs a same-source dual-modality input by transforming raw acoustic signals into temporal waveforms and gramian angular difference field (GADF) images, thereby enriching feature diversity without introducing sensor inconsistency. A multi-scale residual image encoder (MSR-IE) and a hybrid temporal encoder with multi-receptive convolutions (HTE-MRC) are designed to extract modality-specific features. Subsequently, integration is carried out through a cross-modal contrastive fusion module. During this process, heterogeneous feature Spaces are aligned into a unified, domain-invariant embedding. At the algorithmic level, a dual-task guided fault discriminator (DGFD) is developed to jointly perform coarse-grained health assessment and fine-grained fault identification, with dynamic task reweighting to balance learning under class-imbalanced conditions. Results on two rolling bearing acoustic datasets across six imbalance regimes show that the proposed method achieves 97.9 % accuracy and 98.9 % G-mean, with notably improved minority-class detection and balanced performance under severe imbalance.

title: Speed-guided diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder for fault diagnosis under limited data
abstract: Deep learning-based fault diagnosis has shown great potential in intelligent condition monitoring. However, its performance heavily depends on large amounts of labeled data, which are often scarce in real-world industrial scenarios, especially under varying speed conditions. The data limitations hinder the generalization ability of fault diagnosis models. To address this issue, we propose a novel speed-guided denoising diffusion probabilistic model integrated with variational autoencoder (SDPM-VAE) for generating high quality data. The speed signal is incorporated as a conditional prior through a cross-attention mechanism to preserve speed-dependent characteristics in the generated data. Additionally, a hybrid VAE and DDPM framework is proposed to enhance data quality while reducing computational cost. The coarse reconstructions and latent representations derived from the VAE are integrated into the reverse diffusion process. Experimental results on two gearbox datasets demonstrate that the SDPM-VAE outperforms four state-of-the-art methods in both the quality of the generated data and fault diagnosis accuracy, thereby validating its effectiveness for data augmentation under limited data conditions.

title: Spatio-temporal variational reconstruction deep support vector data description for anomaly detection in bridge SHM data
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) systems are essential for ensuring infrastructure safety, particularly in the long-term evaluation of structures like bridges. However, factors like sensor malfunctions, traffic accidents, and data anomalies resulting from structural deformations can cause monitoring data to deviate from the actual structural response, significantly compromising the accuracy of assessment results. Existing anomaly detection methods often encounter challenges such as class imbalance, strong temporal dependencies, and spatial correlations in multi-sensor data. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel anomaly detection framework, Spatiotemporal Variational Reconstruction with Deep Support Vector Data Description (STVR-DeSVDD). First, the STVR-DeSVDD model integrates a graph attention network (GAT) with a long short-term memory (LSTM) network, enabling the model to effectively capture sensor interactions and their time-varying patterns. This approach addresses both temporal and spatial dependencies in multi-sensor data during long-term monitoring. Second, the model combines a variational autoencoder (VAE) with deep support vector data description (DeSVDD). By minimizing latent space reconstruction error and controlling hypersphere volume, the model improves the compactness of normal data and reduces the risk of hypersphere collapse, thereby refining the boundary between normal and anomalous data. Finally, a pseudo-data-driven adaptive thresholding method is proposed. This method incorporates physical information noise to dynamically adjust the detection boundary, allowing the model to adapt to changing detection criteria in multi-sensor and time-series data environments. Experimental validation using both a truss bridge model dataset and the Z24 bridge benchmark dataset demonstrates that STVR-DeSVDD outperforms traditional methods in anomaly detection, showcasing its substantial potential for practical applications.

title: A novel tool wear and remaining useful life prediction network based on multi-scale time–frequency information of milling force
abstract: Tool wear and remaining useful life (RUL) monitoring technology plays a crucial role in enhancing machining quality and reducing production costs.
