Nevertheless, prevailing methodologies predominantly focus on utilizing models to automatically extract features directly from temporal signal data, often overlooking the rich time–frequency information inherent within these signals, thus compromising the prediction accuracy of the models. Research indicates that time–frequency information associated with tool wear in cutting force signals is primarily concentrated within the vicinity of the tool’s rotational fundamental frequency and its harmonics. Therefore, this study proposes a network architecture (SRT-MFF-TWPN) for tool wear and RUL prediction based on multi-scale time–frequency information. Initially, the one-dimensional (1D) cutting force signals are transformed into two-dimensional (2D) time–frequency representations (TFR) through the Synchro-Reassigning Transform (SRT) to enhance the feature representation capability of the data. Concurrently, the Multi-Frequency Focusing (MFF) module is employed to automatically extract time–frequency features localized at the tool’s rotational fundamental frequency and its harmonics. The extracted time–frequency features are input as multi-channel features into the 1D convolutional neural network based on the DenseNet architecture, with the SE block adjusting channel weights to improve the model’s predictive capability. Finally, validation tests conducted on both the PHM2010 benchmark dataset and a self-constructed dataset demonstrate that, for identical backbone networks, data processed with the SRT-MFF method yields a marked improvement in the model’s predictive capability for tool wear and RUL.

title: An innovative diagnostic method for lubricant faults with multiple contaminants in journal bearings using acoustic emissions
abstract: In journal bearings, early and reliable detection of lubricant contamination is critical for fault diagnosis and condition-based maintenance. Acoustic emission (AE) technology, as a nondestructive testing method, can capture the minute energy releases associated with bearing faults and thus offers clear advantages for early fault monitoring in rotating machinery. Focusing on particulate and water contamination in journal-bearing lubricants, this paper proposes an AE signal processing and diagnosis framework that combines the Enhanced Feature Mode Decomposition (EFMD), Robust Median Difference (RMD), Adaptive Huber Synchrosqueezing Transform (AHST), and a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN). The EFMD builds on conventional FMD by introducing adaptive spectral-peak-based subband segmentation and a correlated-kurtosis-gain early-stopping mechanism, and, when combined with the RMD, enables the selection of frequency bands that carry the most fault-relevant information. The AHST leverages higher-order phase correction, Huber-loss-based adaptive weighting, and energy-driven smoothing windows to improve the accuracy of instantaneous-frequency estimation and the time–frequency energy concentration under noisy conditions. Comparative experiments conducted at rotational speeds of 900, 1200, and 1500 r/min under various particle and water contamination levels show that the EFMD-RMD-AHST scheme achieves higher and more stable classification performance on the tested platform, with average recognition accuracies exceeding 99 % for particle contamination and ranging from 98.30 % to 99.19 % for water contamination, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency under the considered operating conditions.

title: Data-driven diagnosis of wind turbines based on structural response data using environmental and operational conditions normalization and soft assignment methods
abstract: Data-driven structural health monitoring (SHM) frameworks are becoming an important part of the SHM practice due to ease of data collection and processing. Normalization of structural response data with respect to environmental and operational conditions (EOCs) is critically important for these data-driven frameworks as they do not use any baseline physical model and make predictions solely based on observations used in training. A key issue in real world experimental datasets collected for SHM is the lower quality of EOCs data available compared to structural response data. In this work, a strategy is proposed to extract features that correlate with EOCs from the high-quality structural response data. To do so, a mechanical model of the structure without and with structural damage is built and the response of the structure is simulated under different EOCs. Structural response features are regressed against EOCs and those that correlate with EOCs and are insensitive to structural damage are used for EOCs data normalization. Furthermore, a new approach based on soft assignment is introduced for EOCs data normalization and its performance is evaluated relative to the existing state of the art clustering in EOCs space approach. The efficiency of proposed methodologies is evaluated using the experimental and simulation datasets from a small scale research wind turbine located at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL).

title: Fault-tolerant path planning for cable-driven manipulators based on a diffusion strategy
abstract: Cable-driven manipulators often perform tasks in radiation, toxic, high-temperature and high-pressure environments. In such conditions, cable wear or failure cannot be addressed on-site. To address operational safety issues arising from cable abrasion in these scenarios, this study proposes a physics-informed diffusion policy framework for fault-tolerant path planning of cable-driven manipulators. Given the hyper-redundant degrees of freedom in cable-driven manipulators, the system can redistribute loads and continue functioning despite cable damage. First, a virtual-work-based cable tension estimation network embedding physical constraints is developed to achieve high-accuracy tension prediction corresponding to joint postures. Subsequently, tension guidance is integrated into the denoising diffusion model, leveraging collision-free reference trajectories as priors, thus iteratively generating fault-tolerant trajectories in high-dimensional joint spaces that satisfy both low-tension and obstacle avoidance constraints. Multidimensional experiments evaluating tension prediction accuracy, path feasibility, and algorithm scalability demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces average tension in damaged cables while ensuring path safety, achieving a planning time of only 9.7 s. Furthermore, the method maintains stable convergence and low jitter even with up to three damaged cables. Experimental results validate the algorithm’s effectiveness in fault-tolerant path planning for cable-driven manipulators, presenting a promising new paradigm for continuous and reliable operations in extreme environments.

title: Semi-supervised structural damage classification with constrained Bayesian nonparametric mixture models and transmissibility-guided knowledge transfer
abstract: AI-driven structural damage diagnosis based on vibration responses, such as transmissibility functions (TFs), has attracted increasing attention recently. However, unsupervised methods are primarily limited to damage detection, while supervised methods are often restricted by the scarcity of well-annotated training data from various damage scenarios. To bridge this gap, this work proposes a semi-supervised learning framework for TF-based structural damage classification by integrating constrained Dirichlet process mixture models (DPMMs) with a novel knowledge transfer technique. The constrained DPMM is introduced for clustering to identify discriminative information within the training set, which captures different patterns of structural behavior based on the statistical properties of TFs. A constraint-aware truncation-free variational inference method is developed to estimate the posterior of the constrained DPMM, which incorporates human supervision into the inference process through pairwise constraints. The discriminative information learned by the constrained DPMM, embedded within the cluster assignments, is used to pretrain a deep neural network (DNN), aiming to leverage the representation learning capability of DNNs to automatically extract discriminative features from raw TFs. To map these discriminative features to diagnostic class labels corresponding to actual structural conditions, a knowledge transfer technique is proposed, which replaces the pretrained DNN’s output layer with a sub-network and finetunes it using labeled training data to form a new DNN for damage classification. This semi-supervised learning framework utilizes deep learning to avoid manual feature extraction while reducing the amount of labeled data required to train the deep classifier by leveraging the knowledge acquired by the constrained DPMM. These attributes make it well-suited for structural damage classification, where labeled training data are scarce and unlabeled data are more accessible. Two case studies demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms some state-of-the-art approaches, owing to the constrained DPMM’s ability to capture different patterns of structural behavior within the training set and the effective mapping from these patterns to diagnostic class labels through the knowledge transfer technique.

title: Simulation and interpretable learning co-driven framework for multi-objective seismic monitoring of substation equipment
abstract: Electrical equipment in substations subjected to earthquakes typically exhibits brittle damage at multiple vulnerable sections, but the exact positions on the sections are unpredictable. Relevant standards and research raise the importance of the stress response levels in seismic assessment. However, monitoring all strains at the vulnerable sections necessitates lots of strain sensors for each equipment, which is impractical because of the extensive quantity of equipment in a substation, and the strong electromagnetic interference induced by the equipment. Therefore, this paper proposes a simulation and learning co-driven prediction framework to identify multi-objective monitoring schemes. It develops multiple machine learning (ML) models to predict peak stress at multiple vulnerable sections by inputting easily-monitored responses (MRs). In which, the simulation model is cooperated to acquire precise response data, addressing the scarcity of actual samples due to the absence of monitoring systems and the limited number of earthquakes. Then, it ranks the importance of MRs for each ML model using the Shapley additive explanation method, and combines the important MRs of various ML models through the proposed Intersection, Union, or Stack strategies. The combined MRs facilitate the reconstruction of ML models, which are subsequently implemented at the site to monitor responses for post-earthquake efficient predictions. A case study on a high-voltage transformer bushing is performed. Shaking table tests validate the efficacy of the obtained monitoring schemes in both intact and damaged scenarios, revealing the practicality of applying the proposed framework to efficiently identify damage to substation equipment after earthquakes.

title: MLG-Net: A hybrid framework for bridge cable damage identification using acoustic emission technology
abstract: Bridge cables are critical load-bearing components that transfer the weight of the main beam and deck in cable-stayed bridges. To ensure safe operation and effective maintenance, real-time monitoring of cable integrity is essential. Acoustic emission (AE) technology provides an effective means of real-time damage monitoring; however, distinguishing broken wire signals from noise remains a challenge, particularly in complex operational environments. To address this issue, this paper proposes a deep learning framework that integrates conventional manual features temporal feature with a long short-term memory (LSTM) autoencoder, and spatial feature extraction using graph convolutional networks (GCN): MLG-Net (manual LSTM GCN-Net). First, AE signals are collected from full-scale bridge cable breakage experiments, and conventional manual features are extracted. Next, a long short-term memory autoencoder captures the temporal evolution of AE signals, while a graph convolutional network leverages spatial correlations among multi-sensor AE data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 99.4% accuracy, 99.0% recall, and a 99.2% F1 score, significantly outperforming conventional classifiers. This study highlights the potential of integrating manual and deep learning-based feature extraction for bridge cable health monitoring and provides a foundation for future research on real-world AE-based structural health assessment.

title: Multimodal-based model for asynchronous motor fault diagnosis under noisy and variable operating conditions: a novel hybrid approach
abstract: Motors are pivotal in modern industry, especially as global demand for automation and smart manufacturing surges. Accurate fault diagnosis is crucial for stability maintenance, but existing approaches lack satisfactory accuracy and efficiency. This study integrates the multi-scale Convolution Neural Network (MSCNN),Bidirectional Mogrifier-Gated Recurrent Unit (BiMGRU), and Multi-head Attention Mechanism (MHAM) to propose a multimodal-based hybrid model of MSCNN-BiMGRU + MHAM for asynchronous motor fault diagnosis. The MSCNN channel is responsible for spatial feature extraction, and the BiMGRU channel is responsible for temporal feature extraction. While MHAM is responsible for efficient integration and extraction of multimodal features. Furthermore, to refine the model’s performance, an enhanced whale optimization algorithm (EWOA) is innovatively presented and embedded during model training, systematically optimizing hyperparameters to boost model generalization and training effectiveness. Numerous validations are conducted by the real vibration datasets of asynchronous motor gathered under noisy and various operating conditions. Compared to traditional approaches and the current mainstream deep learning models, the proposed hybrid model with EWOA optimization attains the impressive prediction accuracy. It delivers an effective and efficient approach to tackle the issues of motor fault diagnosis.

title: Federated Open-Set Fault Diagnosis for Unknown Bearing Fault Detection
abstract: Deep learning improves the accuracy of fault diagnosis. In traditional centralized training approaches, it often requires centralizing a large amount of labeled data across multiple clients, which is impeded by privacy and security constraints. Federated learning addresses this challenge by enabling collaborative model training without sharing raw data. However, most existing federated fault diagnosis methods focus on the closed-set assumption and cannot handle unseen faults that may occur in industrial environments. To this end, we propose a Federated Open-Set Fault Diagnosis (FOSFD) method. Specifically, during the training phase, the proposed method enhances the decision boundaries of the global model by generating augmented features locally using MixUp-based data augmentation strategy and aligning prototypes of known categories through the central server. During the testing phase, anomaly scores based on distances between testing samples’ feature representations and prototypes are computed to identify known or unknown faults. Experiments on Case Western Reserve University and Paderborn University bearing fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in terms of accuracy (Acc), area under the curve (AUC), and open set classification rate (OSCR), thereby delivering superior unknown-fault detection.

title: Adaptive filtering and multi-scale MixStyle network for cross-domain fault diagnosis of marine electric thruster bearings
abstract: Variations in operational conditions and noise interference deteriorate the performance of intelligent fault diagnosis models for marine electric thruster bearings. To address this challenge, we propose an adaptive filtering and multi-scale mixStyle network for cross-domain fault diagnosis of marine electric thruster bearings (AFMM). First, the multiscale attention-based MixStyle framework with multi-scale attention is developed based on MixStyle, which explicitly combines multi-scale decomposition and attention mechanisms to capture hierarchical fault patterns. Furthermore, to mitigate noise amplification in random feature mixing, a Hybrid Adaptive Filter is proposed, combining the frequency-domain selectivity of Butterworth filters with the dynamic adaptability of deep neural networks. Additionally, a source domain prototype refinement strategy is developed and combined with JMMD to achieve cross-domain fault diagnosis. Finally, extensive validation experiments are conducted by integrating the developed marine electric thruster simulation platform. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits significant noise robustness and cross-domain fault diagnosis accuracy.

title: A Multi-scale attention fusion framework based on KAN for rolling mill fault diagnosis
abstract: Three challenges remain in the area of rolling mill fault diagnosis: (1) Existing deep learning methods often struggle to extract key fault information; (2) Redundant fault features can interfere with models; (3) The existing multi-source information fusion models seldom study the complementarity of different modal characteristics. These challenges not only lead to an increase in defective steel products but also may cause production accidents during the operation, ultimately affecting the normal production of steel by enterprises. To solve these challenges, the study proposes a multi-scale attention fusion framework based on KAN (MAFF-KAN) for rolling mill fault diagnosis. Firstly, the dual shock feature approach is proposed to extract shock characteristics from signals. Secondly, KAN is first used in the field of multi-sensor-based rolling mill fault diagnosis to boost the effectiveness of the model. Additionally, KAN is used to develop the feature enhancement module that improves the rolling mill’s fault characteristics. Then, a multi-level parallel attention fusion improvement structure is suggested to achieve incremental fusion and utilization from shallow to deep fusion characteristics. The effectiveness of the suggested approach is validated by two case studies. The findings demonstrate that MAFF-KAN is superior to existing fault diagnosis methods and has better diagnostic capability.

title: A novel multi-scale dense residual shrinkage GAN for data-limited rotating machinery fault diagnosis
abstract: Fault diagnosis of rotating machinery is crucial for industrial safety, yet practical applications face significant challenges, including high data acquisition costs, scarce fault samples, and severe class imbalance, which severely limit the performance of deep learning diagnostic models. This paper proposes a multi-scale dense residual shrinkage generative adversarial network (MDRS-GAN) specifically designed to address fault diagnosis under limited data conditions. The method innovatively introduces a multi-scale generator that employs multiple sub-generators working collaboratively with a multi-head attention mechanism to achieve dynamic fusion of multi-scale features, significantly enhancing sample distribution simulation capabilities. Simultaneously, a hybrid time–frequency discriminator based on dense-block deep residual shrinkage networks is constructed, integrating dense connections, an improved efficient channel attention mechanism, and soft-thresholding denoising techniques to enhance sensitivity to critical features in both time and frequency domains, achieving dual functionality of sample authenticity recognition and fault classification. Additionally, a Bayesian optimization strategy is introduced to adaptively adjust discriminator hyperparameters, improving model training stability and efficiency. Extensive experiments on CWRU and XJTU-SY bearing datasets demonstrate that: generated samples achieve feature distribution similarity exceeding 0.8 (maximum 0.91) with real samples; under extreme small-sample conditions (only 2 samples per class), fault diagnosis accuracies reach 94.32% and 95.83% respectively; under severe class imbalance (100:1), accuracies maintain at 96.46% and 96.06%. Compared with existing methods, MDRS-GAN shows significant advantages across all evaluation metrics, providing an effective solution for data-limited rotating machinery fault diagnosis in industrial scenarios.

title: Order-adaptive subspace scale learning for unsupervised anomaly detection under time-varying rotational speed conditions
abstract: Under time-varying speeds, rotating machinery experiences pronounced dynamic effects, making this operational phase highly susceptible to faults. Anomaly detection under such non-stationary condition is challenging, as speed-induced distribution shifts in vibration signals often lead conventional methods to mistake normal variations for faults, resulting in false alarms. Although data driven methods aim to learn speed-invariant representations, its generalization to unseen speed profiles remains limited. To address this, we propose a physics-informed Order-Adaptive Subspace Scale Learning (OASSL) method that integrates order tracking grounded in the physical relationship between vibration harmonics and shaft rotation. This approach resamples time-domain signals into the angular domain to generate unified order-frequency features, considerably eliminating the influence of speed fluctuations. Furthermore, a novel multi-subspace sampling and subspace scale learning strategy is introduced within the network, which enhances the extraction of subtle fault signatures and improves robustness against varying operating conditions. Experimental results on time-varying speed datasets demonstrate that the proposed OASSL significantly outperforms existing methods in reducing false alarms and accurately identifying faults under complex speed variations.

title: Terahertz characterization of internal debonding defects of composites under class imbalance condition using lightweight network
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology, a promising alternative to traditional non-destructive testing (NDT) methods, emerges great potential for quantitative characterization of debonding defect in Glass Fiber Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) composites. However, during the intelligent identification of debonding defects inside composite, there are challenges with class imbalance in THz datasets leading to reduced accuracy, and traditional deep learning models struggle to balance classification precision with inference speed. Therefore, a lightweight THz three-dimensional characterization system based on Ghost Bottleneck Attention Module Network (GBAMNet) for THz class-imbalanced dataset is proposed to ultimately achieve the automatic characterization of hidden debonding defect inside GFRP. Ghost layer convolution and Bottleneck Attention Module (BAM) modules are specially designed to capture essential features from the raw THz signals with a low computational cost, and thus realizing real-time, high-accuracy categorization of THz signals. The ghost feature factor s is introduced to control the number of ghost feature mappings generated by linear transformations within the Ghost layer, increasing the quantity of feature mappings in the network to enhance representational capabilities with minimal computational and parameter overhead. Moreover, the Gradient Harmonizing Mechanism (GHM) Loss function addresses the class-imbalance issue by dynamically adjusting the gradient weights of each sample to achieve a balanced gradient distribution. The comprehensive performance of GBAMNet with respect to classification accuracy and inference velocity are validated by a series of experiments on the class-imbalanced dataset. Overall, our proposed system will promote the actual applications of Terahertz non-destructive testing (THz NDT) scenarios for automatic and real-time defect characterization.

title: Two-stage autoencoder reconstruction based unsupervised delamination imaging using laser sensed wavefields
abstract: Delamination quantification using guided wavefields has gained attention due to the high sensitivity of ultrasonic guided waves and advances in wavefield scanning. Although supervised deep learning enhances wavefield analysis, its application is limited by the high cost of large-scale labeling. Semi-supervised approaches alleviate this issue but still depend on curated, defect-free reference data. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes an unsupervised framework that integrates Convolutional Autoencoders (CAE) with guided wavefields, requiring neither labels nor historical data. The framework enables delamination quantification from a single wavefield snapshot captured when direct waves fully cover the inspection region. It leverages neural networks’ tendency to overfit dominant healthy patterns, causing poor reconstruction in delaminated areas. The snapshot is divided into uniform patches and symmetrically flipped to enhance data diversity. Each patch is independently reconstructed by the CAE, and a pixel-wise reconstruction error map highlights delamination regions as high-error zone. A two-stage training strategy further reinforces healthy-region reconstruction. Experiments on scanning laser Doppler vibrometer data validate the effectiveness of the augmentation scheme, the two-stage strategy, and the framework’s robustness to varying defect shapes and locations. Overall, the proposed method provides a practical and robust solution for wavefield-based delamination detection without pre-collected or labeled data.

title: MS-DAWCAE: multi-scale deep adversarial wavelet convolutional autoencoder toward unseen fault diagnosis with limited data
abstract: Deep learning has achieved rapid development in mechanical fault diagnosis. However, it still faces challenges in practical applications due to limited fault samples and the emergence of unseen fault types. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Deep Adversarial Wavelet Convolutional Autoencoder (MS-DAWCAE) for unseen fault detection and known fault diagnosis in small-sample scenarios. The model first integrates wavelet scattering transformation with multi-scale convolutional encoding to extract hierarchical features that capture both local anomalies and global structural patterns, thereby improving reconstruction of known categories and enlarging reconstruction errors for unknown faults. Accordingly, a collaborative adversarial learning module with dual discriminators is then designed to regulate latent representations and supervise reconstruction quality, effectively compressing intra-class variations and enhancing separability between known and unknown categories. Furthermore, a fully connected classifier is incorporated into a multi-task framework to enable accurate identification of known faults while maintaining sensitivity to novel ones. Extensive experiments on industrial datasets demonstrate that, compared with advanced machine learning and transfer learning–based methods, MS-DAWCAE achieved an F1 score of at least 0.90 on the FST dataset under various operating conditions. Moreover, on a publicly available centrifugal pump dataset, MS-DAWCAE outperforms the optimal method by 15%–25% under small-sample settings, validating its effectiveness, robustness, and scalability for practical industrial fault diagnosis.

title: Maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network for rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios
abstract: Achieving cross-domain remaining useful life (RUL) prediction, improves efficiency of RUL prediction in ensuring the reliability of mechanical equipment. However, current research mainly focuses on single cross-domain scenario such as cross-working conditions, while few studies concerning applicability for multiple cross-domain scenarios. In practical applications, the challenge of extracting domain-invariant features caused by diverse data distribution discrepancies accompanying multiple cross-domain scenarios, coupled with the inherent limitations of existing methodological frameworks, limits the generalization performance and application efficiency of current cross-domain RUL prediction methods. Therefore, this paper proposes a maximum prediction discrepancy domain adaptation network (MP2DAN), to achieve rolling bearing RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios. In MP2DAN, to address the performance limitation under multiple cross-domain scenarios, a maximum prediction discrepancy (MPD) domain adaptation (DA) approach is proposed. Leveraging the correlation between decision boundaries of different RULs and target domain samples, MPD flexibly learns domain-invariant feature representations from diverse data distribution discrepancies, through a three-stage adversarial training designed between the feature extractor and two RUL predictors. Then, drawing on the characteristics of MPD framework, a synergistic adversarial self-supervised learning (SASL) approach is designed, which aims to empower the target domain to promote MPD in achieving DA, and constrain the feature generation of target domain to ensure the effectiveness of prediction results through knowledge transfer and self-supervised learning. Finally, the ablation and comparative experiments are performed on three bearing datasets. Through the performance quantification and visualization analysis, it is verified that MP2DAN can effectively and generically realize RUL prediction under multiple cross-domain scenarios.

title: GC-TimeGAN: Time–frequency domain model for high-fidelity reconstruction of Maglev track irregularity
abstract: Track irregularity is one of the primary sources of vibration disturbances in maglev trains, and its precise modeling is critical to improving simulation model fidelity and optimizing controller design. This paper proposes a model for modeling high-speed maglev track irregularity that integrates both time domain and frequency domain, namely the globally conditioned time series generative adversarial network (GC-TimeGAN). The model captures the complexity of track irregularity comprehensively by conditioning on frequency spectrum information, which is relevant to engineering applications. It generates high-speed maglev track irregularity data that align with the spectral characteristics of the track. Experimental results demonstrate that GC-TimeGAN outperforms traditional methods and other generative models in terms of modeling accuracy and feature consistency. This research provides a more accurate and practical modeling approach for track irregularity data generation, with direct relevance to engineering applications.

title: Decoupling the feature manifold structure: a domain incremental method for mechanical fault diagnosis under variable rotational speeds
abstract: Fault diagnosis of typical rotating machinery is of great significance for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of mechanical equipment. Machine learning-based intelligent diagnosis methods have achieved significant progress, but most existing approaches suffer from catastrophic forgetting and lack the ability to incrementally adapt to new operating conditions. To address this challenge, a domain-incremental fault diagnosis method with decoupled feature manifold structures (DFMS) is proposed for mechanical equipment operating under variable rotational speeds. In the proposed framework, although the physical fault types remain unchanged, vibration signals corresponding to the same fault exhibit significantly different data distributions under different rotational speeds, which can be interpreted as domain-dependent latent manifolds. To explicitly model these variations, vibration signals are first transformed into feature representations, and fault features acquired under different operating conditions are then mapped into fault-domain-specific latent subspaces using an autoencoder-based manifold representation. The reconstruction error is employed as a distance metric to characterize the proximity between an input feature and the corresponding fault-domain manifold. Furthermore, an adaptive weighted confusion contrast loss is designed to reduce classification ambiguity caused by manifold overlap across different domains. To alleviate catastrophic forgetting during incremental learning, a knowledge distillation loss with dynamic parameter adjustment is introduced to preserve the reconstruction-error distributions of previously learned fault-domain manifolds, and a feature distillation loss is employed to stabilize latent representations across incremental stages. The proposed DFMS method is applicable to fault diagnosis tasks under quasi-stationary operating conditions, such as constant-speed or piecewise constant-speed scenarios. Extensive experiments conducted on a gear transmission test rig and a high-speed wheelset bearing test rig demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method for domain-incremental fault diagnosis of typical rotating machinery under variable rotational speed conditions.

title: Dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network guided by lamb wave physics for damage localization
abstract: Lamb wave technology has become a powerful tool in composite structural health monitoring, enabling the detection and characterization of internal damage. However, the pronounced anisotropy of composite structures gives rise to intricate spatiotemporal correlations among multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Existing methods typically treat these signals as independent Euclidean sequences, which restricts their capacity to capture the coupling characteristics across multiple channels. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a novel damage localization approach based on a dual-stream spatiotemporal graph attention network (DS-STGAT), which is explicitly grounded in the physical principles of Lamb wave propagation. First, a Lamb wave graph is constructed using transfer entropy (TE) and time-of-flight (ToF), providing a graphical representation of multi-channel Lamb wave signals. Second, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) and a graph attention network (GAT) are employed to extract temporal and spatial features, respectively. Third, a bidirectional cross-attention (BCA) module is introduced to fuse spatiotemporal information, while damage localization regression is subsequently conducted using a multi-layer perceptron mixer (MLP-Mixer). Finally, experimental evaluations on simulated damage in composite plate structures demonstrate that DS-STGAT achieves superior damage localization performance, significantly outperforming existing benchmark methods.

title: Enhancing interpretability via fine-grained objectives: A manifold-learning structured model for fault diagnosis of rolling bearings under noisy conditions
abstract: Dictionary learning (DL) has emerged as an effective data-driven approach for fault diagnosis due to its powerful sparse representation capability. However, its application to rolling bearing fault diagnosis still faces several challenges, including low accuracy, vulnerability of sparse reconstruction to strong noise interference, and insufficient discriminative power of the encoding. To address the above challenges, we propose a bearing fault diagnosis method based on a dual-analysis dictionary learning (DADL) with non-local sparsity (NLS) and block-diagonal (BD). The proposed method introduces a NLS term to characterize the underlying geometric manifold structure of the samples, aiming to extract key class-discriminative features under strong noise conditions. In addition, a BD term is incorporated to constrain the encoding into structured and discriminative sparse subspaces, with the goal of constructing features that are more easily recognized by the classifier. The proposed method maps the two learned constraints into a first analysis dictionary and a second analysis dictionary, respectively. For test samples, diagnostic results can be obtained through a simple projection operation, making the process more computationally efficient. In addition, the dual-analysis dictionary not only mines the essential features of the data, but also encourages the sub-analysis dictionary to learn more refined and interpretable feature subspaces. Finally, a linear classifier is jointly trained to perform the fault identification task. Extensive experiments on three challenging bearing fault datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high average diagnostic accuracies. In addition, comparative results with several advanced DL methods further demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed method.

title: A knowledge fusion-driven domain generalization diagnosis framework for unseen operating conditions
abstract: In engineering applications, deep learning-based fault diagnosis must balance generalization and model complexity amid dynamic conditions. High generalization often demands complex models, yet excessive complexity reduces computational efficiency and hinders deployment. To address this, we propose Multi-knowledge Domain Generalization with Dynamic Temperature Distillation (MDG-DTD), a knowledge fusion-driven framework. First, we introduce a distillation method that fuses multiple specialized teacher models via confidence weighting and feature alignment to derive a generalized teacher model. Second, a dynamic temperature distillation strategy integrates attention transfer and adversarial temperature regulation to adaptively adjust the distillation process, optimizing student model learning and efficiency. Experimental results on the motor current and industrial robot vibration datasets validate MDG-DTD’s superiority over existing domain generalization methods in diagnosing faults under unseen conditions. Notably, the student model, using only 0.15% of the teacher model’s parameters and 0.36% of its floating point operations, retains at least 96.33% and 97.78% of its performance, respectively.

title: Physics-guided residual correction model for monitoring machining deviations of complex thin-walled parts considering spatial–temporal dynamics
abstract: Machining deviation of complex thin-walled parts critically affects the product performance and stability. However, accurate deviation monitoring is significantly challenged by the complexity of the processing environment. Traditional theoretical models are computationally expensive, while existing deep learning methods often operate as black-box models with limited interpretability. To address these challenges, this study proposes a spatial–temporal physics-guided residual correction model (ST-PGRC), which integrates the theoretical machining deviation model with a Transformer-based learning module. Initially, a theoretical deviation model is established through machining dynamics and kinematics analysis. A spatial–temporal mapping module links vibration signals with the toolpath, converting temporal information into spatially meaningful features. Ultimately, the Transformer encoder learns the residuals between theoretical results and experimental results through its global attention mechanism, capturing the interactions between the theoretical model and spatial–temporal features and subsequently correcting the theoretical deviations. Experiments on thin-walled workpieces demonstrate that ST-PGRC achieves an RMSE of 0.0069 mm and reduces monitoring error by at least 22.5% compared with physics-guided neural networks, residual networks, and purely data-driven neural networks. The proposed method offers a reliable and interpretable solution for machining deviation monitoring.

title: Using implicit correlations among synchronized vibration signals from pixels to improve the accuracy of structural damage detection
abstract: In recent years, deep neural networks have been used increasingly to process vibration signals for detecting structural damage. However, the effectiveness of deep neural networks relies on having many vibration signals, which are difficult to acquire in practical engineering scenarios. To address this limitation, a phase-based motion estimation (PME) technique has been introduced, which treats each pixel as an independent sensor, enabling the extraction of millions of vibration signals from a single video. PME not only provides sufficient training data for deep neural networks but also ensures that the signals obtained from multiple pixels are perfectly synchronized in the temporal domain. The implicit correlations among synchronized signals from multiple pixels (i.e., pixel-dependencies) have the potential to enhance damage detection. However, it remains challenging to use the pixel-dependencies effectively to facilitate damage detection. To address this issue, a multi-feature-attention network is proposed. Innovatively, the contribution of pixel-dependencies to damage detection is quantified. By assigning greater attention weights to pixel-dependencies with greater contributions, the network achieves a substantial improvement in damage detection performance. The effectiveness of the proposed method was validated by successfully detecting subtle bolt looseness in a steel structure, showcasing its superior performance in structural damage detection tasks.

title: A hidden failure state identification method for steel-spring floating slab track isolators using MVFuseNet
abstract: Isolators in steel-spring floating slab track (SS-FST) systems can suffer from hidden failures, such as fractures and fluid leakage, which may lead to safety risks like train derailments. However, research on fault modeling and failure state identification is limited. This paper proposes MVFuseNet, a fault-diagnosis framework for identifying failure states of steel-spring isolators. The framework constructs a dataset from multi-source vibration signals generated from field wheel-drop tests and simulations, ensuring high-quality data for classification. In addition, a novel time–frequency feature extraction method based on phase-coupled time–frequency analysis (PC-TFA) enhances damage-sensitive features, while a multi-channel phase-enhanced variational decomposition (MC-PEVD) method generates robust inputs for deep learning. Finally, an improved deep residual network is used for high-precision classification of failure states. Experimental results show that MVFuseNet outperforms existing methods in feature representation and classification accuracy, providing valuable support for the safe operation of SS-FST systems.

title: DHFGAT: A dynamic heterogeneous fusion graph attention network for early gearbox fault detection
abstract: Accurate detection of early faults in industrial gearboxes is a critical but challenging task, particularly under dynamic operating conditions. Converting multi-sensor signals into graph-structured data via Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) offers a framework based on signal correlation modeling. However, the efficacy of this approach hinges on the quality of the graph structure, which is generally compromised by suboptimal construction methods and the inclusion of redundant features. To address these challenges, this study proposes a heterogeneous data fusion framework named Dynamic Heterogeneous Fusion Graph Attention Network (DHFGAT). Specifically, the current signal is first preprocessed to align its data morphology with the vibration signal. Then, to construct an information-rich graph structure, the Regularized Dual Averaging (RDA) algorithm adaptively selects the key feature subsets of the signal, thereby suppressing interference from redundant features. Subsequently, a training architecture that integrates the Spiking Neural Encoder (SNE) with the Simplified Graph Attention Network (SGAT) is adopted to achieve accurate and robust feature fusion and fault classification. Finally, extensive experiments were conducted on a test rig with eight fault types. The results demonstrate that DHFGAT achieves maximum average detection accuracies of 99.59% and 98.36% under constant and variable speed conditions, respectively. The proposed method provides a robust, reliable solution for early gearbox fault detection and offers insights into the optimal sensor combination for complex industrial scenarios.

title: Knowledge-guided RUL prediction for multi-sensor devices under a data-model interactive framework
abstract: For complex industrial devices monitored by multi-sensors, accurate and reliable remaining useful life (RUL) prediction directly determines the effectiveness and economy of preventive maintenance strategies. Current mainstream methods either rely excessively on data-driven models, resulting in the lack of physical interpretability, or are limited by fixed knowledge constraints, making it difficult to adapt to the dynamic characteristics of multi-sensor data. To address this, this paper proposes a knowledge-guided RUL prediction method under a data-model interactive framework. Specifically, based on the composite health indicator (CHI) constructed by weighted fusion of multi-sensor monitoring data and the RUL predicted by stochastic degradation modeling under the concepts of first hitting time (FHT), an optimization objective function integrating RUL prediction accuracy, monotonicity, and slope consistency is designed. This forms a feedback loop for knowledge-guided CHI construction and stochastic degradation modeling, enabling optimal adjustment of fusion coefficients for multi-sensor data and failure thresholds corresponding to CHI. Thus, dual optimization of the accuracy and physical rationality of prediction results is achieved. Meanwhile, a Bayesian update method for degradation model parameters is proposed to realize online RUL prediction and quantification of prediction uncertainty. Finally, the advantages of the proposed method in improving RUL prediction accuracy, interpretability, and generalization are verified based on the C-MAPSS dataset and milling cutters dataset.

title: A physical knowledge-informed bearing fault feature extraction network based on Mamba
abstract: In contrast to signal processing methods that depend extensively on significant domain expertise, deep learning offers end-to-end feature self-learning capabilities, thereby providing a promising option for rolling bearing fault diagnosis. However, supervised learning paradigms that rely on categorical labels predominantly capture class-discriminative features, potentially resulting in the omission of essential fault-specific information within the feature space and diminishing the interpretability of the model. Therefore, this paper proposes an interpretable weak fault feature extraction framework, named Mamba-FeNet, which integrates Mamba’s exceptional sequence modeling strengths with physical prior knowledge of bearing fault. Firstly, a modal information estimation algorithm based on the marginal spectrum is introduced to extract potential resonance parameters from the frequency domain. This algorithm guides the resonance frequency settings in the simulation model and generates fault template signals based on prior physical knowledge. Secondly, the Mamba-FeNet is designed to model the vibration signals using selective state space, achieving end-to-end extraction of fault features under the encode-mask-decode paradigm. Thirdly, fault impact template signals are combined with normal signals scaled randomly in amplitude to form mixed signals for training the Mamba-FeNet, and a multi-model information weighted fusion strategy is designed based on the Envelope Spectrum Kurtosis (ESK). Finally, an interpretable analysis visualizes Mamba-FeNet’s internal structure and variables to intuitively demonstrate the fault feature extraction process. The proposed method is validated through simulations and experimental signals, showing superior performance compared to several advanced signal processing methods and deep learning methods.

title: A Riemannian-Hyperbolic Space-Based Algorithm for multisensor data fusion in spline degradation monitoring
abstract: Spline wear threatens the reliability of mechanical transmission systems, but conventional monitoring fails to reconcile heterogeneous data, capture dynamic degradation, or delineate hierarchical states. Here we present a geometric deep learning framework for multisensor fusion: vibration (macroscopic dynamics) and acoustic emission (AE, microscopic damage) signals are encoded as symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices to form a Riemannian manifold. Log-Euclidean metrics and Riemannian means mitigate cross-modal misalignment, while an attention-based graph neural network (GATConv) fuses features to learn spatiotemporal dependencies. Fused representations are embedded into Poincaré ball space—leveraging hyperbolic geometry’s exponential volume growth to enhance hierarchical wear separability—with unsupervised clustering and temporal mapping enabling time-resolved monitoring. On industrial datasets (slewing bearing, spline wear), the framework consistently outperforms mainstream methods by achieving effective cross-modal alignment, superior clustering quality, and accurate full-cycle wear tracking. This work establishes a geometric deep learning paradigm for mechanical health monitoring, advancing predictive maintenance in critical engineering systems.

title: A novel mechanism-data dual-driven prediction method for tracking error in ultra-precision machining
abstract: The formation mechanism of tracking error in ultra-precision machining is highly complex, as it is influenced by multiple coupled factors.Traditional single-driven modeling methods—either mechanism-driven or data-driven—face inherent limitations: the former struggles to accurately capture the nonlinear dynamics of servo systems, while the latter suffers from poor interpretability.To fill this gap, this paper proposes a novel mechanism-data dual-driven tracking error prediction method. Firstly, a mechanism-driven prediction module for the deterministic physical components of tracking error is established based on servo control theory and parameter identification experiments. Then, based on the hybrid deep learning algorithm (TCN-BiLSTM-MHA), a data-driven module is developed to fit the unmodeled tracking error residuals. TCN and BiLSTM capture the long-term dependencies inherent in servo dynamics, while the MHA mechanism identifies key features and adaptively allocates their weights. Finally, a dual-driven prediction method is proposed by integrating the theoretical model with the residual prediction model. Experimental results demonstrate that compared with conventional single-driven methods, the proposed method achieves superior prediction accuracy, with a mean absolute error (MAE) as low as 0.000012 and a relative improvement of up to 65.71%. This work provides a reliable technical support for tracking error compensation and further improves the machining accuracy of optical components.

title: An unsupervised domain adaptive fault diagnosis for rotating machinery based on physical wavelet convolution and joint distribution alignment
abstract: Under the conditions of strong noise and small samples, the subtle fault features of rotating machinery are often obscured, and traditional deep learning methods face the challenges of poor interpretability and a heavy reliance on large labeled datasets. To address these issues, an unsupervised fault diagnosis method based on an asymmetric modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel convolutional neural network (AMGDWKCNN) is proposed. Firstly, an asymmetric modulation physical convolution layer (AMPConv) is designed. By employing an asymmetrically modulated Gaussian difference wavelet kernel, it matches the asymmetric impact characteristics of vibration signals, thereby enhancing the model’s physical interpretability. Secondly, a dynamic nonlinear noise reduction mechanism is constructed, which employs a dual-attention-guided flexible soft threshold function to adaptively suppress noise interference, while leveraging the KAN activation function to enhance the nonlinear expression capability of fault features. Finally, a joint distribution alignment module is proposed. By combining category-conditional second-order statistical matching loss with predictive entropy uncertainty metrics, it dynamically weights and aligns category semantics with global distributions, thereby enhancing the model’s generalization performance across operating conditions. Experimental validation conducted on two publicly available bearing datasets and a self-built gearbox dataset demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively extract subtle fault features under the scenarios with strong noise and small samples, achieving high accuracy and strong generalization.

title: A domain-correction framework for structural response reconstruction with imperfect FEM and sparse measurements
abstract: Deep learning for structural response reconstruction faces two fundamental barriers: scarce real-world data and the practical inevitability of imperfect finite element models (FEM). While FEM-generated data offer a solution, the systematic bias between simulation and reality is often overlooked, limiting generalization. This work proposes a domain-correction framework that strategically leverages this bias. We employ a minimally calibrated FEM as a biased simulator to pre-train a Bidirectional GRU network with Top-k sparse attention (BiGRU-SA), instilling physics-regularized priors. A Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) regularized transfer learning stage then actively corrects the simulation bias by aligning feature distributions, requiring only a tiny fraction of real data. Validated on a cantilever beam and a wind turbine blade, the framework demonstrates robust bias-correction capability. Crucially, despite significant time-domain discrepancies in the initial FEM, it achieves high-fidelity reconstruction (average R2 > 0.9966) using less than 20% of the available real data. This approach provides a practical and robust pathway for integrating deep learning into structural health monitoring under realistic constraints of model imperfection and data scarcity.

title: In-situ optical emission spectroscopy monitoring of laser powder bed fusion based on spectral data prior knowledge and feature-decision level fusion network
abstract: Porosity defects are common quality issues in Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) manufacturing. Optical emission spectroscopy (OES), a key technique that reflects the interaction between the laser and the material, has been widely used in laser processing monitoring. However, the spectral signals in the LPBF process are extremely weak and complex, and there is a lack of reliable OES monitoring approaches. To address these challenges, this study proposed an OES monitoring framework driven by spectral data prior knowledge. First, the spectral signals and plasma features of different porosity defects in the LPBF process were systematically analyzed, and the correlation between the process and spectral signals was explored, revealing the defect-related spectral features of both emission lines and the background continuous spectrum, along with their underlying physical mechanisms. Building on this, a physics-informed spectral signal-to-image mapping method was proposed, which converted high-dimensional spectral data into dual-channel spectral grayscale mapping images, thereby enhancing spectral features strongly correlated with defects. Finally, the MSI-FDFNet model was developed for in situ porosity monitoring during the LPBF process. Results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively extracts distinctive features from different spectral bands, achieving an accuracy of 95.51% in identifying multiple porosity defects, significantly outperforming models using only feature-level or decision-level fusion. Additionally, visualization analysis confirms that the model can adaptively focus on defect-sensitive key spectral band information, enabling reliable monitoring through multi-level fusion. This study highlights the potential of physics knowledge-driven OES monitoring for in-situ monitoring of the LPBF process.

title: Remaining useful life prediction of complex equipment based on adaptive dual-branch multi-scale feature fusion model
abstract: Precise Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is critical for ensuring the reliability and operational efficiency of complex equipment. However, existing data-driven methods are often limited by their inability to capture multi-scale degradation dynamics or sustain performance under fluctuating operating conditions. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Dual-Branch Multi-Scale Feature Fusion (ADB-MSF) framework. The architecture integrates a self-attention mechanism to elucidate inter-sensor correlations, followed by a multi-scale Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) that simultaneously captures transient anomalies and long-term degradation trends. A gated enhancement module is further incorporated to refine feature representations by highlighting informative features while suppressing irrelevant noise. Uniquely, the model features an adaptive dual-branch prediction module that dynamically activates the most appropriate prediction pathway based on the input degradation state, ensuring robustness in complex environments. Additionally, a weighted Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss function is introduced to prioritize prediction accuracy near the critical end-of-life phase. Extensive experiments on stratospheric airship and C-MAPSS datasets confirm that ADB-MSF yields superior predictive performance compared to existing state-of-the-art baselines.

title: IAA-CRL: A universal information-adaptive augmentation based contrastive representation learning framework for remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearings
abstract: Accurate degradation-state identification and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of rolling-element bearings are pivotal for predictive maintenance, yet these tasks are severely challenged by ambient noise, complex operating conditions, and the intrinsic non-linearity of the degradation process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel Introspective Adaptive Augmentation Contrastive Representation Learning (IAA-CRL) framework tailored for bearing RUL prognosis. IAA-CRL innovatively integrates contrastive learning with a dynamically optimized data-augmentation strategy. An augmentation selector is introduced to adaptively determine the optimal fusion of transformations from a physics-constrained candidate pool, ensuring that the generated samples preserve critical degradation semantics while maximizing diversity in a purely data-driven manner, without requiring prior domain knowledge for the fusion strategy. Furthermore, a multi-scale contrastive loss is devised to effectively fuse instance-level and timestamp-level features, thereby capturing discriminative degradation representations. The superiority of IAA-CRL has been empirically validated through comprehensive benchmarking on both the FEMTO-ST and XJTU-SY datasets. Compared with state-of-the-art methods (including CBHRL, USL, SimCLR, and SupCon) IAA-CRL yields significant improvements in prediction accuracy on the majority of bearing samples, demonstrating enhanced robustness and generalizability.

title: A dual-stage framework for industrial fault diagnosis under domain shift via enhanced voiceprint representation and hierarchical ensemble learning
abstract: While existing acoustic-based fault detection and diagnosis (AFDD) methods have achieved notable success, their performance in real industrial environments remains constrained by domain shifts, scarce fault samples, and limited computational resources. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight dual-stage framework that integrates enhanced voiceprint representation with hierarchical ensemble learning to achieve robust AFDD. First, an adaptive time–frequency feature modeling module is developed to construct enhanced local voiceprint representations from Mel spectrograms, effectively extracting fault-related acoustic patterns with improved discrimination and robustness under noisy and dynamic operating conditions. Second, a hierarchical ensemble learning strategy that integrates CatBoost, XGBoost, and logistic regression is designed to progressively refine the decision boundaries in the extracted feature space, thereby enhancing multi-level feature utilization, diagnostic stability, and decision process interpretability across different domains. Finally, extensive experiments on the DCASE 2022 Task 2 benchmark and a real-world power transformer dataset demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability compared to state-of-the-art AFDD approaches. Especially in various noise scenarios, the average diagnostic accuracy of the power transformer is improved by nearly 10%.

title: Model-data integration and visual transfer for small sample intelligent fault diagnosis of spindle thrust bearing
abstract: The demand for condition monitoring and stable operation of high-precision equipment such as machine tools has promoted the optimization of maintenance strategies. However, the traditional equipment signal acquisition and intelligent diagnosis framework faces double limitations, that is, the scarcity of historical bearing fault data seriously affects the accuracy of the diagnosis model based on deep learning, and the contact vibration measurement method is difficult to cope with the layout requirements of complex industrial environments. For this reason, an intelligent diagnosis workflow of model-data integration and visual transfer is proposed for the raceway fault of thrust bearing of machine tool spindle. Firstly, the dynamic model of four-degree-of-freedom contact bearing is established to generate displacement simulation data with rich characteristics. Secondly, a sub-pixel visual vibration measurement method is proposed to collect the displacement signal of real equipment operation. Finally, the dynamic simulation data is migrated to the visual displacement data diagnosis. To address the inherent limitations of simulated signals and the instability in model accuracy caused by domain shifts, we propose a Mutual Information − Domain Adversarial Network. By incorporating the key principles of minimal-redundancy-maximal-relevance from information theory, this approach significantly enhances the robustness and accuracy of domain adaptation tasks. The effectiveness of the proposed method and diagnostic workflow is validated and analyzed through six simulation-to-reality transfer tasks. Results demonstrate that the intelligent diagnostic framework based on model-data integration and visual transfer effectively addresses the under-sampling problem and improves fault diagnosis accuracy.

title: An interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery
abstract: Deep learning has achieved significant success in intelligent fault diagnosis owing to its powerful nonlinear mapping capabilities. However, the lack of interpretability of deep learning-based fault diagnosis methods with black-box characteristics has seriously hindered their widespread industrial application. To address this issue, an interpretable adaptive denoising convolutional network (IADC-Net) is proposed for intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machinery in this paper, which constructs a comprehensive interpretability framework. In this method, the interpretable signal processing layer is driven by adaptive fusion denoising wavelet convolution (AFDWC) module, enhancing the model’s generalization capabilities in various scenarios. The AFDWC integrated with multiple wavelet basis kernel can capture abundant multi-scale mechanical fault information. The adaptive soft threshold denoising (ASTD) dynamically removes noise interference on channel features, and the energy-entropy ratio channel weighting adaptively highlights frequency bands more relevant to faults. Then, the interpretable feature extraction layer leverages the sparse interaction characteristics of traditional convolutions to elucidate its intrinsic mathematical implications through sparse representation, which is of great significance to the engineering applications of various convolutional networks. And, the interpretable result analysis layer visualizes the model results with attention weight and output features to help users understand the decision process and trust diagnosis results. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified and analyzed by the public fault datasets and the industrial robot experimental platform, demonstrating the interpretability of model, the rationality of network structure and the superiority of diagnostic performance. The code library is available at: https://github.com/GTH25/IADC-Net.

title: Towards trustworthy milling chatter detection via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion
abstract: Chatter is an instability phenomenon in the milling process that may adversely affect surface quality and machining efficiency. To achieve high-performance machining, online chatter detection is of critical importance in mechanical manufacturing. However, existing methods primarily rely on signal processing techniques and single classifiers, which limits their interpretability and generalization capability, thereby resulting in untrustworthy detection results under variable cutting conditions. To deal with this limitation, this paper proposes a milling chatter detection method via physics-assisted feature extraction and stacking-based decision-level fusion. First, a physics-assisted feature extraction method is proposed to extract interpretable and discriminative features by modeling dynamic milling forces and characterizing the chatter evolution mechanism. Then, multiple deep learning-based classifiers are constructed as base models, including a convolutional neural network, a residual network, an Inception network, a capsule network, and a dilated convolutional network. Subsequently, a stacking ensemble learning based on XGBoost is designed to perform decision-level fusion of the outputs from these base models. Milling experiments are conducted to construct a dataset under different cutting conditions, and cross-validation is employed to demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

title: Open-set domain generalization residual feature reconstruction network for intelligent fault diagnosis under unknown time-varying working conditions
abstract: Currently, deep learning has garnered significant attention for addressing fault diagnosis challenges. However, in real-world industrial settings, the complexity of equipment and diversity of operating conditions can lead to unknown faults occurring under target conditions. Consequently, open-set domain generalization fault diagnosis (OSDGFD) has emerged as a critical research direction. However, existing open-set domain generalized fault diagnosis suffers from negative transfer, drastic changes in feature distributions under non-stationary time-varying rotational speed conditions, and insufficient revelation of fault features. These issues severely hinder performance research in open-set domain generalized fault diagnosis. Therefore, this paper proposes the Residual Feature Reconstruction Network for Intelligent Fault Diagnosis in Unknown Time-Varying Conditions (RFR-OSDG). First, a compact and reconstructable latent representation for known-class features is learned using known-class feature distribution mechanisms, while KL divergence constrains the normality of the latent distribution. Unknown classes, failing to conform to this distribution, exhibit larger reconstruction errors and are thus preliminarily distinguished. Building upon this foundation, an adaptive domain-aware class boundary loss constructs a dynamic decision boundary. This boundary constrains intra-class samples to remain within the boundary region while excluding out-of-class samples, thereby enhancing the model’s boundary recognition for known classes and reducing cross-class confusion and misclassification of unknown classes. By minimizing the triplet loss, the aggregation of similar features and the separation of dissimilar features are enhanced. An entropy-enhanced category-aware mechanism is designed to address the issue of inconsistent data distribution between the source domain and the target domain. Finally, experimental results under non-stationary time-varying speed show that the proposed method, RFR-OSDG, has better clustering and classification performance as well as superior generalization.

title: A hypergraph-enhanced state space model-Mamba framework for cross-domain response reconstruction guided by physical information
abstract: In data-driven structural response signal reconstruction tasks, the scarcity of high-quality, well-marked batch response data and the ambiguous spatial dependency patterns between response data constitute critical bottlenecks that constrain the performance of response reconstruction models. To address this challenge, this work proposes a novel cross-domain response reconstruction method based on a Hypergraph-enhanced Mamba (State Space Model) network (HeMamba) — a dual-stream framework that simultaneously processes temporal and spatial information. Specifically, the method utilizes the Mamba to capture long-term dynamic dependencies in multi-sensor signals, employs hypergraphs to model the higher-order spatial relationships among sensors, incorporates a designed two-layer Hypergraph Convolutional Network (HGCN) to capture their spatial dependency patterns, and additionally introduces a physics-based loss function derived from Power Spectral Density (PSD) to constrain the training process. Furthermore, a physics-informed transfer learning paradigm is introduced, wherein the model is pre-trained using finite element numerical simulation data. By freezing the spatial encoding module, the knowledge of structural physical response laws and intrinsic patterns learned by HeMamba is transferred to scenarios with limited real measured data for fine-tuning, thereby guiding the Mamba model to perform response signal reconstruction in the measured domain under physical constraints. Experiments on a tower steel structure indicate that the proposed method effectively alleviates the reconstruction accuracy degradation caused by data scarcity. With fine-tuning on a small amount of measured data, the reconstructed signals achieve an R2 value of 0.9798 and exhibit high-precision response reconstruction across the full frequency band, significantly outperforming baseline models trained directly. Notably, even under structural damage conditions, the proposed method still can transfer physical knowledge learned from the source domain to response reconstruction in the target domain. This study provides a feasible technical pathway for high-precision cross-domain response reconstruction under small-sample conditions.

title: Dynamics-guided disentangled hypersphere prototype for rotor system fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions with limited data
abstract: Rotor systems are fundamental components of rotating machinery, and their accurate fault diagnosis is the cornerstone of equipment safety. However, in practical industrial scenarios, existing data-driven methods are challenged by the coupling effect of variable operating conditions and limited training data. The feature variations induced by variable operating conditions typically require massive data for complex distribution fitting, which inherently conflicts with the reality of limited data. To address this dilemma, a dynamics-guided disentangled hypersphere prototype (DG-DHP) framework is proposed, which integrates physics-based dynamics modeling with data-driven representation disentanglement and prototype learning. First, a dynamic model of the rotor system is constructed to simulate a large amount of diverse data, and real-world noise patterns are injected to enhance data fidelity, thereby alleviating the scarcity of training data. Second, a representation disentanglement mechanism based on Brownian distance covariance is proposed to extract fault-related representations that are invariant to variable operating conditions via an explicit statistical regularization. Finally, adaptive hypersphere prototype learning is developed to replace traditional classifiers for fault diagnosis, thereby simultaneously facilitating the fitting of complex distributions and rapid adaptation to limited real-world samples. The proposed DG-DHP framework is validated on two rotor systems, demonstrating its superiority in rotor system fault diagnosis under variable operating conditions with limited data.

title: A graph attention network framework utilizing Kolmogorov–Arnold networks for dynamic analysis of complex structures in unseen scenarios
abstract: The rise of deep learning (DL) has greatly improved the analysis of complex structural responses. However, traditional DL models are limited by their dependence on large datasets, which hampers generalization to unseen scenarios and adaptability to various structural forms. To address these challenges, this paper introduces GATKAN, a novel graph attention network framework based on Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KAN). GATKAN models complex structures as graphs, integrating spatial topology into the training process. Utilizing a multi-head attention mechanism, it captures temporal response patterns and aggregates data from each graph node. The Kolmogorov–Arnold network updates potential states and projects data into the desired dimensions. Experimental results show that GATKAN generalizes well across unseen scenarios, particularly for complex systems with varying structural forms. The model’s robustness is further validated by noise introduction and sensitivity analyses. Comparison with baseline models demonstrates GATKAN’s superior prediction accuracy, especially in handling node features and dynamic system responses. Moreover, it reduces training data requirements while maintaining high accuracy, making it a promising tool for practical engineering applications.

title: A Class-Aware Supervised Contrastive Graph Network for CNC machining condition monitoring with class-imbalanced data
abstract: Machining state monitoring plays a critical role in ensuring quality, productivity, and reliability in CNC manufacturing. However, real-world industrial scenarios are often characterized by severe class imbalance and limited annotated data, which significantly challenge the robustness and generalization of existing learning-based approaches. To address this issue, we propose a Class-Aware Supervised Contrastive Graph Network (CSCGN), a unified framework that rethinks imbalanced industrial signal learning from a representation-centric perspective. Instead of treating signal segments independently, the proposed approach explicitly models the intrinsic structural relationships of one-dimensional sensor signals through a dynamic graph mechanism, while incorporating class-aware contrastive learning to enhance discriminative representation under imbalance. By jointly integrating multi-view signal representations, physics-informed topological modeling, and imbalance-aware optimization, the proposed framework effectively captures both structural dependencies and minority-class characteristics in noisy industrial environments. Extensive experiments on representative CNC machining tasks, including chatter detection and tool wear monitoring, demonstrate that CSCGN consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods across various imbalance settings. The results highlight its strong capability in minority-class recognition while maintaining overall robustness, indicating its potential for reliable deployment in real-world industrial systems.

title: Decoupling compound faults under data imbalance: A multi-task dynamic balanced learning network for gearbox fault diagnosis
abstract: Gearbox is a core component in mechanical transmission systems, and its accurate fault diagnosis is critical for ensuring operational safety of mechanical equipment. Although intelligent diagnosis methods have achieved promising results, they still face significant challenges. First, gearbox is a complex system with tightly coupled components (e.g., gears and bearings). Most existing methods focus on diagnosing isolated components, failing to effectively decouple and identify multi-component compound faults. Second, in actual engineering, fault data is usually scarce and severely imbalanced compared to normal data, which significantly degrades the performance of conventional data-driven models. To address these challenges, a multi-task dynamic balanced learning network is proposed for compound fault decoupling diagnosis with imbalanced data. Specifically, gearbox compound fault diagnosis is reformulated as a component-level multi-task diagnosis problem. First, a shared backbone network is designed to extract common features from vibration signals, followed by two kernel-adaptive task-specific branch networks that hierarchically disentangle component-level fault features for different tasks. Then, an adaptive balance loss is utilized to reweight training samples and alleviate the class imbalance influence. Finally, a task dynamic balancing strategy is incorporated to dynamically coordinate and optimize multiple diagnostic tasks during training. Extensive experiments are conducted on both real-world engineering and public datasets. The results show that the proposed method still achieves over 98% diagnostic accuracy on both gear and bearing diagnosis tasks even under severe class imbalance condition, demonstrating its superiority and robustness compared to other advanced methods.

title: Physics-guided safe collaboration: an uncertainty-gated heterogeneous semi-supervised regression framework for tool wear prediction
abstract: To address the dual challenges of labeled sample scarcity and poor physical interpretability in tool wear prediction, this paper proposes a Physics-Guided and Uncertainty-Gated Safe Collaboration Regression (PGS-CoReg) framework. This heterogeneous dual-branch design achieves closed-loop calibration between mechanism-driven and data-driven paradigms. Specifically, a Physics-Guided Gaussian Process Regression (PGGPR) embeds Zhu’s wear mechanism as a Bayesian prior to anchor global trends, employing combinational kernels to decouple non-stationary fluctuations. Concurrently, a Physics-Constrained Long Short-Term Memory (PG-LSTM) network introduces a multi-task loss with monotonicity and mechanism consistency constraints, ensuring predicted trajectories strictly adhere to thermodynamic laws. Crucially, the framework utilizes PGGPR’s posterior variance as a dynamic gate to filter pseudo-labels, effectively blocking error accumulation and logical drift. Experiments on the PHM 2010 dataset demonstrate that PGGPR and PG-LSTM reduce prediction errors by 10.0% and 18.2% against baselines.
