With only 20% labels, PGS-CoReg achieves an RMSE of 17.50 μm, surpassing the fully supervised LSTM baseline. Incorporating Non-IID heterogeneous data further reduces error by 19.6%, increasing the Confidence Interval Coverage Rate to 94.0%. Remarkably, cross-scenario validations on the NASA dataset confirm its robust sensor-agnostic transferability, effectively overcoming mathematically ill-posed early-stage extrapolation and massive blind-zone interpolation under severe domain shifts and extreme label scarcity (merely 3 labels). This study establishes a verifiable methodology for highly reliable predictive maintenance and tool health management in small-sample industrial scenarios.

title: Interpretable multiscale algorithm unrolling network using learnable Gabor filters for fault diagnosis
abstract: Intelligent fault diagnosis has emerged as a pivotal research area in intelligent maintenance systems, stressing interpretable intelligence and trustworthy decision-making for reliable and safe engineering applications. To this end, this study proposes the Interpretable Multiscale AlGorithm unrolling Network using learnable Gabor filters (IMAG-Net). Specifically, IMAG-Net establishes a physically optimization-unrolling framework that integrates learnable Gabor filtering with multiscale convolutional sparse coding, embedding the sparsity prior of fault-induced into a trainable neural architecture for adaptive and interpretable fault diagnosis. Distinct from traditional deep learning approaches, the proposed framework enhances interpretability and decision transparency through structured convolutional sparse coding and adaptive multiscale decomposition, where Gabor filters with learnable center frequencies automatically capture dominant signal components that correspond to fault characteristic frequencies and their harmonics. To further ensure physical fidelity, the learned multiscale representations are analyzed alongside sparsity-guided signal reconstructions derived from salient sparse activations, thereby validating the reliability and internal consistency of the network’s decision logic. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a diagnostic accuracy exceeding 94% under high-noise conditions (σn=1.0), consistently outperforming conventional deep learning baselines while preserving physically meaningful and interpretable diagnostic representations.

title: Conditional diffusion-based time–frequency data augmentation with multi-scale coordinate attention for diesel engine fault diagnosis
abstract: Diesel engine vibration signals are characterized by multi-source impulsive excitations and strong non-stationarity. The scarcity of fault samples and severe class imbalance make it difficult for existing generative models to simultaneously achieve high generation quality and effective diagnostic improvement after augmentation, and often lead to attenuation of mid- and high-frequency textures as well as over-smoothed edges in generated time–frequency images. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention conditional diffusion model (MSTFCA-CDM) for fault time–frequency sample augmentation in diesel engines. Continuous wavelet transform (CWT) time–frequency images are used as the generation target, and a multi-scale time–frequency coordinate-attention module is embedded into the conditional diffusion framework to enhance the representation of impulsive structures at different scales and critical time–frequency regions. In addition, a frequency-domain consistency loss is introduced to constrain the two-dimensional spectral magnitude distributions of the predicted and true noise, thereby improving the recovery of mid- and high-frequency textures and local edge details. Experiments on the TBD234 diesel engine dataset show that the proposed method achieves better performance than the compared methods in terms of generation quality, distribution consistency, and augmentation-assisted diagnostic performance within the investigated experimental setting. When the sample ratio between the normal class and each fault class is gradually balanced from 20:1 to 1:1, the classification accuracy improves from 58.34% to 98.90%. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of multi-scale modeling, coordinate attention, and frequency-domain consistency constraints. The results suggest that MSTFCA-CDM is effective for fault time–frequency sample augmentation and diagnosis under severe class imbalance in a controlled experimental setting.

title: Adaptive and robust motor intent decoding for cross-day dexterous finger force predictions
abstract: Motor intent decoding based on neural signals provides a promising pathway for intuitive human-robot interactions. Among various neural signal sources, binary spiking activities of motor units (MUs) serve as a reliable basis for intent decoding. However, the non-stationary nature of MU action potential poses a major challenge for robust intent decoding. To address this issue, we developed an adaptive motor intent decoding framework that dynamically refined the MU pool to maintain cross-day reliability. The framework integrated three modules: (1) a cross-validation component for selecting MUs with consistent decoding performance across days, (2) a flag policy to exclude inactive and inaccurate MUs based on temporal activation consistency, and (3) a refinement component to retain only finger-specific MUs that can lead to accurate individual finger force predictions. We validated our new approach by quantifying finger force performance. We obtained high-density surface electromyographic (sEMG) recordings over three days. We then performed adaptive source separation to extract neuronal firing spikes for subsequent motor intent decoding. We also demonstrated the feasibility of our approach during real-time control of a robotic finger. The results demonstrate that our developed adaptive motor intent decoder consistently achieved higher prediction accuracy across multiple days than the non-adaptive decomposition method. Compared with deep learning approaches, our approach outperformed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), while achieving comparable performance to CNN-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) across days. These findings highlight the robustness of MU-level adaptive motor intent decoding in overcoming cross-day neural signal variations, thereby contributing to the development of accurate and robust signal processing strategies for reliable and practical applications in human-robot interactions.

title: Noise-firewall: mitigating pseudo-label poisoning in semi-supervised fault diagnosis via parameter decoupling
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis in industrial settings faces the dual challenges of scarce supervision and label noise. Although semi-supervised learning (SSL) can leverage unlabeled data, it becomes fragile under label noise because corrupted supervision distorts representation learning and subsequently contaminates pseudo-labels, causing confirmation bias and error propagation. To mitigate this issue, this paper proposes a Noise-Firewall framework that couples robust representation learning with SSL via additive parameter decomposition (ω=σ + γ) and dynamic regularization. The σ-branch is encouraged to learn stable fault representations, while the auxiliary γ-branch absorbs noise-induced optimization pressure, thereby structurally shielding σ from corrupted labels. Built upon the protected σ-branch, Confidence-Aware Pseudo-Labeling (CAPL) is further developed: pseudo-labels are generated strictly from σ predictions, and the γ-branch is frozen during pseudo-label backpropagation to prevent pseudo-label poisoning. Extensive experiments under multiple noise types (20%/40%) and up to 40% unlabeled data on two public benchmarks—Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Paderborn University (PU)—validate the mechanism and stability of the proposed components, and further perform systematic comparisons with representative SSL methods on a real robotic belt-grinding dataset. For example, on CWRU with 40% symmetric noise, accuracy improves from 61.8 ± 6.9 to 78.6 ± 1.1; under the joint setting of 40% symmetric noise with 40% unlabeled data, PU and the robotic dataset reach 93.15% and 90.2% accuracy, respectively. Finally, γ is discarded at inference, enabling a “train-complex, infer-simple” deployment with no additional inference overhead.

title: Physics-inspired multiwavelet KAN for interpretable bearing fault diagnosis under harsh operating conditions
abstract: Deep learning models for rotating machinery diagnosis often lack interpretability and suffer severe performance degradation under strong noise. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Physics-Inspired Multiwavelet Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) for robust and transparent bearing fault diagnosis. Building upon the Wav-KAN architecture, we develop a parallel multiwavelet expert framework utilizing Morlet, Laplace, and Mexhat activations to structurally capture complementary fault signatures. An adaptive evidence-weighting fusion mechanism is further introduced to dynamically balance expert contributions based on input signal characteristics. Extensive experiments across three bearing datasets, including a complex turbopump test rig, demonstrate the framework’s superior noise robustness. Notably, it achieves 92.05% accuracy on the PU dataset under severe −10 dB noise, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art deep learning, wavelet-based, and single-wavelet KAN baselines. Further analyses show that the learned wavelet scales remain close to theory-derived characteristic scales, that fusion weights vary across fault categories, and that decision attribution focuses on localized fault-related signal regions, providing supportive evidence for the interpretability of the proposed framework.

title: Stiffness-constrained bandgap tailoring in sinusoidal compression-torsion metamaterials: inverse design and MIGA-PINN optimization
abstract: Effectively attenuating low-to-mid-frequency vibrations while maintaining load-bearing stiffness remains a critical engineering challenge. This study introduces a novel sinusoidal compression-torsion coupling metamaterial, whose vibration bandgap characteristics and mechanical stiffness can be synergistically tailored. Analytical models for stiffness and bandgap boundary frequencies are derived theoretically to provide physical constraints for a physics-informed neural network (PINN)-based forward model. Conversely, a neural network (NN)-based inverse model maps target mechanical properties back to unit cell geometric parameters. Subsequently, a Multi-Island Genetic Algorithm (MIGA)-PINN optimization strategy is implemented to tailor vibration bandgaps to target ranges while satisfying stiffness constraints. The optimization targets include: (1) minimizing the onset frequency of the first bandgap; (2) minimizing the interval between the first two bandgaps; (3) maximizing the bandgap width; and (4) customizing bandgap ranges. Experimental and numerical validations demonstrate the efficacy of both the forward-inverse design and the MIGA-PINN optimization strategy, with predictions showing strong agreement with experimental and simulation data. Notably, an optimized metamaterial subject to a stiffness constraint of 5000 N/m achieves stable vibration attenuation across the 100–1000 Hz range. These findings demonstrate the targeted vibration control capabilities of the metamaterials under stiffness constraints and provide a computationally efficient approach for their rational designs.

title: An improved unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network for motor eccentricity monitoring assisted by simulation data
abstract: Rotor eccentricity in motors frequently leads to severe vibration. Although deep learning algorithms provide an effective approach for monitoring eccentricity conditions, labeled data for such faults is typically scarce in real-world industrial settings. To address this, we propose a novel unsupervised domain adversarial transfer network, assisted by simulation data, for monitoring motor eccentricity. First, a multiphysics-coupled model integrating electromagnetics and stator structure is established to simulate the vibration response of the stator casing under different rotor eccentricity conditions, thereby generating a simulated dataset with varying eccentricity levels. Then, an electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation test device is designed to validate the multiphysics model through modal testing. Next, an adaptive wavelet image style transfer network is employed to migrate the “style” of the time–frequency images from the experimental data to those of the simulated data, enhancing their similarity in the time–frequency domain. Finally, the stylized simulated images serve as the source domain, while the unlabeled experimental images constitute the target domain. Within the framework of a domain adversarial neural network (DANN), joint distribution adaptation (JDA) and conditional contrastive domain (CCD) adaptation loss functions are incorporated to jointly optimize the model. Experimental results on the electromagnetic–mechanical excitation separation device demonstrate that the proposed method effectively detects the degree of rotor eccentricity.

title: Remaining useful life estimation of ball-screw feed drives using a nonlinear digital twin and PINN–AIDB framework
abstract: Ball-screw feed drives (BSFDs) govern positioning accuracy and operational availability in computer numerical control (CNC) machine tools, yet reliable remaining useful life (RUL) estimation remains challenging owing to constrained controller sensing and complex electromechanical interactions. This study presents a real-time RUL estimation framework operating exclusively on controller-resident OPC–UA telemetry, without auxiliary vibration instrumentation. A validated nonlinear digital twin, confirmed at 0.020%–0.026% stroke error under pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS) excitation, provides surrogates for frictional dissipation and torsional microslip, defining a physics-derived degradation driver Φ(t). This driver regularises a compact physics-informed neural network fused with an anchor-informed degradation baseline (PINN–AIDB). The framework incorporates residual ODE constraints, monotonicity enforcement, and anchor consistency, whereas the Weibull model serves as a transparent statistical baseline. Pre- and post-accelerated life test (ALT) states calibrate an acceleration factor AF∗≈82.6 that maps laboratory exposure to an equivalent field horizon of approximately 8260h, consistent with catalogue-referenced BSFD fatigue lives. Validation under no-load and loaded conditions (0kg to 150kg, 5000 to 20 000 mm/min) confirms severity-consistent RUL compression across a 249h range (≈3% of nominal lifetime). The proposed PINN–AIDB projects the field horizon with a deviation of 11h from the catalogue-anchored reference, a 90% confidence-interval width of 211h, and 100% threshold-crossing feasibility, while reducing feedrate-order monotonicity violations from five (baseline estimators) to one across all 16 operating conditions. Ablation confirms that Φ(t), monotonicity enforcement, and anchor constraints address complementary identifiability limitations under controller-resident sensing without auxiliary condition-monitoring hardware.

title: A semi-supervised tool wear monitoring approach integrating physics-guided weak labels and uncertainty quantification
abstract: Driven by the Industry 5.0 paradigm, tool wear monitoring has become essential for ensuring machining quality and production efficiency. However, the supervision asymmetry between readily available sensor signals and scarce labeled data hampers the industrial deployment of monitoring models. To address this issue, a physics-guided semi-supervised learning method with uncertainty quantification is proposed. First, multi-source heterogeneous features that characterize local cutting dynamics and historical degradation information are constructed via adaptive feature filtering. Second, the improved parallel symbolic regression learns trend-constrained symbolic degradation mappings and generates physics-guided weak labels that are consistent with the irreversible evolution of tool wear, thereby alleviating the supervision bottleneck caused by insufficient true labels. Subsequently, a staged conformal prediction strategy quantifies stage-related uncertainty of weak labels and constructs adaptive loss weights to reduce the interference of low-reliability weak labels during model training. Finally, a physics-guided cross-attention fusion module is designed to leverage degradation trend information as guidance for adaptive interactions among heterogeneous features, while a raw-feature bypass is introduced to preserve data-driven information and reduce the risk of negative transfer caused by local weak-label bias. Ablation studies confirm the advantages of the proposed method in preserving trend smoothness, suppressing heteroscedastic noise, and improving late-stage identification accuracy. Compared with the best-performing baseline, the proposed method reduces RMSE and MAE by 14.2 % and 10.9 %, respectively, while R2 increases by 1.2 %. Further validation shows that the proposed method can robustly adapt to different cutting conditions. Meanwhile, its lightweight online inference architecture enables deployment on resource-constrained industrial edge devices.

title: A domain knowledge informed approach for anomaly detection of electric vehicle interior sounds
abstract: The detection of anomalies in automotive cabin sounds is critical for ensuring vehicle quality and maintaining passenger comfort. In many real-world settings, this task is more appropriately framed as an unsupervised learning problem rather than the supervised case due to the scarcity or complete absence of labeled faulty data. In such an unsupervised setting, the model is trained exclusively on healthy samples and detects anomalies as deviations from normal behavior. However, in the absence of labeled faulty samples for validation and the limited reliability of commonly used metrics, such as validation reconstruction error, effective model selection remains a significant challenge. To overcome these limitations, a domain-knowledge-informed approach for model selection is proposed, in which proxy-anomalies engineered through structured perturbations of healthy spectrograms are used in the validation set to support model selection. The proposed methodology is evaluated on a high-fidelity electric vehicle dataset comprising healthy and faulty cabin sounds across five representative fault types viz., Imbalance, Modulation, Whine, Wind, and Pulse Width Modulation. This dataset, generated using advanced sound synthesis techniques, and validated via expert jury assessments, has been made publicly available to facilitate further research. Experimental evaluations on the five fault cases demonstrate the selection of optimal models using proxy-anomalies, significantly outperform conventional model selection strategies.

title: Impact acoustic-based damage identification of bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning
abstract: Bridge expansion joints are susceptible to deterioration under long-term vehicle loading and environmental effects. The resulting damage may affect structural performance and driving comfort, making rapid and reliable damage identification important for bridge maintenance. This study proposes an impact acoustic-based damage identification method for bridge expansion joints under vehicle-induced excitation using attention-enhanced one-class learning. Acoustic sensors are integrated into a moving load system to acquire acoustic responses from key components, including the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone. The resulting acoustic signals are characterized using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs). On this basis, a compact Transformer encoder with an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) mechanism, termed ECA-TinyTransformer, is constructed to jointly model global temporal dependencies and critical frequency-band information. At the decision level, Deep Support Vector Data Description (DeepSVDD) models damage identification as anomaly detection using only healthy samples, addressing the scarcity of damage data. Experimental results demonstrate that, under the fully damaged condition (State 4), healthy and damaged samples are clearly separated in the learned feature space. The proposed method achieves accuracies of 0.968, 0.965, and 0.968 for the center beam, support bar, and concrete in the anchorage zone, respectively, with recall values approaching 1.000. Comparative studies further demonstrate the superiority of the proposed framework over representative temporal modeling architectures and one-class anomaly detection methods. The proposed framework provides an effective and practical solution for intelligent condition assessment of bridge expansion joints under moving-load excitation, highlighting the potential of one-class acoustic monitoring for bridge infrastructure inspection.

title: A physics-guided evidential multimodal uncertainty framework for small-sample welding defect detection using magneto-optical and infrared imaging
abstract: Traditional data-driven welding defect detection methods often suffer from poor interpretability, performance degradation under small-sample conditions, and an inability to quantify decision-making reliability. To address these issues, this study proposes a novel Physics-guided Evidential-based Multimodal Uncertainty Framework (PEMUF) for weld defect classification using magneto-optical imaging (MOI) and infrared thermography (IRT). A coordinated MOI-IRT nondestructive testing system is developed to acquire complementary magnetic and thermal responses of weld defects. Based on the distinct physical sensitivities of the two modalities, leakage magnetic field information from MOI and heat diffusion characteristics from IRT are explicitly encoded into modality-specific prior channels, improving the physical interpretability and discriminability of input representations. PEMUF further combines hierarchical multimodal interaction, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion. The hierarchical attention mechanism enhances intra-modal representation learning and cross-modal complementary interaction, while spectral manifold augmentation enriches the effective feature distribution under limited training samples. In addition, Dempster-Shafer evidential fusion with Dirichlet uncertainty modeling is introduced to generate both defect-category predictions and uncertainty scores. Experiments are conducted on a four-class resistance spot weld defect dataset, including defect-free, crack, pit, and incomplete fusion samples. Using the full training set, PEMUF achieves an Accuracy of 99.04 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9908, and a Brier Score of 0.0271. More importantly, when only 20 % of the training samples are used, the model still maintains an Accuracy of 96.31 %, a Macro F1 of 0.9617, and a Brier Score of 0.0529, demonstrating strong robustness and probability calibration under small-sample conditions. Comparative experiments, ablation studies, confusion matrices, t-SNE visualization, Grad-CAM++ analysis, and uncertainty evaluation further confirm that physical priors, spectral manifold augmentation, and evidential fusion jointly improve feature discrimination, generalization, and reliability-aware decision-making. These results indicate that PEMUF provides an effective and reliable solution for small-sample multimodal weld defect inspection.

title: Hydraulic system compound fault diagnosis based on decoupling-oriented feature optimization and uncertainty-aware evidential fusion
abstract: Compound fault diagnosis in complex hydraulic systems remains challenging because of strong feature coupling among fault combinations. This paper proposes a D-S (Dempster-Shafer) theory-enhanced convolutional neural network (DSNN) integrating decoupling-oriented feature optimization with uncertainty-aware evidential fusion. The proposed method reconstructs the original diagnosis task into several similarity-aware subtasks to improve the separability of compound fault features under coupled fault modes. Fault categories are first grouped according to feature-distribution distances. The divided groups are used as the focal elements for subsequent D-S theory-based diagnostic reasoning, where uncertainty-aware soft grouping allows overlapping focal elements. Then, dedicated CNN-based submodels are trained to estimate basic probability assignments (BPAs) for divided focal elements while performing task-specific feature optimization. Finally, a differentiable D-S evidence fusion layer combines the BPAs from all submodels and indicates conflicts among submodel evidence through the conflict factor. Experiments on an SCM hydraulic test rig and an open-source hydraulic dataset show that DSNN achieves superior diagnostic accuracy and robustness.

title: AWT-DDFN: an end-to-end adaptive wavelet transform-dual domain fusion network for bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: Deep learning has been widely used in intelligent fault diagnosis of rolling bearings. Existing fault diagnosis methods usually use multi-scale wavelet transforms to convert raw 1D vibration signals into time–frequency representations as model inputs. However, such preprocessing brings high computational cost, inevitable information loss and tedious manual parameter tuning, which hinders real end-to-end diagnosis. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an adaptive wavelet transform–dual domain fusion network (AWT-DDFN), a complete end-to-end framework that directly processes raw vibration signals without manual preprocessing. AWT-DDFN adopts a learnable wavelet convolution layer to replace fixed wavelet transforms, realizing joint optimization of feature extraction and fault diagnosis. Meanwhile, the network uses a dual-branch structure to capture complementary discriminative features: a frequency-domain branch based on pointwise convolution and a time-domain branch combining grouped convolution and dilated convolution. This structure effectively reduces model complexity and parameters, making the model lightweight and robust to noise and trivial signal variations. The features of the two branches are fused by element-wise addition before being sent to the classifier for fault identification, forming a seamless end-to-end diagnosis pipeline. Experiments on PU and CWRU datasets show that AWT-DDFN achieves superior diagnosis performance and stronger noise robustness than state-of-the-art methods, with fewer parameters and lower computation cost. By discarding handcrafted preprocessing, the proposed framework provides a lightweight, end-to-end and deployable intelligent diagnosis solution with strong practical value for industrial scenarios under complex working conditions and strong noise.

title: FRP-M2DA: cross-modal multi-source domain adaptation via frequency-domain recurrence and multi-level adversarial alignment for cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
abstract: In complex variable operating-condition scenarios, bearing fault diagnosis faces two coupled challenges: pronounced distribution shift and insufficient discriminative information from a single view. To address these issues, this paper proposes FRP-M2DA, a frequency-domain recurrence plot (FRP)-guided multimodal multi-source adversarial domain adaptation framework for robust cross-domain diagnosis. FRP transforms one-dimensional spectral sequences into a two-dimensional structured representation that explicitly captures recurrence structures and global correlations associated with fault-induced impulsive components. A heterogeneous dual-stream encoder is then constructed, where a Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) extracts multi-scale global texture semantics from FRP, and a multi-scale CNN (MSCNN) models local transients from the raw vibration sequence, enabling complementary “global–local” representation learning via feature fusion. To handle multi-source transfer, FRP-M2DA introduces multi-level multi-source adversarial alignment by placing domain discriminators in both modality-specific subspaces and the fused space, thereby enforcing domain invariance at multiple representation levels and mitigating insufficient alignment and negative transfer. Moreover, a bidirectional cross-view contrastive regularization (InfoNCE) is incorporated to enhance semantic consistency across heterogeneous views, promoting intra-class compactness and inter-class separability on the unlabeled target domain. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks (JNU cross-speed and PU cross-load) and an engineering test-rig dataset with coupled speed–load shifts demonstrate that FRP-M2DA consistently outperforms representative baselines and state-of-the-art domain adaptation methods, achieving superior generalization, balanced class-wise performance, and reliable fault detectability under composite operating-condition variations.
keywords: Bearing Fault Diagnosis under Variable Operating Conditions

title: A Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network for Extracting Incipient Fault Signatures in Rotating Machinery
abstract: Signal decomposition is an important task in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) of mechanical transmission systems characterized by nonlinear and non-stationary vibration responses. However, conventional signal processing methodologies are often constrained by fixed basis functions and manual parameter tuning, which compromise noise robustness and limit their ability in capturing transient signatures of incipient faults. Leveraging the paradigm of signal processing-informed neural networks, this paper proposes an interpretable Frequency-Aware Residual Decomposition Network (FARCD-Net), which unfolds iterative filtering into a learnable framework to reduce reliance on manually designed optimization objectives. Specifically, a Generalized Adaptive Decomposition Module (GADM) is constructed via residual learning to generalize the conventional filtering operator, preserving the underlying decomposition principle. To enhance feature extraction in noisy environments, a data-driven Frequency Masking Layer (FML) is introduced. The layer learns adaptive spectral weights, enabling the network to dynamically localize transient signatures within resonance bands. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations on a run-to-failure benchmark and a high-speed train bogie system demonstrate effective extraction of fault-induced transients, with physical interpretability supported by intermediate network representations.

title: A differentiable physics-embedded framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification
abstract: To address the need for thermally informed tire modeling for handling-oriented force prediction under limited thermal sensing, this paper presents a differentiable physics-embedded sequential framework for thermally informed Neural-UniTire modeling and identification. First, a differentiable radial thermal model is developed from a continuous radial thermal formulation through finite-volume Crank–Nicolson discretization, with hybrid global, physics-parameterized, and neural thermal coefficients used to reconstruct radial multilayer thermal states from sparse boundary measurements. Then, a Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model is developed by embedding neural networks into the UniTire framework and extending it to unsteady conditions through a second-order hysteresis element. Finally, a thermally informed correction mechanism is introduced for the Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model, in which reconstructed radial multilayer thermal states with operating-condition information are used to generate neural thermo-correction factors for stiffness- and friction-related parameters. Experiments on an MTS flat-track test rig with a passenger-car tire and a semi-slick tire under pure lateral-slip and longitudinal-slip conditions show good agreement with the measured temperature and force responses. The radial thermal model achieves accurate temperature estimation from sparse boundary measurements. The unsteady Physics-Embedded Neural-UniTire model improves force prediction over the steady-state formulation, especially in the nonlinear slip region and phase lag. The thermally informed model improves force prediction over the baseline and sparse-input ablation models under pulse-excitation conditions, while the learned thermal correction remains physically interpretable.

title: End-to-End predictive modeling of excavator hydraulic systems
abstract: Accurate prediction of the dynamic response of excavator hydraulic systems is a key prerequisite for model-based control applications. However, existing studies have not established a direct mapping from cylinder outputs to joystick signals. To address this issue, this study proposes an end-to-end predictive model that integrates a joystick-signal baseline with data-driven modeling. Specifically, the joystick-signal baseline is jointly determined by the mechanism-based relationship between cylinder motion and hydraulic flow and the predefined electro-hydraulic control mappings, providing an initial prediction reference for the model. Subsequently, a two-stage long short-term memory (LSTM) network is introduced for data-driven modeling. In the first stage, sensitivity-based weighting dynamically adjusts the weights of the input variables to capture the dynamic nonlinear characteristics of the system. In the second stage, the weighted input features from the first stage are combined with the joystick-signal baseline to form a new input sequence, which is then modeled using a multilayer LSTM. In addition, a delay-aware structure is designed to account for the non-fixed delays between joystick signals and cylinder states. Experimental results show that the prediction errors remain within 10 % under in-distribution validation, while R2 values above 0.88 are achieved on an independently collected gravel excavation dataset from another excavator of the same model, demonstrating good prediction performance and generalization capability. The proposed architecture requires only 4 MB of storage and achieves an inference time of less than 2 ms per prediction, indicating strong potential for real-time applications.

title: High-Order Fourier-Basis LSTM-PINN for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction in whole-angle vibratory gyroscopes
abstract: The bias of a whole-angle vibratory gyroscope is not a stationary offset but an angle-dependent waveform shaped by structural errors, circuit-induced control and detection errors, and thermally driven operating variations, whose coupled effects are represented in the present observation model by effective Fourier bias components rather than separated into source-specific parameters. Existing bias models usually rely on low-order angular harmonics, especially the 2θ and 4θ components, which limits their ability to represent high-order angle-dependent bias structures. This study proposes a High-Order Fourier-Basis Long Short-Term Memory Physics-Informed Neural Network (LSTM-PINN) framework for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction and harmonic component characterization. High-order potential and Rayleigh dissipation functionals are retained up to the eighth order, from which a 2/4/6/8 even-order Fourier harmonic basis is derived. This Lagrangian-derived harmonic structure defines the Fourier-basis analytical decoder of the LSTM-PINN solver. Instead of treating the angle-dependent bias waveform as an unconstrained regression target, the solver infers the scale-factor term and Fourier bias components from historical sequences of the amplitude-control envelope, quadrature-control envelope, and resonant frequency, and reconstructs the angle-dependent bias waveform through the Lagrangian-derived analytical decoder. Experiments on 16-electrode micro-shell gyroscopes show stable reconstruction, with a mean RMSE of 6.62×10−4 deg/s and a mean R2 of 0.9886. Architecture ablations show that both the PINN and the LSTM are necessary: relative to the black-box LSTM baseline and the MLP-PINN baseline, the full LSTM-PINN reduces the 1 Hz mean RMSE by 90.5% and 59.2%, respectively. Expanding the physically admissible basis from 2θ/4θ to 2θ/4θ/6θ/8θ reduces the across-label mean RMSE by 32.0%, while repeated-segment tests show quasi-stationary inferred high-order components. Over a seven-day evaluation horizon at ±1 and ±8deg/s, the Day-7 across-rate mean RMSE and R2 were 9.765×10−4deg/s and 0.9857, respectively. Within the validated micro-shell device and laboratory operating range, these results support the proposed framework as a device-physics-constrained temporal method for angle-dependent bias waveform reconstruction.

title: Evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for fault diagnosis in dynamic open environments
abstract: The practical implementation of deep learning models for real-time mechanical fault diagnosis in open environments remains challenging, primarily due to data acquisition difficulties, dynamic industrial fluctuations, and the emergence of novel failure modes in real-world applications. Conventional open-set domain generalization (OSDG) methods often fail to generalize to such scenarios, as they typically necessitate extensive offline training data spanning multiple source domains. To address these limitations, an evidence-causality dual adversarial framework for single-source OSDG is proposed, enabling online fault diagnosis in dynamic open conditions under limited data. Specifically, a sample weight-aware evidential loss is introduced to mitigate overconfidence in boundary-ambiguous samples. Furthermore, an evidential neural network is employed for uncertainty quantification, thereby enhancing diagnostic reliability and the robust detection of unknown failure modes. Concurrently, an uncertainty-guided data generation module is developed to augment data diversity while preserving semantic consistency. Finally, an adversarial causal feature disentanglement module is designed to extract highly discriminative causal features, effectively suppressing spurious correlations induced by dynamic distribution shifts. Extensive experimental evaluations conducted on three rotating machinery datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in fault diagnosis under dynamic, open industrial environments. The code will be available on GitHub at https://github.com/Fanyang199711/SOSDG.

title: Chatter-sensitive feature construction and dual-branch learning for machining state identification in micro-milling of glow discharge polymer
abstract: Glow discharge polymer (GDP) ablators with micro-milled modulated microstructures are increasingly used in inertial confinement fusion (ICF) applications. However, self-excited vibration/chatter, generated from an insufficient-stiffness manufacturing system, could degrade the resultant surface quality and process productivity during micro-milling. In this study, a physically guided data-driven framework was developed for chatter-sensitive feature construction and machining-state identification in micro-milling of GDP polymers. Tri-directional milling-force and acceleration signals were in-situ acquired during micro-milling with a single-edge diamond tool. Wavelet packet decomposition (WPD) was initially employed for noise suppression and signal reconstruction, with optimal parameters determined using an energy-weighted feature evaluation strategy. Variational mode decomposition (VMD) was then applied to isolate state-sensitive intrinsic mode functions (IMFs), and a state-discriminative energy–entropy criterion was developed to determine task-oriented decomposition parameters. Based on the selected chatter-sensitive modes, eight multi-domain features were extracted and organized into two heterogeneous feature tensors. A dual-branch Inception Residual network (DIR-Net) was constructed to independently encode force- and acceleration-related features before high-level feature fusion. Experimental results showed that WPD improved the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the milling-force and acceleration signals by 65.8 % and 43.0 %, respectively. DIR-Net achieved an identification accuracy of 97.08 % and a macro-averaged F1-score of 97.02 % on the independent test set, outperforming conventional CNN and ResNet benchmarks. Feature visualization and online monitoring results further indicated improved separability among air-cut, stable cutting, and chatter states, as well as stable recognition performance under the unseen tool-overhang and tool-size conditions. The proposed research framework provides an interpretable solution for chatter identification and online monitoring in ultra-precision micro-milling of GDP.

title: Fusing multi-sensor data in graph convolutional networks for robust structural damage detection against environmental and operational variations
abstract: In structural health monitoring, environmental and operational variations (EOVs), along with extreme class imbalance in damage severity datasets, substantially compromise damage detection accuracy and reliability. To address these challenges, a collaborative node-edge graph convolutional network (CNEGCN) is proposed for structural damage detection, incorporating advanced feature extraction, node-edge co-embedding, and a physics-informed loss formulation. First, a reference signal reconstruction method combined with wavelet coherence is developed to extract features sensitive to structural damage while remaining robust to environmental variations. Second, a network architecture employing collaborative node-edge embedding is constructed to effectively fuse heterogeneous multi-location sensor data, specifically acceleration and strain measurements. Finally, a two-stage training scheme transitioning from conventional cross-entropy loss to a physics-informed multiple damage location assurance criterion loss is implemented to mitigate overfitting on minority damage classes. Validated across three experimental and numerical cases of varying complexity, the proposed CNEGCN demonstrates stable classification performance and strong robustness to noise and EOVs, achieving classification accuracies exceeding 0.98 and competitive Macro F1 scores. The proposed CNEGCN offers an efficient online diagnostic solution for real-time structural damage monitoring under complex environmental conditions.

title: Parameter identification and unknown excitation inversion of piezoelectric cantilever beams using multi-network PINNs with Fourier feature mapping
abstract: Constructing a highly accurate multiphysics coupling model is a fundamental prerequisite for advancing piezoelectric energy harvesting systems from theoretical design to practical engineering applications. However, in real engineering scenarios, external excitations are often uncertain, and key system parameters, such as mass, stiffness, and damping ratio, are easily affected by operating conditions, leading to significant deviations from their theoretical design values. Conventional system identification methods strongly rely on known external excitations and stationary operating assumptions, and therefore are difficult to apply to piezoelectric systems with time-varying parameter uncertainty and complex oscillatory dynamic responses. As a result, identification failure and insufficient accuracy are commonly encountered in practice. To address these challenges, a multi-network-structure physics-informed neural network (PINNs) method embedded with temporal Fourier feature mapping is proposed in this study. The proposed method improves the representation capability of the multiphysics model for oscillatory responses and local temporal details, thereby enabling accurate identification of key parameters and inversion of unknown excitation forces in piezoelectric systems. Numerical results show that, under free vibration, sinusoidal excitation, and random excitation conditions, the relative errors of the identified equivalent mass, equivalent stiffness, and equivalent damping ratio are all less than 5%. In addition, the unknown excitation force can also be accurately inverted. The proposed method demonstrates satisfactory identification accuracy and robustness, and can provide effective methodological support for high-precision modeling and practical design of piezoelectric energy harvesting systems.

title: Physics-guided Siamese tracker for robust vision-based structural displacement monitoring under visibility degradation
abstract: The vision-based structural displacement monitoring technique has significant potential for structural health monitoring (SHM). However, its field applications are severely limited due to reduced target visibility caused by factors such as occlusion, fog, and light changes. To address these challenges, this paper presents a robust vision-based displacement monitoring framework named CP-SiamRPN. It makes use of an enhanced deep Siamese network architecture, along with a physical consistency mechanism to eliminate non-physical drift and a confidence-guided mechanism to quantify tracking uncertainty and adjust parameters accordingly. In contrast to existing deep learning-based methods, the proposed framework has zero-shot generalization capabilities, which enable deployment on new target instances without target-specific retraining or fine-tuning. This is particularly valuable for reliable structural displacement monitoring of diverse target types under traffic or environmental interference. Systematic validation has been conducted by impact testing on simply supported beams, shake table testing on five-story frame structures, and field monitoring of bridges. The results demonstrate that, under the visibility-degradation scenarios examined (occlusion, illumination variation, and progressive blur), the proposed method maintains accurate displacement measurement and provides an explicit indicator of tracking reliability.

title: Image-to-image translation-based visual vibration displacement measurement of a rotating body with tilted viewing angle in horizontal plane
abstract: In the modern industrial field, the dynamic stability of rotating bodies is crucial to the operational efficiency and safety of equipment, and accurate measurement of their vibration displacement is of great significance. Although image recognition algorithms have already realized the visual measurement of vibration displacement of rotating bodies, the existing algorithms still have problems such as targeted data processing and relying on manual labeling. For this reason, this paper proposes a method for measuring the vibration displacement of rotating bodies with tilted viewing angles in the horizontal plane, integrating image-to-image translation with traditional vision techniques. Image-to-image translation is leveraged to convert images of rotors with tilted viewing angles captured at different oblique angles into a unified perspective. This method effectively reduces data dependency in vibration displacement extraction. Additionally, considering the characteristic features of rotor vibration images, a spatial integration and cross-dimensional optimization strategy is designed. A stepwise downsampling scheme, a DepthCascade Block (DCB) module, and a Cross-Axis Grouped Residual Block (CAGRB) module are introduced to optimize the generator network of pix2pixHD, thereby improving the quality of view transformation. The proposed method combines deep learning and traditional vision techniques to realize the vibration displacement measurement of the rotor, while eliminating human-induced errors caused by manual labeling. Based on ablation experiments, comparisons with multiple neural networks model, and comparisons with eddy current sensor data, the results show that at an acquisition rate of 2000 frames per second, the root mean square error (RMSE) for vibration displacement measurements at the three oblique angles was as low as 0.0236 mm, 0.0288 mm, and 0.0348 mm, respectively, with peak signal-to-noise ratios (PSNR) reaching 41.18 dB, 39.98 dB, and 39.65 dB, respectively. Furthermore, in comparison with image-recognition-based vibration displacement extraction methods, the proposed method can effectively extract rotor vibration displacement under stable illumination and at the three fixed tilted viewpoints tested in this study. However, a clear failure boundary is observed at viewpoint 3 under the combined effects of low illumination and a complex background.

title: Intelligent non-destructive evaluation of complex defects using magnetization-excited infrared thermography
abstract: Aircraft hydraulic pipelines are critical components of aircraft hydraulic systems, and reliable inspection of their surface defects is essential for ensuring operational safety and maintenance efficiency. Existing inspection methods for ferromagnetic surface defects are often limited by specimen contamination, insufficient adaptability to complex curved structures, or low inspection efficiency. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent inspection framework that integrates Dual-mode Electromagnetic Magnetization-excited Infrared Thermography (DEMIT) with deep learning-based defect detection. By employing controllable circumferential and longitudinal magnetization, DEMIT enables rapid and non-contact inspection without contaminating the specimen surface, while promoting more uniform thermal excitation and more consistent defect-sensitive thermal responses in complex curved components. The proposed framework is further implemented in a self-developed automated inspection system to support efficient defect imaging and intelligent recognition. For accurate localization and classification of weak and small defects under complex backgrounds, a Calibration Guided Super Resolution Enhanced Transformer Detector is developed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves mAP by 2.5 percentage points over the best-performing baseline and achieves the best overall performance on Scratch, Pit, and Mesh defects, especially for weak and small Pit defects. This study provides an efficient and practically deployable solution for intelligent inspection of surface defects in aircraft hydraulic pipelines and other complex ferromagnetic components commonly found in industrial systems.

title: A multi-scale frequency domain information-driven method for ultrasonic welding quality prediction
abstract: Ultrasonic welding is extensively used in industries such as automotive and electronics, where the tensile strength of the welding joints serves as a critical indicator of manufacturing quality, yet is subject to fluctuations caused by multiple uncertain factors during production. Moreover, the complex physical interactions of the process produce time series features rich in high-frequency ultrasonic information, which is critical for achieving accurate predictions of quality performance. This work develops a deep learning framework that accurately predicts joint tensile strength by fusing multi-source signals. Specifically, a high-fidelity acquisition system was established to synchronously capture high-frequency vibration, pressure, and displacement signals during welding. The proposed Gated Multi-scale Fast Fourier Transform Network (GMS-FFTNet) operates directly in the frequency domain, integrating a global Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to capture long-range dependencies and a local Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) to resolve transient details. It is enhanced by an adaptive spectral filtering mechanism that dynamically emphasizes critical frequency bands, overcoming the limitations of conventional time-domain models that often struggle with spectral information loss. To synergize the insights from different sensors, a dedicated gating network effectively fuses the multi-source signal features. The model accurately predicts tensile strength, achieving a coefficient of determination of 82.17%. Furthermore, the visualization of attention weights serves to correlate the model’s inference with the manufacturing process of the ultrasonic welding. This method not only presents a robust solution for reliable quality monitoring of ultrasonic welding but also offers a generalizable framework for other dynamic manufacturing processes with high-frequency information.

title: A joint optimization network for force identification on nonlinear structures
abstract: Accurate force identification is fundamental to the structural health monitoring and integrity assessment of complex engineering systems. However, nonlinear structural dynamics invalidate the superposition principle and render the inverse problem ill-posed, making dynamic force identification highly challenging. Existing model-driven and algorithm unrolling (AU) methods rely on explicit analytical forward models to compute Jacobian matrices, which are often unavailable for practical nonlinear structures. To overcome this limitation, this paper proposes a joint optimization network (JO-Net) for nonlinear structural force identification. JO-Net replaces the analytical Jacobian with an automatically differentiable surrogate model embedded in a deep unrolling framework. The surrogate network learns nonlinear forward dynamics and provides sensitivity information via automatic differentiation, while the proximal gradient descent algorithm is unrolled into a layer-wise network with a convolutional encoder–decoder serving as a learnable proximal operator. A key feature of JO-Net is the simultaneous optimization of the surrogate model and the inverse AU network, enabling adaptive refinement of structural mappings and mitigation of modeling errors. Numerical and experimental validations on nonlinear structures demonstrate that JO-Net significantly outperforms purely data-driven and model-based Kalman filter methods. By combining the surrogate model gradient with a data-driven gradient mapping matrix, the proposed method achieves a better balance between robustness and accuracy. Furthermore, JO-Net demonstrates superior robustness against measurement uncertainties and maintains reliable identification performance for unseen force–amplitude ranges within the tested nonlinear structures.

title: Multistage health state estimation and uncertainty quantification for bearing remaining useful life via graph-guided representation learning
abstract: Bearing degradation follows stochastic and nonlinear trajectories, which makes the accurate prediction of remaining useful life (RUL) a critical challenge in industrial prognostics. Recent deep learning-based methods have achieved promising performance in bearing RUL prediction. However, they have limited ability to explicitly account for changes in degradation behavior during the prognostic process. Health-stage information has been employed to characterize degradation progression, but it is typically used only for stage estimation rather than guiding degradation representation learning or RUL prediction. To address this limitation, we propose the Stage-Aware Graph-guided Embedding-Uncertainty Quantification (SAGE-UQ) framework. The proposed framework consistently leverages health-stage information through degradation representation learning and uncertainty-aware RUL prediction. Specifically, graph-guided spectral representation learning and stage-aware temporal contrastive learning were employed to jointly estimate health-stage information. This estimated stage information is further exploited to learn degradation representations that capture health-stage transition characteristics. It is then leveraged to guide uncertainty-aware RUL predictions. The proposed framework explicitly incorporates health-stage transition ambiguity into predictive uncertainty. Experimental results demonstrate that SAGE-UQ consistently outperforms representative baselines and recent state-of-the-art methods. It achieves an average root-mean-square error (RMSE) reduction of approximately 17.4%. The lightweight architecture and low inference latency enhance its practicality for online prognostic applications.

title: TimeXer-based main bearing temperature prediction and Bayesian fault early warning for offshore wind turbines via transfer learning
abstract: Main bearing failures are a primary driver of offshore wind turbine unplanned downtime, yet data-driven monitoring methods lack cross-turbine generalization and probabilistic fault detection. This study proposes an integrated framework combining the TimeXer model, transfer learning, and a two-stage Bayesian fault early warning system for main bearing temperature prediction. The TimeXer model applies patch-level tokenization to endogenous variables and cross-variable attention to exogenous SCADA inputs, capturing temporal dependencies and inter-variable coupling. Fault early warning sequentially applies a three-sigma threshold, Bayesian posterior probability estimation, and a three-step persistence criterion to suppress false alarms. A two-phase transfer learning protocol adapts the source-domain model to target turbines using limited data. Validated on 41,906 ten-minute SCADA samples from Yangjiang, China, the model achieves R2 = 0.9898, RMSE = 0.3172 °C, and MAE = 0.1636 °C on the 58# 8.3 MW source turbine, surpassing Transformer, LSTM, and XGBoost baselines by up to 42.1% in RMSE. Transfer to the 24# 6.8 MW and 33# 8.3 MW target turbines yields R2 = 0.9851 and 0.9840, with RMSE below the source baseline. The early warning system attains a step-level false alarm rate of 2.1% with a 94.4% detection rate, and component-wise ablation, prior sensitivity analysis and residual normality testing are reported to substantiate each design choice. Normalized error analysis further shows that the lower target-domain RMSE reflects the reduced temperature variability of the target machines rather than an accuracy gain. The framework provides a scalable pathway for offshore wind turbine predictive maintenance.

title: Feature–label similarity-aware hypergraph attention network: A semi-supervised fault diagnosis method for machinery under extremely low label rate scenarios
abstract: Label propagation algorithms (LPAs) and graph neural networks (GNNs) are semi-supervised learning models that have yielded satisfactory results in machinery fault diagnosis under limited labeled data conditions. However, LPAs consider only label similarity, while GNNs primarily focus on feature similarity, and both encode pairwise connections that inherently fail to capture high-order correlations, consequently limiting the ability to make full use of scarce labeled and massive unlabeled data. To address the above limitations, this paper proposes a novel semi-supervised learning model, named feature–label similarity-aware hypergraph attention network, to jointly model high-order feature and label similarities for machinery fault diagnosis under extremely low label rate scenarios. Firstly, a hypergraph of all samples is constructed to encode their high-order correlations beyond pairwise connections. Then, a hypergraph attention network is constructed, in which a cross-attention mechanism is employed to adaptively learn the importance weights of node–hyperedge interactions, facilitating propagation and aggregation of class-specific features along hyperedges from both labeled and unlabeled samples. Subsequently, a hypergraph LPA is integrated into the proposed framework, propagating label information from labeled samples to their neighbors, to fully exploit scarce label information. Finally, the semi-supervised fault diagnosis model is jointly optimized by imposing supervised constraints on classifier predictions and propagated labels for labeled samples, along with a consistency constraint between them for unlabeled samples. Experimental results on three machinery fault diagnosis datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior diagnostic accuracy compared with the state-of-the-art approaches, especially when the label rate is as low as 1 %. The related code was released at https://github.com/yushi1006/FLSHGAT-for-semi-supervised-fault-diagnosis.

title: A rotor dynamic balancing method without trial weights based on multi-sensor feature fusion with an attention mechanism
abstract: Accurate identification of unbalance parameters lies at the core of rotor dynamic balancing technology. In this paper, a deep learning approach is integrated with rotor dynamic balancing theory, and a multi-sensor feature fusion dynamic balancing method without trial weights based on the attention mechanism is proposed. First, considering the unique nature of the dynamic balancing process, a rotor model with varying unbalance parameters was established, and the dataset for model training was augmented by adding bandpass noise. Subsequently, a neural network model for unbalance identification based on the multi-head attention mechanism was designed, and ablation experiments were conducted to verify its superiority over single-sensor models and the feature fusion model without attention. Finally, both a finite element simulation model and an experimental model of a triple-disk rotor system were established for dynamic balancing validation. The simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed dynamic balancing method can substantially reduce the vibration amplitudes of the rotor across all critical speed regions. Moreover, compared with the influence coefficient method (ICM), the proposed method requires only a single run-up process to complete the dynamic balancing procedure, significantly improving the balancing efficiency and achieving superior balancing performance across all critical speed regions.

title: Impact damage localization in woven CFRP laminates using laser-ultrasonic wavefields and a masked spatiotemporal reconstruction network
abstract: Barely visible impact damage (BVID) can compromise the structural integrity and service reliability of composite structures. Laser-ultrasonic full-wavefield analysis provides an effective nondestructive evaluation approach for such damage, as it can capture the spatiotemporal evolution of guided-wave propagation. However, existing data-driven wavefield analysis methods generally rely on costly damage annotations and are often limited to two-dimensional spatial image analysis, thereby insufficiently exploiting the spatiotemporal information contained in laser-ultrasonic wavefields. To address these limitations, this study proposes a self-supervised three-dimensional spatiotemporal anomaly localization method for impact damage detection in woven carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. The proposed method uses only undamaged wavefield data during training. Random spatiotemporal masking is applied to local wavefield clips, and a masked 3D reconstruction network is trained to learn the normal spatiotemporal propagation patterns of guided waves. During testing, anomaly heatmaps are generated through multiple random masked reconstructions of the inspected wavefield and spatiotemporal aggregation of the resulting reconstruction residuals, thereby characterizing local scattering that deviates from normal propagation patterns and enabling effective damage localization. Experimental results on woven CFRP specimens with single and multiple impact damage sites demonstrate that the proposed method can generate concentrated damage-related anomaly responses for most damage sites. Compared to conventional energy imaging techniques, the proposed method presents more distinct damage-related hotspots and does not produce obvious concentrated damage-like responses on the undamaged specimen. These results suggest that self-supervised spatiotemporal reconstruction based on normal wavefield learning provides a feasible framework for label-free laser-ultrasonic localization of impact damage in composite laminates.

title: A multimodal fusion network guided by environmental semantics for reconstructing missing bridge strain trends
abstract: Long term bridge strain trends describe the gradual evolution of structural responses under environmental actions and operational loads, providing important information for structural health monitoring and condition assessment. However, communication interruptions, sensor abnormalities, and unstable data transmission can lead to missing strain data, which affects the completeness of monitoring records and the reliability of subsequent analysis. This study proposes an environmental semantics-guided multimodal fusion network for reconstructing missing bridge strain trends. The network mainly consists of an environmental semantic modulation module and a temporal reconstruction module. The environmental semantic modulation module encodes environmental textual descriptions into semantic representations and introduces environmental contextual information through feature-wise semantic modulation. The temporal reconstruction module uses a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D CNN) to extract local trend variation features and a modified Transformer encoder to model long-range temporal dependencies, enabling environment-aware strain trend reconstruction. Based on strain data obtained from a real bridge field monitoring experiment, this study constructs several typical missing scenarios and validates the proposed method through comparison with multiple baseline methods. The results show that the proposed model can effectively recover the original strain trends under different missing conditions and outperforms the compared methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and robustness. Ablation experiments further demonstrate the effectiveness of the environmental semantic modulation and temporal reconstruction modules.

title: Cost-sensitive active learning for rotating machinery fault diagnosis under data imbalance
abstract: Data-driven fault diagnosis has become an important approach for ensuring the reliability and safety of rotating machinery. However, practical deployment is often hindered by severe data imbalance and label scarcity. Active learning (AL) mitigates label scarcity by selecting the most informative samples for annotation to improve model performance. Nevertheless, conventional AL strategies typically optimize for overall accuracy and treat all misclassifications equally. Consequently, they fail to account for the asymmetric operational costs of diagnostic errors, particularly the greater losses caused by missed detections and severity underestimation. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes a cost-sensitive active learning (CS-AL) framework tailored for highly imbalanced fault distributions. In this framework, raw vibration signals are first transformed into two-dimensional time–frequency representations via continuous wavelet transform (CWT). A Bayesian convolutional neural network, integrated with a convolutional block attention module, is developed to extract fault-sensitive features, while epistemic uncertainty is quantified through Monte Carlo (MC) dropout. To explicitly penalize high-risk errors during sample selection, an asymmetric diagnostic cost matrix is constructed to formulate a cost-sensitive acquisition score based on the expected pairwise misclassification cost. To optimize annotation efficiency, a diversity-aware clustering mechanism selects representative prototypes from this high-risk candidate pool. Experimental validations on the CWRU bearing and MCC5-THU gearbox datasets demonstrate that the CS-AL framework achieves enhanced diagnostic performance and significantly reduces high-cost misclassification risks compared to representative AL baselines. The results confirm the effectiveness of CS-AL in accurately allocating limited labeling resources to rare, safety-critical faults while minimizing total operational risk under imbalanced conditions.

title: A multi-scale progressive fusion method for predicting the remaining useful life of gears guided by a control-equation-compatible a priori cascade
abstract: Gears are core transmission components of high-end equipment in aerospace, rail transit and other key fields. Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of gears is critical for equipment prognostics and health management (PHM), to ensure operational safety and reduce maintenance costs. Aiming at key limitations of existing data-driven gear RUL prediction methods, including strong data dependency, insufficient physical interpretability, low mapping accuracy and weak cross-condition generalization, this paper proposes a novel progressive multi-level feature fusion RUL prediction framework guided by cascaded control equation compatibility priors. Taking gear vibration time-domain signals as the sole input, the framework sequentially adopts three customized modules: Governing Equations Auto-Encoder (GEAE) to extract physically consistent robust degradation features, Multi-scale Fusion Network (MsNet) to construct health indicators for degradation characterization, and Dual Temporal Constraints Network (DTCNet) to achieve accurate RUL mapping. Systematic validation on two heterogeneous datasets demonstrates that the framework reduces RMSE by up to 40.6% and improves R2 by 25.0% over end-to-end methods, while significantly enhancing HI monotonicity and trendability. Cross-seed statistical tests confirm its robustness (coefficient of variation ≤ 1.9%). The method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art approaches and exhibits strong cross-scenario generalization.
